body: _Distilled from `.andromeda/a11y-plan.md` (adopted reading). wrap-session's cascade re-derives it when the plan changes._

**Tier:** 0
**WCAG target:** SC 2.1.1 Keyboard · SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) · SC 2.4.3 Focus Order — the reach (tier, criteria, the `a11y` leg's fourteen files with no required status check, what an assistive technology reads unmeasured, the named limits) published in `docs/capabilities.md` under `## Accessibility reach`; its pin `.github/scripts/test_capability_statement.py` reads none of these claims, so a change to the reach is made in that document by hand

- **Tool:** Rust tests in `tests/blitz-tests` over the AccessKit tree — `build_accessibility_tree()` (or `Document::accessibility_tree()`, which a `DioxusDocument` enriches with each element's stable id as `author_id`) after `resolve`, `test_that` matchers on `role()` / `is_hidden()`, `assert_role(html, id, expected)` and `unknown_tags(html)` helpers; since 2026-10-17-upstream-sync-engine-debts two upstream files assert the builder's name and description reads off the built tree with `verify_that!` — `accessibility_label` (13 tests: a `<label for>` and a wrapping `<label>` each naming a `select` and a `textarea`, a `<label>` naming no hidden `input`; `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` and its precedence, fallback and hidden targets) and `accessibility_description` (3: `aria-description`, `aria-describedby` in order, targets outside the tree excluded) — in the workspace test leg, per package and in the `a11y` leg; beside them `accessibility_merged_states` (3: the merged `aria-expanded`, `aria-disabled` and `aria-level`, each a stated table with its count asserted), `inert_subtree` (6) and `accessibility_active_descendant_unread` (1) assert the builder off the built tree in both layout modes, in the same legs, `inert_subtree` and `accessibility_active_descendant_unread` also three rounds in the `stand-repeat` leg (named `--test`s of its list), all three in the `a11y` leg.
- **Focus harness:** `Harness::focused()` / `hovered()`.

- **Keyboard harness:** a Tab and Shift+Tab key-press focus check exists on the stand, driven through the harness's `press` / `press_with` (`stand_snapshot_state.rs`); since 2026-10-13-range-input-interaction a range-input key and click check runs in both layout modes (`range_input_interaction.rs`: a 7-row keys table and a 5-row clicks table, one `input` per change and none on a no-change Home, the input focused after every click, a disabled range taking neither keys nor a click), and on the stand `stand_act_range.rs` moves the Timer slider through the driver by click and key, an arrow step after two Tabs leaving it focused with role `Slider`, its name and the forward focus sequence unchanged; since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness `stand_keyboard.rs` drives Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space and the CRUD list's keys headlessly on the four lean tasks through the same `press` / `press_with`, reading the focused node back per step, in both layout modes, and pins the flight booker's `select#flight-type` (named `Flight type` by `aria-label`, its second Tab stop) moving its choice by its arrows (`the_flight_type_select_moves_its_choice_by_its_arrows`, 23 tests), and walks the load page's `LOAD_TAB_ORDER` and Cells' `CELLS_TAB_ORDER` forward and back in both layout modes, the load page's button taking Enter and Space, Cells' arrows and Enter opening the moved-to cell's editor and its value committing by keyboard; a select key and typeahead check runs in both layout modes — `select_interaction` (18 tests: a 14-row keys table and a 7-row typeahead table, one `input` and one `change` per change and none for no change, the typed text kept for one second of the document's clock, a disabled select taking no key and no click) and, through the driver, `stand_act_select` (10 tests: Tab `fx-before` → `fx-pick` → `fx-named` → `fx-after` → `fx-before`, the disabled `fx-off` skipped, an option chosen by a click then a key) — both in the `a11y` leg, both three rounds in the `stand-repeat` leg, `stand_act_select` by its `stand_` prefix and `select_interaction` by the leg's named `--test` list; the select list's keyboard and focus coverage is headless — `select_popup` (25 tests), `stand_act_popup` (12) and `stand_keyboard`'s list walks (`the_flight_type_walk_holds_with_its_list_open_and_after_each_close`, `a_click_opens_the_list_focus_stays_on_the_select_and_the_walk_goes_on_from_it`) assert SC 2.1.1 and 2.4.3 on it in both layout modes, `stand_keyboard` in the `a11y` leg and the other two outside it, in the workspace `test` leg and three `stand-repeat` rounds, and the windowed list is read and not run.

- **Contrast harness:** built since 2026-10-13-stand-contrast-harness — `Harness::text_contrast` (blitz-test-harness, read-only) reads an element's text/background pair and font metrics from computed styles as a `TextContrast` (`ratio` by `contrast_ratio`, the WCAG 2.x formula restating blitz-paint's Chrome-matching helper; `required_ratio` 3.0 for large text, else 4.5); `stand_contrast` states three tables, read by one shared reader and asserted row for row in both layout modes — the 17 control rows beside a painted-pixel witness (pass 13, fail 0, exempt-inactive 3, no-text 1: since 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions the stand's accent is one step darker, the operator's F5, a stand change and no engine change, so the four accent controls read `#ffffff` on `#3a5ce5` at 5.47 where `#4a6cf7` read 4.39 and failed), 14 `TEXT_ROWS` (the CRUD list rows and the text outside the controls, all pass) and 20 `STATE_ROWS` (the colour states reached by input, hover and active included: pass 19, exempt 1) — so SC 1.4.3 is met on every measured non-exempt stand row; it runs in the workspace `test` leg, per package and, since 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions, in the `a11y` leg. Since 2026-10-19-visual-lint its first non-test caller is escher-driver's visual lint (`Session::lint` in process and the `lint` verb on every carrier, recorded), whose `contrast` reading reports a node below `required_ratio()` and keeps the same exempt rule (`enabled == Some(false)`), with no second formula or threshold. The default sheet holds an engine-default chosen-row pair for a `multiple` select's rows, `#000000` on `#c8c8c8`, Chromium's inactive selected pair, hardcoded by design as the engine holds no tokens, 12.56:1 measured by `select_interaction` in both layout modes. An open select list's colours are engine constants on `SelectListView`, in no sheet — `HIGHLIGHT_TEXT` `#000000`, `HIGHLIGHT_BACKGROUND` `#c8c8c8`, `DISABLED_TEXT` `#6d6d6d`, `BORDER` `#999999` — and `select_popup_painted` (6 tests) reads the highlight and a disabled row as painted against those constants and measures the plain pair at the default sheet and at the stand, in both layout modes, so SC 1.4.3 is asserted on the list in the harness; a highlighted row's contrast and a blended text's pair are unread by the lint (`Harness::text_contrast` reading `None` past an element on its walk with a `mix-blend-mode` other than `normal`, pinned by `a_blended_ancestor_reads_none_and_an_unblended_one_its_pair`, no stand row moving) and a closed select's own pair is unread.
- **Structured violation JSON / WCAG mapping of existing tests:** NOT YET MEASURED.

- Roles: `role` attribute → HTML-AAM mapping → `Role::Unknown`; landmarks, lists, tables, form inputs by `type`, links only with `href`; a single select's `ComboBox` writes `expanded` from its list's open state, reading no `aria-expanded`, an author's `open` or `aria-expanded` on it steering nothing and `:open` not matching it; the tree's focus stays on the select and its chosen option reads `selected`; the highlighted row is in no snapshot and no tree and the snapshot holds no `expanded` key, and what an assistive technology reads of the list is not measured; a `multiple` select's `ListBox` writes `set_multiselectable`, and an `optgroup` reads `Role::Group`, its non-empty `label` attribute its name, named in the tree and painted as a header of an open list, heavier than a row by weight on every build, a header choosing nothing — what an assistive technology reads of them is not measured.

- Hidden: `hidden` / `display:none` / `visibility:hidden` exclude the subtree — an `option` of a `select`, its child or under its `optgroup` (`is_select_option`), excepted from `display: none`, which every option of a single-choice select but its chosen one computes and a `multiple` select's rows do not: it stays in the tree, `hidden`, `inert` and `visibility: hidden` still excluding it; `aria-hidden` marks hidden; an element carrying `inert` is excluded with its subtree too, and so from the snapshot, and a hit passes through it, removing `inert` restoring the tree and the hit (the `inert` read ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18).

- State (since 2026-10-10-snapshot-states): the builder reads `aria-selected`, `aria-pressed` and `aria-invalid` by value on every element — a select's option excepted, its `selected` its chosen state (`select::is_chosen`), true or false, with no `aria-selected` read, and its non-empty `label` attribute its `label` where it has no `aria-label` — — trimmed, lower-case, exact — onto the node's `selected`, `toggled` (`mixed` kept) and `invalid` (a value outside the list reads True); `aria-pressed` sets `toggled` on every role but the five checkable ones, and `aria-checked` `true` / `false` / `mixed` sets it on a `CheckBox` · `Switch` · `RadioButton` · `MenuItemCheckBox` · `MenuItemRadio` role alone (`role="switch"` mapping to `Switch`), a native `input` of type `checkbox` or `radio` reading neither — the toggle read per role ratified by the founder (2026-10-18), `accessibility_states`' fourth test its pin; each attribute is read once, and the one other write of `toggled` is a native checkbox's or radio's own checked state on a checkable role — `Toggled::True` or `False` from `checkbox_input_checked()`; under any other role it writes nothing, so `pressed` never begins to read on it, `accessibility_states`' `a_click_and_a_space_move_a_native_control_in_the_tree` its pin, what an assistive technology reads of it not measured. The snapshot takes the three from the tree as `selected` · `pressed` · `invalid`, a boolean model with two limits (a mixed toggle reads not pressed; a grammar or spelling error reads invalid). Ratified by the founder (2026-10-10); what an assistive technology reads is unmeasured, the windowed witness, at an active assistive technology, which this version does not reach, owned by a `.andromeda/residuals.md` line that reads `re-carried:0.2.0` on the founder's F1 (2026-10-14), the headless half — the tree the shell hands the adapter — proven on the stand since 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions. Check: `accessibility_states` (6, both layout modes; three rounds in the `stand-repeat` leg, a named `--test` of its list; in the `a11y` leg — the fourth reading `aria-checked`'s three values on a checkable role alone and four unchecked natives reading neither attribute, the fifth `aria-pressed` on a checkable role reading nothing). Since 2026-10-17-upstream-sync-engine-debts the builder also holds upstream's six reads, as upstream wrote them: `aria-labelledby` (Names, below), `aria-describedby` (the referenced nodes as `described_by`), `aria-description` (its text into AccessKit's description), `aria-expanded` (a boolean, on every element but a single select, which reads none and writes `expanded` from its list's open state), `aria-disabled` (`true` → `set_disabled`) and `aria-level` (a number, with the tag and role defaults); upstream's own `parse::<bool>` `aria-selected` and unfiltered `aria-label` reads were dropped in the merge, so there is still one read per attribute; the snapshot reads no description and its `enabled` reads the `disabled` attribute, so `aria-disabled` moves no snapshot reading; no stand file states any of the six, and the description and the three new closed values leave only to the platform adapter, which no stand binary builds — what an assistive technology reads of them is not measured (ratified as upstream's behaviour by the founder, 2026-10-17).

- Stand markup (attributes only): the flight booker's date inputs state `aria-invalid`, and the stand states no `aria-pressed` — the flight booker's mode is one `select#flight-type`, whose options state its choice by `selected`; the CRUD list is a `listbox` and its rows `option`s with `aria-selected`. Since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness (the operator's decision) the list `crud-list` takes `tabindex="0"` and an `onkeydown` — the third CRUD Tab stop — and, focused, ArrowDown selects the next visible row (the first when none is selected), ArrowUp the previous, Home the first and End the last, as a row's click does. One gap stands open: the rows are not focusable and the tree's focus is the list, never the option — the builder reads no `aria-activedescendant`, so an assistive technology learns the current row only from its `selected` reading; an `aria-activedescendant` read in the builder, or a roving focus, is SC 4.1.2 work outside the tier-0 target, kept unread on the founder's F2 (2026-10-14) and pinned by `accessibility_active_descendant_unread` (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18). The second, the list's empty accessible name, closed at 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions: the list is named `People` by `aria-label`. Cells: `cells-grid`, named `Cells` by `aria_label` with no role, is one Tab stop; the arrows move `current`, clamped, and bring the cell into view; Enter opens the editor on `current`, focused, and the editor's Enter commits and returns focus to the grid; Tab leaving an open editor commits it; `.cells-grid:focus .cell.current` draws a 2px outline in the stand accent; role and cell semantics stay out, owned by a `.andromeda/residuals.md` line.

- Focus: Tab / Shift+Tab via `focus_next_node` / `focus_prev_node`; focusability recomputed on `tabindex` / `href` / `disabled`; focus resets to body on removal; the tree's focus is the focused node only where it is among the built nodes, else `u64::MAX`, the window, so the tree never names a node it did not build; since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness, in every document (ratified by the founder), a pointer click on a `button` (any type) or an `input` of type `submit`, `reset` or `button` focuses it, then submits the form owner when it is a submit button — a disabled form control still stops the walk first, a disabled ancestor `div` not (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), a click on a `select` focuses it, clearing its typeahead and the document's text selection, and on a single select also opens its list or closes one standing, two clicks on one point opening then closing, each focusing (a disabled select stopped by the walk's gate first, so it neither focuses nor acts; a click on a row of an open list choosing it, a disabled row changing nothing and leaving the list open and a group header choosing nothing; a press outside the list closing it with no event, and a driver `click` on an element under the list refused `covered`; a label's click on a bound single select focusing it and opening nothing; an option of a closed single select, under a group too, is not clicked — a driver `click` on one is refused `covered`; a click on a `multiple` select's row runs `click_select_row`, a disabled select stopping it, otherwise focusing the select and clearing the typeahead and the text selection, a plain click choosing the row alone, Ctrl or Meta flipping it, Shift spanning and a disabled row changing nothing), and a click on any other element (a CRUD row, the list) still clears focus; two pointer clicks on one point within 500 ms and 2 px are a double click, read on the document's clock — on a harness-built document the harness's `VirtualClock`, so two driver `click`s on one point with no `advance` between them are a double click, selecting a word in a text input — while each still focuses its target as one click does (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); `:focus-within` matches the focused element and its ancestors by the `FOCUS_WITHIN` element state, while `:focus-visible` never matches; `:open` matches a `details` or `dialog` carrying `open` by the `OPEN` element state, in every document, flipped when a `details`'s first `summary` toggles it through the mutator — `open_state`'s 4 tests, in both layout modes, read the `open` attribute by presence at construction, move it through a mutator write and removal and a summary's click and Enter, and read `:open` matching. Enter and Space (since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness, in every document, ratified by the founder): a pressed Enter on the focused node that is no disabled form control (`ElementData::is_disabled`; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18 — a `disabled` attribute on a `summary` or an `a` gating neither key, as HTML does) dispatches a Click on a `button`, a `summary`, an `input` of type `submit`, `reset` or `button`, or an `a` with `href`; a released Space (`handle_key_up`) dispatches the same Click on a `button`, a `summary`, or an `input` of type `submit`, `reset`, `button`, `checkbox` or `radio` — a link takes no Space, and a text input and a range input take neither key there; the Click (`Node::synthetic_click_event_data`) runs the app's handlers (a Dioxus `onclick`), then `handle_click`, whose checkbox and radio arms dispatch, after `input`, a `change` with the same value, in every document, a checkbox always and a radio only where it was not checked before the click (`checkable_change_event`), while typing in a text input and a range's key and pointerdown fire `input` and no `change` (`text_range_no_change_event`). Range input (since 2026-10-13-range-input-interaction, in every document, ratified by the founder): focused and with no `disabled` attribute (read by presence), it steps up on ArrowRight/ArrowUp, down on ArrowLeft/ArrowDown, goes to its minimum on Home and its maximum on End, every other key doing nothing — each change marks the changed set and fires one `input`, a move that changes nothing none; a click focuses it without moving its value, and a main-button pointerdown sets the value from the hit's fraction of the content box, clamped to [0, 1]. Select: a focused single-choice `select` (no `multiple`) that is no disabled form control (`ElementData::is_disabled`), its list closed, takes ArrowDown / ArrowUp to the next / previous enabled option and Home / End to the first / last enabled option (with none chosen, ArrowDown reads as Home and ArrowUp as End), and a character pressed with no Ctrl, Alt or Meta as typeahead — the first enabled option whose label starts with the text typed, compared in lower case, the text kept for one select until 1 s of the document's clock passes; Enter, and a Space with no typed text standing, open its list on press, on the chosen option and firing nothing, a released Space doing nothing more, a disabled, inert, hidden or empty select opening nothing, and every other key does nothing; each change marks the changed set and dispatches one `input` then one `change`, a key that changes nothing firing none; an `optgroup`'s options are the select's own in tree order, a disabled group's rows reading as disabled. With the list open — an engine overlay on every document, remote pages included — the engine paints it over the page and focus stays on the select: its keys move the highlight over enabled rows and choose nothing, a pointer over an enabled row moving it too; Enter and Space choose the highlighted row and close, Tab in either direction chooses and closes before focus moves, one `input` then one `change` firing and none for the option already chosen; Escape closes with the value unchanged and no event, as a second click, a press outside and a page scroll do, a wheel outside closing it and then scrolling; a close clears the typed text, and a select made inert, disabled, hidden or removed while open closes its list. A list shows at most `MAX_ROWS` 20 and scrolls by key and by wheel, its thumb painted, taking no hit and not draggable, its rows one height, and it opens and closes with no motion. A focused `multiple` select that is no disabled form control takes ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home and End: alone they choose that row alone, with Shift they span from the anchor (with no cursor yet from the last chosen row), and with Ctrl or Meta they move the current row and change nothing; with a valid `size` a key brings the current row into view through `scroll_into_view`; a Space with no typed text standing flips the current row and with text standing joins it, a character with no Ctrl, Alt or Meta chooses its match alone, its disabled rows are never chosen and Ctrl+A is not modelled; the driver's `type` on any select focuses it with no click, so it fires no DOM focus events on a single select either, closes any list and clears the typeahead, a text opening on a space typing nothing, and the driver's `press` holds no Ctrl, so a non-adjacent `multiple` set cannot be built through the driver, a limit its help states, its fix owned by a `.andromeda/residuals.md` line (target: next).

- Disabled-ness is keyed one way since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness (in every document, ratified by the founder): the `DISABLED` state (`:disabled`) reads the attribute's presence, and the pointer-move gate, `ClickTarget::Disabled`, `handle_click`'s walk gate, the Enter and Space activation and focusability read `ElementData::is_disabled` — that presence on a `button`, `input`, `select` or `textarea` alone (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) — so `disabled="false"` and a bare `disabled` on a form control match `:disabled` and are not focusable, a bare `disabled` set after creation takes its focusability away, and a `<div disabled tabindex=0>` takes focus. dioxus-native-dom removes a falsy value of its 28 boolean attributes — upstream's `is_bool_attr` predicate since 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship (`disabled`, `checked`, `hidden`, `inert` among them; a framework-written `inert: false` is removed, while a truthy `inert` (by presence on itself or an ancestor element) takes focusability, hits and the tree away from its subtree (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) and Tab reaches the buttons under `inert: false`; HTML's focus fixup is built, in every document, so a node holding focus when it comes under `inert`, a subtree moved under an inert box included, gives focus up as the mutator flushes, no DOM `blur` or `focusout` firing; the fixup reads `is_inert()` alone, so a focused control that no longer shows, by `hidden`, `style="display:none"` or CSS alone, keeps focus and takes keys, with no panic, the limit owned by a `CARRY:` on the entry «A11y re-read»), so a `hidden: false` element stays displayed, in the tree and in the snapshot; an attribute outside the list holding `false` is still written as `"false"`. The snapshot reads `enabled` by presence — the driver's `disabled` refusal cause is stated on the same presence reading ("the element carries the `disabled` attribute, which the snapshot reads as not enabled") and is detected on it and on nothing else: the driver refuses a `click` or a `type` as `disabled` when the snapshot reads the element not enabled, with nothing dispatched and focus as it was, and acts on the same control once it reads enabled (`stand_act_disabled.rs`), and the driver's schema defines no role or name set of its own — `checked` a native checkbox's or radio's state, else, on a checkable role, the node's `toggled` reading (`True` true, `False` and `Mixed` false; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), and `value` from the element (a `select`'s `value` `BaseDocument::select_value` — the chosen option's value, for a `multiple` select its first chosen option's in tree order, nothing with none chosen — its options, its children and those under an `optgroup`, kept in the tree as `ListBoxOption` nodes, each `selected` from its chosen state, a closed select's options under it with its select's client rect as their `bounds`, which the driver's visual lint leaves out of its overlap reading in every document with an open list's rows and groups, an open list's row reading its painted row's `bounds` (`Entry.in_select_box`, read through `closed_select_of` for a closed select's option and through `select_list_bounds` for an open list's row or group, never the role) — the stand's flight booker at boot no `overlap`, `stand_lint` reading `[0, 0, 0, 0]` — while a `multiple` select's rows and groups read their own client rects and its rows are linted as usual; a range input's `value` its current value since 2026-10-13-range-input-interaction — `ElementData::range_input_value`, the formatted value a key or a pointerdown moved, while its `value` attribute keeps the boot value; a password or file-input value reads the fixed mask `MASKED_VALUE` — and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, a password's typed text is in no painted frame either: blitz-paint paints its value as bullets, its caret at the bullet of its caret index, in every document and through every renderer that paints with blitz-paint, windowed included (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-12), two values of one length painting byte-identical frames, focused or not, in both layout modes (`password_painted_masked.rs`); a click inside a field holding a value places the caret by the bullets — `click_password_input` lays out one U+2022 per character through `BaseDocument::layout_as_text_input`, finds the bullet under the point and moves the real editor to that character, so no width of the real characters reaches the caret: two values of one length read one index, in both layout modes (`password_caret_click.rs`; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); the windowed paint is not run; a textarea's typed text reads back as its `value`, proven on an in-file fixture where it is named by `aria-label`), and `focused` from the tree — proven after a click, a Tab press and Shift+Tab (`stand_snapshot_state.rs`). The snapshot's text form (`Snapshot::to_text`) reads that model, never the tree or a control: one line per node, its role and name the node's, with no second mapping (`stand_snapshot_text.rs`). The text's parts (`Snapshot::text_parts`, `TextPart`) are one more reader of that model through the text form and of nothing else — consecutive pre-order lines of `to_text`, never a split line, the parts concatenating to the whole text with every node id on exactly one line — and the driver's `snapshot` reads a screen over `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` in parts: on an over-budget fixture, in both layout modes, each part's lines equal their lines in the whole text, a password's line reads `MASKED_VALUE` in every part, and exactly one line reads `focused` after a click (`stand_snapshot_parts.rs`). The snapshot's diff (`Snapshot::diff`) is one more reader of that model: a text change is reported on the element whose accessible name it changes, by its id and never as a text-run entry, a hidden element leaves and returns with its descendants, and a focus move names exactly the controls whose `focused` reading moved (`stand_diff.rs`). Since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface an MCP tool result is one more reader of that model and of nothing else — a `snapshot` result is `to_text`'s output itself for a whole screen, equal byte for byte to `Session::run`'s screen text in both layout modes (`stand_mcp_tools.rs`), and, for a screen read in parts, its JSON line `{"text","part","parts"}` holding that part's text — through `serve_mcp` a walk's text blocks equal the JSON lines `Session::run` writes, in both layout modes (`stand_snapshot_parts.rs`), its crossing to an MCP client ratified by the founder (2026-10-10). Since 2026-10-12-self-description a password input typed through an MCP `type` reads `MASKED_VALUE` in the tool result, role `PasswordInput` and a non-empty name, the typed text in neither result, in both layout modes — a test-only element of the shared password page `fixtures::password_named` (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/fixtures/mod.rs`), no stand task or app gaining one; and two further readers of the same model state closed words only: the node keys' help that `help` serves (each key's reading, the boolean model's two limits among them) and `DiffNode::differs`, a changed node naming the readings that differ from before the step in node-key order — the Flight Booker's Book names eight nodes — seven that only moved, each `differs` = `[bounds]`, and since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness `flight-book` itself, which the click now focuses, `differs` = `[focused, bounds]` (`stand_diff.rs`). Since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot the driver's `screenshot` is one more reader of the model's bounds and of nothing else in it — an element shot, addressed by stable id and refused as every id-addressed call is, is the node's bounds rounded outward and cropped to the part that can be seen — and a shot changes nothing: no focus moves, `has_changes` stays false and the next diff is empty, in both layout modes (`stand_act_screenshot.rs`).

- Stand cue: `stand_flight_booker.rs` asserts the invalid-date cue (`invalid` class + `disabled` Book) without colour; `stand_accessibility_ids.rs` pins each lean task's Tab sequence (`focus_next_node` from the root element) against the shared table `tab_order` in the stand checks' shared module — CRUD's restated since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness to six stops, `back-btn`, `crud-filter`, `crud-list`, `crud-name`, `crud-surname`, `crud-create`, and the flight booker's to four, `back-btn`, `flight-type`, `flight-start`, `flight-book`, the two other tasks' unchanged and asserts the 14 stand controls' roles and non-empty names — and, since 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions, that every interactive-role tree node of the four lean tasks reads a non-empty name (the nine roles of `INTERACTIVE_ROLES`; the CRUD list named `People` by `aria-label`), each `REGION_NAMES` row's name in the tree and the snapshot, and that the tree the shell hands the adapter (`Document::accessibility_tree` through `&dyn blitz_dom::Document`) equals `harness.doc.accessibility_tree()` node for node, with the same focus and root, every `author_id` on it the node's `element_id`; `stand_actionable_keys.rs` asserts every actionable element of the lean tasks and Home reads an author key (`DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable()` empty, in every state), with no `tabindex`, role or Tab-order change, and since 2026-10-14-stand-requirement-sweep the three non-lean tasks too — Temperature Converter · Circle Drawer · Cells 0 · 0 · 0, in both layout modes and with Circle Drawer's dialog open, through nine author ids added by `id:` lines alone (until then 2 · 3 · 676), and the load page the stand serves reads none either (`stand_load_page`); the load page and Cells hold Tab-order, keyboard and contrast rows (`stand_keyboard`, `stand_contrast`, `stand_load_page`, `stand_cells_served`; `LOAD_TAB_ORDER` and `CELLS_TAB_ORDER` in the shared module beside `tab_order` and `ENABLED_TAB_ORDER`), so SC 2.1.1 and 1.4.3 are asserted on the load page's `load-fetch` Button and on Cells' `cells-grid`; the elements that react to input and state no interactive role are counted and pinned as measured (`stand_non_lean_tasks`: 0 on the four lean tasks, Home and Temperature Converter, Circle Drawer 1, Cells 677, the 676 data cells and `cells-grid`) — no snapshot field says that an element reacts to a click, that reading owned by a `.andromeda/residuals.md` line (target: next) on the founder's C3 (2026-10-14), this count its starting reading; since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness SC 2.1.1 on the stand's buttons is met by measurement: `stand_keyboard.rs` reads Enter and Space on each focused stand button as its click (16 rows, `counter-increment`, `flight-book` and `crud-create` changing the screen; a focused single select such as the flight booker's `select#flight-type` instead opens its list on a pressed Enter, or a pressed Space with no typed text standing, and a released Space does nothing more), and through the driver `stand_act_keys.rs` presses `enter` and `space` on a Tab-focused `counter-increment`, each naming `counter-value`; since 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions Enter and Space also read as the click of the two buttons enabled after boot, `crud-update` and `crud-delete`, each reached by keyboard alone (4 rows), and the Tab walk is asserted in two enabled states, each reached by keyboard alone, against the shared table `ENABLED_TAB_ORDER` — the flight booker after the return flight is chosen on `select#flight-type` by ArrowDown, five stops; CRUD after a row is selected, eight, `crud-update` and `crud-delete` last — every `controls(task)` id lying in `tab_order` ∪ `ENABLED_TAB_ORDER`.

- Platform: accesskit_xplat adapters (windows, macos, unix, android, null); ActionRequested and AccessibilityDeactivated are unhandled TODOs; the tree is built on InitialTreeRequested and rebuilt on a poll that reported work when the document's changed set, taken by that poll, was non-empty — a focus move, a checked change, a rewritten name, a text control's input, a select's changed choice, a single select's list opening or closing and other mutations mark it, a page scroll or a move that closes a list marking its select through `reconcile_select_list` at the next resolve and a wheel elsewhere through `close_select_list`, while a highlight or a wheel move inside a list marks nothing and a pointer move alone does not — through `Document::accessibility_tree` (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-07; before 2026-10-07 the poll-time refresh never ran; no windowed witness on the dev host — still owed at the platform adapter, the stand building no adapter, kept so on the founder's F1 (2026-10-14), and owned by a `.andromeda/residuals.md` line that reads `re-carried:0.2.0`, an active assistive technology this version does not reach; since 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions both halves are proven headlessly on the stand in both layout modes: on Counter, after a drained changed set, each Tab of the whole `tab_order` and an Enter on `counter-increment` leave `has_changes()` true, and the tree read through `&dyn Document` reads the new focus stop and `counter-value`'s new name). A harness settle neither reads nor drains that changed set, and the set is non-empty on a freshly booted harness document — a check reading the flag as "this step changed something" drains first. Names come from text children, a trimmed-non-empty `aria-label` and `<label>` association (`for`-target, else first nested labelable element — a `button`, an `input` whose `type` is not `hidden`, a `meter`, `output`, `progress`, `select` or `textarea`; a hidden input is named by no label); since 2026-10-17-upstream-sync-engine-debts an `aria-labelledby` whose targets hold text outranks both (accname 2B) — its loop runs after the `<label>` → input loop, clears `labelled_by` and pushes the referenced nodes, the `aria-label` staying the fallback when the targets hold none — and that text reaches the snapshot `name`. The seven_guis stand names no `accessibility` feature in its own manifest — dioxus-native-dom's reaches it through escher-driver, so both its binaries compile the accessibility modules — and builds no platform adapter (`accesskit_xplat` and `accesskit_winit` in neither graph), so the stand binary gives no assistive technology a tree; re-read at 2026-10-10-mcp-surface, when escher-driver took `serde_json` as a fourth dependency (one lock line, no package), no platform adapter joins the stand graph.

title: CI legs (one script for CI and the host)

data.head: ## CI legs (one script for CI and the host)

body: - `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast` — the local pre-push gate: fmt → clippy → test → ci-scripts → embolden, stops at the first red

- `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh {leg}` — one leg: `embolden` (the `blitz-paint/font-embolden` witness, the last step of `fast`, with no CI job) or one CI leg exactly as CI runs it: `fmt` · `clippy` · `test` · `ci-scripts` · `build` · `msrv` (needs toolchain 1.91) · `counter` · `wasm` · `doc` · `stand-repeat` (since 2026-10-14-quality-gates, not a fast leg: three rounds of `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked` over every `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_*.rs` and, on the same line, seventeen named targets outside that prefix (`inert_subtree` · `accessibility_states` · `scrolled_box_absolute_position` · `hit_clipped_at_scrolling_box` · `password_caret_click` · `transformed_client_rect` · `accessibility_active_descendant_unread` · `virtual_clock_engine` · `select_interaction` · `text_extent` · `visible_region_transformed` · `hit_non_invertible_transform` · `open_state` · `checkable_change_event` · `text_range_no_change_event` · `select_popup` · `select_popup_painted`), then seven_guis' `cli_commands` · `cli_flow` · `host_binary` · `host_log` · `host_timer` · `mcp_server` · `mcp_log` · `recording` (since 2026-10-19-session-recording), the first red ending the leg — a zero-failure budget, no retry); its merged output lands in `target/ci-logs/{leg}.log`; unknown leg → exit 2

- `bash .github/scripts/apt-install.sh <package>...` — fork CI's package install, called by ci.yml's install steps only (no leg calls it; never run on the dev host): up to 3 attempts, `apt-get update` then `install`, each call under a 120 s bound, and since 2026-10-14-quality-gates each retried attempt first runs a bounded repair, `dpkg --configure -a` (phase `repair`, a failed repair failing that attempt; the first attempt runs no `dpkg`); exit 0 installed · 1 every attempt failed · 2 usage
- `cargo build --workspace --locked` — every crate (dev profile, `debug = "line-tables-only"`); the `build` leg
- `cargo check --workspace` / `just check`
- `cargo build -p counter --locked` — the counter example
- `cargo build -p seven_guis --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --no-default-features --features hybrid --locked` — stand as wasm
- `just small` — size-profile counter build
- `cargo test --workspace --locked` — the CI `test` leg (ubuntu, default features)

- Flags: `--verbose`/`-v`, `--run-quarantined`, `--list`; outputs `wpt/output/wpt_expectations.txt` and `wptreport.json`

- `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh doc` — `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --locked`, the docs gate over every workspace library crate (green; CI's docs job runs the same leg). Beside it: `ci-leg.sh audit` (`cargo deny --locked --workspace --all-features check advisories licenses` over `deny.toml` — the advisories and licences of the whole workspace's graph, since 2026-10-14-quality-gates), `ci-leg.sh a11y` (fourteen integration tests on one `cargo test --workspace --locked` line — `accessibility_hidden`, `accessibility_roles`, `focusability_updates`, `stand_keyboard`, `stand_contrast` and `stand_accessibility_ids`, then `accessibility_states`, `accessibility_label`, `accessibility_description`, `accessibility_merged_states`, `accessibility_active_descendant_unread`, `inert_subtree`, `select_interaction` and `stand_act_select`) and `ci-leg.sh coverage` (cargo-llvm-cov lcov to `target/coverage/lcov.info`, then the per-file table — both `cargo llvm-cov` lines taking `--ignore-filename-regex 'keyboard_compat\.rs$'` since the 2026-10-17 upstream sync, excluding dioxus-native-dom's crate-private `keyboard_compat.rs` (upstream's temporary keyboard-types 0.7/0.8 bridge) until escher takes upstream's retirement of it, the floors unchanged — then, chained since 2026-10-14-quality-gates, `python3 .github/scripts/coverage_floor.py` over three per-crate line floors — `packages/escher-driver` 97 %, `packages/dioxus-native-dom` 83 %, `packages/blitz-test-harness` 90 % — the leg exiting with the floor's status; needs the `llvm-tools` rustup component)

masked as on every carrier, a shot's without its pixels), checked before the spawn — a refusal status `3` with nothing spawned — and passed to the host; taken at most once on `start`, the host role and the `mcp` role, and anywhere else, twice or with no value a usage error, status `2`), then `snapshot [--part <part>]` (`--part` a whole number 1 to 1000; a screen over the snapshot text budget, or a `--part` asked, answers one part as one line `{"text":…,"part":n,"parts":m}`, status `0`, a part past the last the empty text, a whole screen's still `{"text":…}` alone) · `click --id <id>` (a click on a select opens its list and a second closes it; an option of a closed select lies under it and is refused `covered`: click the select first, then the option) · `type --id <id> --text <text>` (on a select, single or `multiple`, which it focuses with no click, closing any list, the text chooses the first option whose label starts with it and, on a `multiple` select, its match alone; a text opening on a space types nothing on any select) · `press --key <key> [--shift]` · `advance --ms <ms>` · `scroll --id <id>` · `screenshot [--id <id>]` (since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot; its accepted answer one line `{"width":…,"height":…,"png":"<base64>"}`, `png` padded base64, status `0`) · `lint` (the eighth instance verb, no argument; `<dir>` must be short — at most 94 bytes as given on Linux (one of 95 ends `state-dir-too-long`, status `3`) and 90 on every other target; past it the session error states the bound and its remedy: a shorter path, or a relative one, which counts only its own bytes

since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay `stand_replay`, 3 tests, not unix-gated: the two committed checks `tests/blitz-tests/checks/counter-cli.json` and `counter-mcp.json` read through `Check::from_bytes` and replayed through `Check::replay` on a fresh stand Counter in both layout modes, each red at its first activation step on a test-local `Counter` variant that adds 2, and a check on a session of another app running nothing; - Crates under `packages/`, apps under `apps/`, example crates under `examples/{name}/`, root examples as `examples/*.rs`; integration tests one file per behaviour in `tests/blitz-tests/tests/`, each its own test target — upstream's single-binary `tests/all.rs` stays in the manifest at `test = false`, never built, pinned by `BlitzTestsTargetsTest` — with the stand checks' shared tables and helpers stated once in `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs`, and what the checks that hold a `Session` share in a second such module, `tests/blitz-tests/tests/session_common/mod.rs`, and the fixture boot and hold, the fixture pages more than one check reads and the held network stand-in `HeldNet` in a third, `tests/blitz-tests/tests/fixtures/mod.rs`, read by `mod fixtures;` — a page with one reader staying in its check's file (none of the three a test target); the two committed kept checks `stand_replay` replays sit in `tests/blitz-tests/checks/`.
- Modules and files open with a `//!` doc; examples open with a `//!` comment saying what they demonstrate.
- Paint rendering is split one module per concern (`blitz-paint/src/render/*`).
- Standard Rust casing. No-op implementations are prefixed `Dummy` (`DummyNetProvider`, …); internal JS natives are prefixed `__blitz_`.
- Consuming builder methods named `with_*` / `without_*` (`with_virtual_time`, `without_timer_thread`).
- Stylo and Parley types are aliased under `stylo` / `parley` modules.
- `#[non_exhaustive]` on extensible public structs (`NavigationOptions`, `Request`).
- Dependencies declared once in `[workspace.dependencies]` and consumed as `{ workspace = true }`; dependency groups separated by comment headers.

- In-repo crates are declared with `default-features = false` — except `seven_guis`, which keeps its default renderer feature (dioxus-native refuses to compile with none); package metadata inherited with `*.workspace = true`.

- App and example crates, blitz-tests, blitz-test-harness, escher-telemetry, escher-driver, blitz-vibey-script (since 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship) and wpt set `publish = false`; docs.rs builds with all features and `doc_cfg` under `docsrs`.
- Crate internals are `pub(crate)` / `pub(super)`; the slotmap key is used only at the storage boundary — public APIs use `NodeId`.

- Optional capabilities are Cargo features forwarded across crates (each dioxus-native feature forwards to the same-named blitz feature; `accessibility` also to dioxus-native-dom's, which gates its own `accessibility_tree` override and its `snapshot`, `snapshot_diff`, `snapshot_text` and `actionable` modules). The workspace takes both Dioxus crates with `default-features = false`, so a feature is on only where a crate names it or depends on a crate that names it — escher-driver names dioxus-native-dom's `accessibility`, which reaches both seven_guis binaries through that edge.

- In the engine and upstream crates `tracing` is gated per call site with a `#[cfg(not(feature = "tracing"))] let _ = …;` fallback; escher-telemetry (no `[features]`) emits its startup and panic events ungated, and escher-driver takes `tracing` with no feature for its spans — the `command` span and, since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface, the `tool_call` span, the parent of `command` on an MCP tool call — built by hand with `tracing::info_span!` (no `#[instrument]`).
- Desktop-only code gated by the repeated cfg list windows / macos / linux / dragonfly / freebsd / netbsd / openbsd.
- Fallible APIs return typed results (`Result<_, CssomError>`, `Result<_, ParseError>`, `Result<Resource, String>`); error types are enums with `Display` and `From` per wrapped error.
- Mutex locks recover from poisoning with `unwrap_or_else(|err| err.into_inner())`.
- `clippy::expect_used` / `clippy::unwrap_used` allowed only locally, next to a justification. Examples may fail with `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`.
- `unsafe` blocks carry an `allow unsafe_code` or `// SAFETY:` comment.
- Borrow conflicts are worked around by taking a child list or layout out and restoring it; let-chains in `if` conditions are used.
- Mutations go through `DocumentMutator`, which flushes deferred work on `Drop`; take a Stylo snapshot before attribute mutation of in-document nodes.
- Event-producing functions take a `dispatch_event` callback.
- Repeated regexes live in `LazyLock<Regex>` or are compiled per worker.
- Gaps marked `TODO` / `FIXME`; ordering-sensitive blocks marked `WARNING: DO NOT REORDER`; sections delimited with `// === … ===`.
- Spec URLs are cited above or next to implementations; constants carry a rationale doc comment.

- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --locked -- -D warnings` — then, only when that line is green and since 2026-10-14-quality-gates, upstream's own blitz-dom line `cargo clippy -p blitz-dom --no-default-features --features svg,woff,accessibility,system-fonts,file-input,custom-widget --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` — each run as its `.github/scripts/ci-leg.sh` leg; `clippy::collapsible_if` allowed crate-wide in browser, blitz-dom, blitz-html, blitz-vibey-script; `clippy::module_inception` in blitz-dom's node module; other allows are local, ideally with a reason; rustdoc warnings are errors workflow-wide, over every library crate.
See `.claude/rules/observability.md` for enforcement; this doc carries the conventions.
See `.claude/rules/testing.md` (authoring) and `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md` (the `Harness` driver).

A single select's list is painted, an engine overlay reaching the screen through `paint_scene` alone and no second OS window: a click, Enter, or a Space with no typed text standing opens it, a group's `label` is named in the accessibility tree and painted as a header, and `size` is read on a `multiple` select and stays unread on a single select; a `multiple` select lays out as `display: block`, `white-space: nowrap` rows padded 0 2px and a single-choice select's group is transparent to layout (`display: contents`) — engine defaults, no design token.

**Full plans:** `.andromeda/design-system.md` + `.andromeda/layout-templates.md`.

_Documented architectural traps from `.andromeda/architecture.md` and the specialist plans. Runtime discoveries go to `session-learnings.md` (curated by `/andromeda-wrap-session`) — this file is for traps known from the code as adopted._

**What breaks:** bumping one side of a coupled pin fails to build or mis-renders.
**How to avoid:** markup5ever/html5ever/xml5ever must match stylo's `web_atoms`; skrifa must match parley and vello; svgtypes must match usvg; taffy is a registry version (0.15) since 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship — a git dep pinned by `rev` until then, so no git dependency is left in the manifest — and parley a registry version (0.12); winit is exact `=0.31.0-beta.3`. Bump the set together.
**References:** arch §Established Decisions [Dependency pinning]

**What breaks:** no longer a panic — `Parallel` traversals are serialised process-wide by the static `PARALLEL_TRAVERSAL_LOCK` (its poison recovered, no panic path), so two documents resolving `Parallel` concurrently on Stylo's global pool no longer panic `already mutably borrowed` (blitz issue 430); the `Default` derive and the field doc both name `Sequential` the default. What still stands: `LAYOUT_CTX` is thread-local with a FIXME for multi-document use.
**How to avoid:** no choice is needed for safety — the windowed `dioxus_native::launch` and the browser build their documents `Parallel`, serialised by the lock, and no headless document (harness, stand or driver) sets `style_threading`, so it resolves `Sequential`, which bypasses Stylo's global pool.
**References:** `packages/blitz-dom/src/config.rs`, `stylo.rs`, `resolve.rs`; arch [Style threading]

**What breaks:** `tree[id]` on a dropped node panics with "invalid SlotMap key used". Since 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship (upstream #1185) a node the Dioxus bridge removes is dropped with its descendants and their `element_id_mapping` / `node_id_mapping` entries are cleared, so a re-render-removed node no longer resolves; until then the mappings were not cleared so dioxus-core could reuse detached nodes.
**How to avoid:** use `get` / `contains_key` for ids that may be stale; never treat a `NodeId` as a stable element identity across remounts.
**References:** `packages/blitz-dom/src/tree.rs`; `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stale_node_mapping.rs`

**What breaks:** `resolve` returns before styling while a `<head>` stylesheet is pending — layout reads look empty; a failed, empty or non-CSS stylesheet stops blocking render, and a bad `href`, `doc.url.resolve_relative` refusing it, starts no load.
**How to avoid:** headless loops resolve until the net provider `is_empty()`, then once more; a `NetProvider` with `is_noop() == true` registers no pending-critical resources; a wrapping handler must forward `NetHandler::error` or the failure stops at the wrapper, as blitz-test-harness's `CountedHandler` forwards it.
**References:** `packages/blitz-dom/src/resolve.rs`; `examples/screenshot.rs`

**What breaks:** hover/focus/active pointing at an anonymous block or a pseudo-element subtree.
**How to avoid:** hit-test results canonicalize to the element; removing a node retargets hover/active to the nearest surviving ancestor and resets focus to body.
**References:** `tests/blitz-tests/tests/interaction_state_*.rs`

title: The changed set is not a diff

data.head: ## The changed set is not a diff

body:
**What breaks:** reading `has_changes()` / `take_changed_nodes()` as "what an agent sees changed". The set is engine-touched: an attribute re-written to itself marks and changes no reading, a further character in a masked password marks and changes no reading, and bounds-only movement (a re-wrap, a scroll with no select list standing) changes a reading and marks nothing, while a select list's opening or closing, a page scroll or a move of the select's box that closes it included, marks its select, and a highlight or a wheel move inside the list marks nothing. It holds `NodeId`s of text nodes too, and a drained id may name a dropped node.
**How to avoid:** take what changed from `Snapshot::diff` over two snapshots; read a drained id through `get_node`; drain before a step you want to observe (after boot the set holds the initial build).
**References:** arch §Cross-cutting Patterns (Invalidation and state integrity); `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_diff.rs`

**What breaks:** a test that changes an attribute inserts `CONSTRUCT_BOX` everywhere and hides an under-damaging restyle bug.
**How to avoid:** drive pure-restyle paths with `:hover`; run both layout modes against the incremental oracle.
**References:** `tests/blitz-tests/tests/anonymous_block_cache_invalidation.rs`, `incremental_oracle.rs`

title: Unsupported CSS that silently reads false

data.head: ## Unsupported CSS that silently reads false

body:
**What breaks:** `:focus-visible`, `:valid`, `:invalid`, `:required`, `:target` always match false, while `:focus-within` matches the focused element and its ancestors by the `FOCUS_WITHIN` element state; Shadow DOM, container queries, 3D transforms, anchor positioning (hits `unreachable!()` on size variants), subgrid/masonry are absent; `background-clip: text` is not supported, `BackgroundClip::Text` being `gecko`-only on Stylo 0.22, and upstream `ac6f9f582`, which paints it, stays left out.
**How to avoid:** stand styles use `:focus`; never feed anchor-positioning sizes to `stylo_taffy`.
**References:** arch [Unsupported features]

**What breaks:** `resolve_url` panics on an unresolvable URL; `set_base_url` unwraps `Url::parse`; parse drivers unwrap `read_from`; shell/event-loop setup unwraps.
**How to avoid:** a driver validates URLs and inputs before handing them to these APIs; a refusal is a typed result, never a panic.
**References:** security-plan §Error Handling (Panic paths)

**What breaks:** text measures 0×0 without `system-fonts`, and some tests skip silently.
**How to avoid:** headless checks that need deterministic text bundle their fonts — the stand checks boot through `seven_guis::stand::options`, which registers the bundled DejaVu Sans with system fonts off (as the WASM builds do); the woff2 decodes only under blitz-dom's `woff` feature, which seven_guis enables itself so a package-alone `-p blitz-tests` build is not vacuous.
**References:** test-plan §8; `tests/blitz-tests/tests/text_selection_anonymous_block.rs`

title: Edition split under the write-time formatter

data.head: ## Edition split under the write-time formatter

body:
**What breaks:** `debug_timer` and `wgpu_texture` are edition 2021; the root `rustfmt.toml` says 2024, so the write-time `rustfmt` hook formats them 2024-style while `cargo fmt` passes their own edition.
**How to avoid:** after editing those two crates, run `cargo fmt --all` and let it win.
**References:** `rustfmt.toml`; `packages/debug_timer/Cargo.toml`; `examples/wgpu_texture/Cargo.toml`

title: Code that does not compile on a path

data.head: ## Code that does not compile on a path

body:
**What breaks:** blitz's non-`net` launch branch references `event_loop`, which is not a parameter of that function; `apps/browser/src/util.rs` is not declared as a module.
**How to avoid:** build with the feature combination you touch, not only the defaults.
**References:** `packages/blitz/src/lib.rs`; `apps/browser/src/main.rs`
- Runtime learnings: `.claude/docs/session-learnings.md`
- Path rules: `.claude/rules/*.md`
- Decisions and rationale: `.andromeda/architecture.md` §Established Decisions
_Distilled from `.andromeda/obs-plan.md` (adopted reading). wrap-session's cascade re-derives it when the plan changes._

**Tier:** 0
**Justification:** NOT YET MEASURED — the reading recorded no telemetry-surface table or must-trace paths.

- **escher's sink:** seven_guis' two binaries install it — `seven_guis_native` calls `escher_telemetry::init(service_identity!())` before `launch`, and the session host `escher-session` calls it first thing in `main` (in both an `Err` is `eprintln!`ed and the binary continues; both stamp `service.name=seven_guis`): a global `Registry` + `EnvFilter` (`RUST_LOG`, default `warn`) + one non-ANSI fmt layer with the escher formatter, printing each event and — a boundary widening ratified by the founder, 2026-10-09 (obs-plan §6) — each closed span of an admitted target, **stderr only**, plus the `log` → `tracing` bridge (`LogTracer`). Idempotent; a foreign subscriber is `InitError::ForeignSubscriber`, never a panic. The headless stand (`seven_guis::stand`, booted in-process by the `stand_*` checks) installs no subscriber — `stand_act_spans`'s two re-run children aside, which install the sink over an in-memory capture, and `stand_mcp_tools`, which installs a hand-written in-process recorder (not escher's sink) that prints nothing.

- **Line format:** `{RFC 3339 UTC time} {LEVEL} {target} service.name={name} service.version={version} {field}={value}…` — one text line per event, not JSON; identity from the binary's own `CARGO_PKG_NAME` / `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` (the OTel resource keys).

- **Upstream loggers:** engine crates emit `tracing` 0.1 events behind per-crate `tracing` features (no-op when off; off in a package-alone build, blitz-dom's turned on by a workspace-wide build); `tracing-subscriber` 0.3 `fmt::init()` to stdout in the upstream apps; `tracing_wasm` on wasm; `log` + `env_logger` in the WPT runner.

- **OTel SDK:** observed absent — escher 0.1.0 ships no OTel export (ruled by the founder, 2026-10-06): no OTel crate, egress or `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` credential path; the transport and the credential path stay undecided, held in `.andromeda/residuals.md` for a later version.

- **Agent-run harness log (measured, not a telemetry sink):** `scripts/agent-run.sh` (test-plan §3) prints JSON lines — `boot`, `run.start`, `test`, `run.end` (also appended to `target/agent-run/events.jsonl`), `status`, `cleanup` — encoded by python3's `json`; harness metadata only, no captured test output, no content-named field; raw cargo output in `target/agent-run/run.log`, never printed.

- **Cold-agent pipe log (measured, not a telemetry sink):** `scripts/cold-agent.sh` (test-plan §3) prints JSON lines — `run.start {ts, task}`, `run.end {every verdict field}` (also appended to `target/cold-agent/events.jsonl`), `status`, `cleanup` — encoded by python3's `json`; the pipe itself installs no `tracing` subscriber, OTel setup or third-party logger and reads no env var; since 2026-10-15-cold-agent-test (the stub and its call log gone) its per-run `mcp.json` spawns `escher-session mcp --record <abs target/cold-agent/record>` with `RUST_LOG=info` on that child only, so the child's escher sink writes its closed `tool_call` / `command` span lines to `target/cold-agent/server.log`, which the pipe reads only to count ` span="tool_call" ` lines, their ` ending="refused" ` / ` ending="error" ` and the accepted lines of each counted verb (`lint` · `screenshot` · `advance`, `span_counts`, giving the verdict's `lint_calls` · `screenshot_calls` · `advance_calls`), never printing or copying it; a judged check is replayed on two further `escher-session mcp` children without `--record`, stderr to `/dev/null`; the agent's check goes to `check.json` and the live session's kept checks to the owner-only `target/cold-agent/record/` (`mkdir -m 700`), none printed or copied.
- **escher's sink — JSON schema · log-file sink · rotation · heartbeat:** NOT YET MEASURED.

- **Embedder drain:** `take_js_errors` / `take_messages` on `ScriptDocument` (≤256 errors retained between drains). A failed fetch in `NetProvider::fetch` logs `Error fetching` and reaches its handler through `NetHandler::error`, a default that does nothing unless the handler overrides it; a stylesheet's handler responds `Err(error)`, so `pending_critical_resources` loses the request and a failed, empty or non-CSS stylesheet stops blocking render, the error text stopping in `ResourceLoadResponse` and the `Resource load failed` line; a bad `href` starts no load, so it reaches no fetch or load line.
| Operation | Output |
| `resolve` phase times (style … subdocs) | printed, `log-phase-times` |
| Frame times | `log-frame-times` per anyrender backend |
| `debug_timer` labelled instants | stdout when `enable` |
| Browser FPS overlay | in-app |
| WPT per-test / per-run stats | printed; scores to Pages (upstream `DioxusLabs/blitz` only) |

No metric counters, gauges, histograms or exporters exist; blitz-paint's layer counters are held in process, and the bench, screenshot and `multi_doc` examples and `paint_tree_bench` print their timings.

CI artifacts (§9): each ci.yml leg's merged output, `target/ci-logs/{leg}.log`, is uploaded only when the leg fails (`ci-log-{job id}`, kept 7 days, unscrubbed build output); the `coverage` job also uploads `coverage-report` (`target/coverage/`, line counts, no user data, `keyboard_compat.rs` excluded by filename since 2026-10-17-upstream-sync-engine-debts) on success, kept 7 days. The package install's output (`.github/scripts/apt-install.sh`; one stderr line per failed attempt) stays in the job's step log — no leg log holds it and no artifact uploads it. The agent-run state area `target/agent-run/`, the cold-agent pipe's `target/cold-agent/`, a session's state directory (`0700`, its socket alone, no log, event or screen content) and a session's recording directory (named by `--record` or `Session::recording_into`, `0700`, one `check-{n}.json` (`0600`, `create_new`) per recorded session holding call content at rest — target ids, a `press` key, an `advance`'s ms, unmasked typed text, a `type` to a masked or unresolved control as `masked` — with each call's `accepted`, its answer digest and the answer kept whole as `answer` — the line the driver wrote, masked as on every carrier, a shot's as `{width, height}` without `png` — so the screens' ids, names, values, snapshot text, diffs and a lint's findings at rest, and no log or event line; unix only; the checks write theirs under `target/tmp/`) are local only — no CI job uploads any of them. Two kept checks are committed in git, `tests/blitz-tests/checks/counter-cli.json` and `counter-mcp.json` (mode `100644`, a public repository): the repository's own scripted stand-Counter sessions, written by `examples/seven_guis/tests/flows/record_checks.sh` (which prints only `step N`), holding the Counter's ids, names, values, snapshot text and diffs and the scripts' calls, no typed text, host path, name, secret or `screenshot` step — read by `stand_replay` and seven_guis' freshness check; no log or event line; uploaded by no CI leg.

- escher-telemetry: `info` `telemetry installed` at target `escher_telemetry` (no argv / path / URL); ERROR `panic` at target `escher_telemetry::panic` with `panic.file` · `panic.line` · `panic.column` · `panic.payload` (redacted).

- Panic hooks: escher's native hook chains (logs, then runs the previous hook — std still prints the raw message, exit code unchanged); `console_error_panic_hook` on WASM; the WPT runner's hook replaces.
> NO RECORDED INTENT.

- **escher's sink applies a target allowlist:** a target starting `blitz` · `dioxus_native` · `stylo_taffy` · `accesskit_xplat` · `debug_timer` · `js_console` prints only `node_id` · `status` · `waiting_nodes` · `property` · `log.module_path` · `log.file` · `log.line` — the message and every other field read `[redacted]`; a target starting `escher_` prints every field except `url` · `href` · `src` · `html` · `text` · `value` · `attrs` · `path` · `request` · `error` · `panic.payload`, which are redacted; a record from any other target is dropped whole — zero bytes, at every level, WARN and ERROR included, whatever `RUST_LOG` names.

- **Logged as-is elsewhere:** the upstream apps' `fmt::init()` and the WPT runner's `env_logger` carry visited URLs, resource URLs, link hrefs, element attributes, outer HTML of failed SVGs, CSS values and text-node contents unscrubbed. Past escher's scrub: std's panic hook prints the raw message, and `log.file` can carry a host path only for a bridged record under an engine target (recorded by construction, not measured). No record from a target outside the allowlist reaches stderr: both sink-installing binaries read no stable id and no accessible name at the default level, `info`, `debug` and `trace` — 0 lines at the default level, the one install line at the others (`escher-session` 1165 → 1 lines at `debug`, 1501 → 1 at `trace`; the windowed stand 12,413 → 1 and 47,482 → 1); the cost is that a third-party WARN or ERROR no longer prints. Typed text is measured in a host's log since 2026-10-10-driver-cli: a hosted `type` reaches the `escher-session` host's instance, and its stderr at `trace` holds 0 occurrences of a typed sentinel, 0 id needles and 0 name needles under both builds (`host_log`); by level, three commands on CRUD write 0 lines unset and 4 from `info` up on the host built alone — three command spans and the install line — and 6 on the workspace-built host, the `blitz_dom::document` INFO line printing twice (re-measured at 2026-10-14-stand-requirement-sweep). It was first measured in process — `stand_act_spans` drives the driver's commands with the sink over a capture at `info` and reads 0 occurrences of the supplied texts, 0 of 36 ids and 0 of 8 names; since 2026-10-14-quality-gates a client's own stderr, the host on flows beyond those three commands and the windowed stand built with the workspace, on the host's display, are measured too — 28 runs by build and level, 0 needles in every run (the client's a one-off reading). Since 2026-10-24-stand-requirement-sweep a recording session's clients are read by a standing check: `host_log`'s third test (unix only) runs each client command at `trace` — `start crud --record`, `type` with a sentinel, `snapshot`, `snapshot --part 1`, `lint`, `stop` — in `hl-client` and `hl-client-rec`, and over all the clients' own stderr reads 0 id, 0 name, 0 sentinel, 0 recording-path and 0 `recorded_needles` occurrences under both builds; a paged `part` read through the `escher-session` host's own sink is read by `host_log`'s fourth test (unix only), which runs `serve cells` at `RUST_LOG=trace` in `hl-cells`, commits a sentinel into a part-2 cell and calls `snapshot --part 2`: 0 id and 0 name needles under both builds, its failures naming a kind and a count only (`host_log` 4; measured at 2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar). A `multiple` select's chosen set leaves only as form entries — on `input` and `change` one `(name, FormValue::Text(value))` per chosen option (`multiple_select_values`) — as the snapshot's `value`, the first chosen option in tree order, and as the options' tree nodes, never as a log line or field, the added-lines census reading 0 (2026-10-31-engine-debts). `size` on a `multiple` select is an attribute read, parsed into a whole number capped at 65534, carrying no text out and moving no redaction shape, an engine change for every document and a boundary widening, ratified (2026-10-31-select-popup). A failed load's error text travels `NetHandler::error` into `ResourceLoadResponse` and the `Resource load failed` line; `url` and `error` are in escher-telemetry's scrub set, so the sink prints `waiting_nodes` and every other field, the message included, `[redacted]`, and no other carrier takes the text (2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph). A shot's image (since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot) is screen content that leaves only in its answer: 0 occurrences of the first 64 base64 characters of a shot in the `escher-session` host's and the `mcp` role's stderr at `trace`, under both builds (`host_log`, `mcp_log`). A shot of an open list carries a page's option labels and group `label`s as pixels, a boundary widening ratified, the shot's own fields unmoved. An `optgroup`'s non-empty `label` is its `Role::Group` name in the accessibility tree, inside the ratified name crossing, and it is also painted, as a group's header in an open list, leaving as pixels in a shot and on no log line or field, a boundary widening ratified; the added lines hold no log site, print or env read, the added-lines census reading 0 (2026-10-31-engine-debts). `SelectListRow.label` holds page text in a public read type and is never logged; a label leaves only as a painted pixel and the snapshot's existing `name` (2026-10-31-select-popup). A lint's line is `span="command" verb="lint"` (with `cause` when refused) and holds no finding, id, bound or count — `host_log` and `mcp_log` each drive one `lint` at `trace` with 0 needles. A part read's line is `span="command" verb="snapshot"` (with `cause` when refused, a `part` outside 1 to 1000 refused `malformed`) and holds no part number, count, size or text — `host_log` and `mcp_log` each drive one part read at `trace` with 0 needles. An option's label is in neither log: `host_log` (unix only, in `hl-popup`) and `mcp_log` each read a select list opened and chosen at `trace`, 0 option needles (2026-10-31-select-popup). A recording host and a recording `mcp` role read at `trace` hold 0 of the recording needles (the kept check's directory name and contents), the span counts unchanged (`host_log`, `mcp_log`); the kept check itself holds call content at rest, unmasked typed text included, and each answer itself as `answer` (a shot's without `png`) — the screens' ids, names, values, snapshot text, diffs and a lint's findings at rest — a file, never a log line, field or print. An open list's row crosses the snapshot and the diff by its own `bounds`, `differs` naming `bounds` within its closed set, adding no field, key name, node key or carrier (2026-10-31-select-popup). The engine's `change` on a checkbox or radio, sent after `input` with the same value, a checkbox always and a radio only where it was not checked before the click, carries the value class `input` already carries; a page's script hears one `change`, from the engine, the script runtime synthesising none; the added lines hold no log site, print or env read, the added-lines census reading 0 (2026-10-31-engine-debts).

- **Agent-run harness:** outside escher's scrub but carries no user content — its event fields take no content-named name and no captured test output; `target/agent-run/run.log` is raw cargo/libtest output, unscrubbed like `target/ci-logs/`, gitignored.

- **Cold-agent pipe:** outside escher's scrub; no event or verdict key is content-named and no transcript text, tool argument, tool answer, reply or check reaches one; the stub's call log is retired with the stub (2026-10-15-cold-agent-test). `target/cold-agent/server.log` is escher's sink output (the allowlist formatter's redaction), counted by span name and never printed or copied; `check.json` holds the agent's check — stand fixture ids and texts — never printed; the live session's kept checks under the owner-only `target/cold-agent/record/` hold its calls and answers at rest, never printed, copied or committed. `target/cold-agent/transcript.jsonl` is raw by design (model output and tool I/O — since 2026-10-15-cold-agent-test the stand's screens from the escher server, element ids, accessible names and control values in snapshot texts and diffs, and on the live run of six apps also Cells' contents, the flight booker's select options and value, a lint's findings and a shot, carried to the model provider on the founder's «Один запуск, до $3 (Рекомендую)» (2026-10-15) — host paths, the client's socket path, a rate-limit line), never printed, gitignored; each committed copy (the live runs' evidence) masks the session dir and the home prefix.

escher is a native-API engine library with no served network API, no served TCP or UDP port — two `blitz-net` tests alone binding TCP on loopback, served by no binary — and no authentication; its one listener is local — the driver session's owner-only Unix-domain socket, which carries the session's lifecycle and, since 2026-10-10-driver-cli, driver calls and their answers (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10); since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface the same calls and answers also cross to an MCP client over the `escher-session mcp` role's own stdio, no listener (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10). title: Threat model highlights (attack surface as measured)

data.head: ## Threat model highlights (attack surface as measured)

body: - **Remote web content** → iframe depth cap 10, `@import` depth cap 16, stale iframe responses discarded by request id; since 2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph, in every document, remote pages included, a failed, empty or non-CSS stylesheet blocks no render (a load that errs reaches `ResourceHandler<StylesheetHandler>::error`, which responds `Err(error)`, so `pending_critical_resources` loses the request) — an engine change for every document; snapshotting a never-styled node is skipped (Stylo would panic); since 2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph, in every document, remote pages included, a stylesheet `href` that cannot be resolved starts no load and blocks no render, read through `doc.url.resolve_relative` and not `resolve_url`, which panics — an engine change for every document; a key press with focus on a control whose anonymous block was dropped does not panic, for `hidden`, `style="display:none"` and CSS alone, `BaseDocument::deallocate_anonymous_block` setting `layout_parent` to `None` on each child still in the slab naming the block; focus stays and the key still acts, `DocumentMutator::flush` unedited; since 2026-10-31-engine-debts `Node::hit_inner` answers `None` for the whole subtree of a transform whose determinant is 0 or not finite, so it takes no hit, on every document, remote pages included, with no log site, print, env read or panic path — an engine change for every document, ratified; since 2026-10-13-range-input-interaction an `input type="range"` in every document — remote pages included — keeps a current value from `min` · `max` · `step` · `value` read through `parse_float`, sanitized finite, clamped and on its step grid, moved by the arrows, `Home` · `End` and pointerdown only with no `disabled` attribute, with no log site or panic path — an engine change for every document and a boundary widening, ratified by the founder (2026-10-07, 2026-10-13); since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness, in every document — remote pages included — `Enter` on a focused `button`, `summary`, submit/reset/button `input` or `a` with `href`, and a released Space on a focused `button`, `summary` or submit/reset/button/checkbox/radio `input`, dispatch a Click (handlers, then `handle_click`: form submission, link navigation, `summary` toggling) only when it is no disabled form control (a `disabled` attribute on a `summary` or an `a` gating neither key), a click on a button focuses it, and `disabled` is read by presence on a form control alone (`button` · `input` · `select` · `textarea`, `ElementData::is_disabled`; `"false"` included; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) for focusability, the pointer and click gates and the activation keys, so a `<div disabled tabindex=0>` takes focus and a disabled ancestor `div` does not stop the click walk, the snapshot's `enabled` reading the same presence — closed name and type gates, no log site or panic path, no carrier, verb, key name, field or span added — an engine change for every document and a boundary widening, ratified by the founder (2026-10-13, 2026-10-14); since 2026-10-31-engine-debts, in every document, remote pages included, `handle_click`'s checkbox and radio arms send, after `input`, a `DomEventData::Change` with the same value, the value class `input` carries — a checkbox always, a radio only where it was not checked before the click — `blitz-vibey-script`'s runtime synthesizing none, so a page's script hears one `change`, from the engine, with no carrier, verb, argument, key name, result field, cause, session error, exit, log field or span added — an engine change for every document and a boundary widening, ratified; since 2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph, behind the `custom-widget` feature, `ElementData::set_custom_widget` replays each existing attribute, parsed page content included, to `Widget::attribute_changed` with no old value, the value's check staying the widget's own — an engine change for every document behind the feature, ratified; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-19, F1 A), a check of any other session never committed; a failed write or a passed bound (400 records, 1,048,576 bytes) ends the recording, its check removed — while the three list lengths of a diff the driver returns (counts only) are recorded on its command span and printed by the sink at `info` or below (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-09: the sentence stands, with the clarification that a diff's content never reaches a log while its three sizes may); since 2026-10-07-act-by-id that caller can be the caller of the driver's `Session::run` — its `snapshot` command returns the text and its acting commands the diff, in process, through the command line or, since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface, as MCP tool results — and since the sink drops every record from a target outside its allowlist, a sink-installing binary's stderr carries no author-key id, no accessible name and no typed text at any `RUST_LOG` level (measured on the `escher-session` host and its `mcp` role while they run calls, and on a recording session's clients: 0 id needles, 0 name needles and 0 occurrences of a typed sentinel at `trace`, under both builds; a paged part read is measured in process and through the `escher-session` host's own sink — seven_guis `host_log` runs `serve cells` at `RUST_LOG=trace`, commits a sentinel into a part-2 cell and reads `snapshot --part 2`: 0 id and 0 name needles under both builds); a password's and a file input's value read the fixed mask, while the file input's DOM attribute and form submission still hold the host path; since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot the mask also holds on the screen's pixels — blitz-paint paints a password `input` masked, a bullet per character, in every document and through every renderer that paints with it (an engine change ratified by the founder, 2026-10-12), so a password typed through the driver never leaves as pixels in a `screenshot`, and since 2026-10-19-session-recording a recorded `type` whose element resolves to a masked control (`dioxus_native_dom::is_masked_input`) or to none is kept in the check as `MASKED_STAND_IN` (`"masked"`) with `masked:true`, never the text, its length or a digest of it (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-19: F1 A · F2 B), though the frame depends on the value's length; a file input's paint is unchanged, and a shot's image reaches no log (its first 64 base64 characters occur 0 times in the `escher-session` host's and the `mcp` role's stderr at `trace`, under both builds) |

| Logged values | request URLs, cache dir path, attribute values | escher's stderr sink (`seven_guis_native`, `escher-session`) redacts them by a target allowlist — engine targets print only safe fields, escher targets redact content-named fields, and a record from any other target is dropped whole at every level (no element id and no accessible name on stderr at `debug` or `trace`); a failed load's error text stops in `ResourceLoadResponse` and the `Resource load failed` line, no carrier taking it, the sink printing `waiting_nodes` and every other field of that line, the message included, `[redacted]`; the upstream apps' `fmt::init()` and the WPT runner's `env_logger` log them as-is |
