_Crate notes. Primary source: `.andromeda/architecture.md` (§Standard Contracts, §Existing Scopes, §Infrastructure Patterns)._

The headless DOM (`BaseDocument`): node tree, CSS parsing and resolution through Stylo, damage, box construction, Taffy/Parley layout, paint-tree topology, event dispatch, scrolling, selection, CSSOM, forms, iframes and the AccessKit tree. It does NOT parse HTML (blitz-html), fetch (blitz-net), paint (blitz-paint) or own windows (blitz-shell). Driven by external code; most users go through a wrapper (`HtmlDocument`, `DioxusDocument`, `ScriptDocument`).

- Provider traits from blitz-traits via `DocumentConfig`: `NetProvider`, `NavigationProvider`, `ShellProvider`, `HtmlParserProvider` (`Dummy*` defaults). `NetHandler::error(url, error)` stands beside `bytes`: `ResourceHandler<StylesheetHandler>::error` responds `Err(error)`, so `pending_critical_resources` loses the request and a failed stylesheet stops blocking render, and `net.rs`'s other resource kinds keep the trait's do-nothing default; an engine change for every document.

- Stylo 0.22, Taffy 0.15 (crates.io registry since 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship, a git rev until then) via `stylo_taffy`, Parley 0.12 (registry), ICU4X 2.3, accesskit (feature `accessibility`).

- `Document` trait (`inner`, `inner_mut`, `handle_ui_event`, `poll`, `id`, and under `accessibility` a default `accessibility_tree` a wrapper may override), `BaseDocument`, the document's clock (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18: `DocumentConfig.clock: Option<Arc<dyn Clock>>`, `None` by default and the document then holding a fresh `WallClock` — wall time, as before — read for the overlay scrollbar fade, the double-click window, pan and the fling's generation, the smooth-scroll start and the fling and smooth frames, a sub-document's config carrying its parent's clock; the crate root re-exports `Clock` (`Send + Sync`, `now() -> Duration`), `WallClock` and `VirtualClock` (every clone reading one time, `advance(Duration)` adding with saturation), and no `Instant::now()` or `SystemTime::now()` stands outside `clock.rs` — an API addition flagged upstreamable), `DocumentMutator` (`set_attribute`, `clear_attribute`, removal and insertion restyle through `restyle_for_attribute_change` and `restyle_for_child_list_change`, with no blanket `RestyleHint::restyle_subtree()`, and the changed-set insert in `remove_and_drop_all_children` stands first; public `BaseDocument::snapshot_node` takes `attr: &LocalName`, its two callers both in `mutator.rs`; an engine change for every document), `EventDriver`/`EventHandler`, query-selector API, CSSOM (the resolved `width` and `height` of `resolved_style_value` read `node.unrounded_layout()`, so a reader gets sub-pixel values where `final_layout` rounds; an engine change for every document), scroll API (`scroll_into_view` scrolls every scrolling box that holds its target, innermost first, then the viewport — a nested box at once, the requested behaviour for the viewport alone — and on a row of an open select list writes the list's `scroll_y` at once and returns, moving no chain and no viewport; `visible_region` reads the part of the viewport an element can be seen through — never a hit — and for a row or a group of an open select list the list's scrollport), the hit walk (`hit_with_scrollbar` answers an open select list first and no scrollbar with it, `hit_inner` holding none of it, so `hit`, `set_hover_to` and `handle_pointerdown` all read the list; past that the walk tests a node's own area where the box stands and stops at the padding box of every box paint clips — either axis of its computed `overflow` not `visible`, or a computed `contain` that includes `paint` (that half ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) — the root element excepted — and skips a node dropped since the last resolve and answers nothing for the whole subtree of a transform whose determinant is 0 or not finite; a box clipped on one axis stops it at its whole padding box while `visible_region` narrows that box on its clipped axis only, so a target beside it along its unclipped axis reads in view and is not reached by a hit — measured since 2026-10-14-stand-requirement-sweep and left as it reads, as are a hit at an element's own box and at a box both transformed and scrolled), `Node::absolute_position` (only its containing blocks' scroll offsets subtracted, so a box that is itself scrolled reads where it stands, its callers — `scroll_into_view` and the test harness's `layout_rect`, `layout_rect_of` and `center_of` among them — moving with it (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18)), `get_client_bounding_rect` and `node_client_rects` (an element read where its transforms move it, as CSSOM View's `getBoundingClientRect` does (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), and `visible_region` reads each clipping box through its transforms via the private `padding_box_in_view` over `transformed_bounds` — exact under a translate and a scale, under a rotation the rotated padding box's bounding box, so it holds corners the box does not show (a measured limit), `None` for a mapped box with a non-finite edge), `build_accessibility_tree` (names from five sources — text children, a trimmed-non-empty `aria-label`, `<label>` association (its `for`-target labelable element by id, else its first nested labelable element — HTML's labelable elements, `button`, an `input` whose `type` is not `hidden`, `meter`, `output`, `progress`, `select` and `textarea`, matched by the private `is_labelable` — pushed onto the bound element's `labelled_by`), a select's option's non-empty `label` attribute where it has no `aria-label`, an `optgroup`'s on its `Role::Group`, named in the tree and painted as a header in an open list, and, since the 2026-10-17 upstream sync, `aria-labelledby`, whose targets' text is set as the computed `label` and outranks a `<label>` and an `aria-label` (the `aria-label` the fallback when the targets hold no text); the same sync's builder also reads `aria-describedby` (pushed as `described_by`), `aria-description` (AccessKit's description field), `aria-expanded` (a boolean, a single select excepted, which reads none and writes `expanded` from its list, an author's `open` on a select steering nothing), `aria-disabled` (`true` sets AccessKit disabled) and `aria-level` (a number, with defaults by tag and role); since 2026-10-10-snapshot-states four state attributes read by value on every element — a select's option excepted, whose `selected` is its chosen state, true or false, with no `aria-selected` read —, the toggle by role — `aria-selected` → `selected`, `aria-pressed` → `toggled` on every role but the five checkable ones, `aria-checked` → `toggled` on those five alone (`CheckBox` · `Switch` · `RadioButton` · `MenuItemCheckBox` · `MenuItemRadio`), neither on a native `checkbox` or `radio` `input`, whose own `checkbox_input_checked()` writes `Toggled::True` or `False` under a checkable role and nothing under any other, an engine change for every document (the toggle read per role ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), `aria-invalid` → `invalid`, each a closed-set match on the trimmed lower-case value, an unrecognized `aria-invalid` reading `Invalid::True`, no log site and no panic path — a direct engine change for every document, ratified by the founder and flagged upstreamable; check `accessibility_states`; the tree's `focus` is written only where `focus_node_id` is among the built nodes, else `u64::MAX`, the window, so the tree never names a node it did not build, an engine change for every document), `BoundingRect`, CSSOM View accessors, `Widget` trait, the public `ElementData::flush_open_state(&mut self)` (it sets `ElementState::OPEN` on a `details` or `dialog` carrying an `open` attribute and clears it on any other; `ElementData::new` calls it, and so do `DocumentMutator::set_attribute` — its arm a second independent `if` after the range re-sanitize arm — and `clear_attribute` on an `open` write, and Stylo's `NonTSPseudoClass::Open` reads that state, so `:open` matches such an element in every document — an upstream engine change, not counted among escher's direct ones), since 2026-10-13-range-input-interaction a range input's current value — `SpecialElementData::RangeInput` (a source break for an external exhaustive match, `SpecialElementData` not being `#[non_exhaustive]`), `RangeInputData` (its one public method `value() -> f64`, exported from `blitz_dom::node` and not re-exported from the crate root) and the public `ElementData` accessors `range_input_data()`, `range_input_data_mut()` and `range_input_value() -> Option<String>` (the formatted current value), `RangeRules`, `RangeMove` and the range helpers crate-internal — and since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot two public read-only methods: `BaseDocument::can_paint_text(&self) -> bool` (whether the font context resolves a family for the `sans-serif` generic, through fontique's `generic_families`) and `BaseDocument::layout_as_text_input(&self, node_id, text) -> Option<parley::Layout<TextBrush>>` (`text` laid out with a text input's editor styles, scale and direction in the document's own fonts, one unbroken line, a fresh `LayoutContext` per call, `None` for a node that is no text input — its two callers are blitz-paint's password mask and blitz-dom's password click caret (`click_password_input`)), and a third read-only reader, `BaseDocument::text_extent(&self, NodeId) -> Option<TextExtent>` with `TextExtent { content, text }` (two `BoundingRect`s, re-exported from the crate root): `content` the client rect less border, padding and any scrollbar, `text` from the content box's top-left moved down by the inline layout's `block_offset` and sized by Parley `Layout::width()` / `height()` over its scale, `None` for an id that does not resolve, a node that is no inline root or one with no inline layout data — it mutates nothing and has no log site, print, env read or panic path; RTL and vertical text read as LTR horizontal lines and a transformed box at its client rect, each pinned by blitz-tests' `text_extent` in both layout modes; its one non-test caller escher-driver's `Session::lint`. Since 2026-10-13-range-input-interaction the range interaction model, a fifth direct engine change for every document (ratified by the founder, flagged upstreamable): an `input` whose `type` reads `range` (ASCII case-insensitive) holds its current value apart from its `value` attribute, its rules in `node/range.rs` against the WHATWG range state (`min` 0, `max` 100 and `step` 1 by default, every value sanitized to `[min, max]` and the nearest grid value); focused and with no `disabled` attribute, `ArrowRight`/`ArrowUp` step it up, `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowDown` down, `Home`/`End` take it to its minimum/maximum, every other key does nothing; a main-button pointerdown sets the value from the hit's fraction of the content box and a click focuses it and changes no value; each change fires one `input` event through the crate-internal `BaseDocument::apply_range_move` and a move that changes nothing fires none (since 2026-10-16-handler-splits-and-readme the range arms' bodies are private named functions — `press_range_input_key` for the keys, `range_track_fraction` and `press_range_input` for the pointerdown — still writing only through `apply_range_move`, `handle_key_or_input_event` and `handle_pointerdown` keeping their signatures, no behaviour changed for any document); a `value` write re-seeds the current value and a `min`, `max` or `step` write or removal re-sanitizes it (a departure from the spec's dirty-value flag, so a Dioxus re-render keeps control); form submission sends the formatted current value. Since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness three more direct engine changes for every document (answered by the founder, flagged upstreamable), the sixth to the eighth: keyboard activation — a pressed `Enter` on the focused node, after the text-input and range arms, dispatches a Click on a `button`, a `summary`, an `input` of type `submit`, `reset` or `button`, or an `a` with `href`, and a released Space (`DomEventData::KeyUp`'s new default action, routed by `events/mod.rs` to the crate-internal `handle_key_up`) the same Click on a `button`, a `summary`, or an `input` of type `submit`, `reset`, `button`, `checkbox` or `radio` — neither a disabled form control, a link taking no Space and a text or range input neither key — both through `dispatch_activation_click` (data `Node::synthetic_click_event_data(modifiers)`, queued by the event driver so the app's handlers run before the default action `handle_click`); a click focuses a button — `handle_click`'s button arm focuses a `button` of any type or an `input` of type `submit`, `reset` or `button` through `generate_focus_events` / `set_focus_to` before it submits a submit button's form owner — since 2026-10-16-handler-splits-and-readme in the private `click_button`, `handle_click` keeping its signature, no behaviour changed — a click on a `select` focusing it through its own arm of the walk, a click on a `multiple` select's row focusing that select through the walk's `option` arm and a click on any other element still clearing focus; and `disabled` is read by presence on a form control alone (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18): the public `ElementData::is_disabled` — `can_be_disabled()` (`button` · `input` · `select` · `textarea`) and a `disabled` attribute present — is what focusability (`ElementData::flush_is_focussable`), the pointer gates and the activation keys read, so a bare, a `"false"` and a `"true"` `disabled` on a form control remove its focusability while a `<div disabled tabindex=0>` takes focus and a `<summary disabled>` or an `<a href disabled>` takes Enter, Space and a click. `inert` is honoured by its presence on an element or an ancestor (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18): `Node::is_focussable` reads false through the crate-private `Node::is_inert`, so the Tab walk, autofocus and `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable` skip it, `hit_inner` answers no hit at it, and the accessibility builder leaves its subtree out of the tree; HTML's focus fixup stands without its events: a node that holds focus when it comes under `inert`, a subtree moved under an inert box included, gives it up at `DocumentMutator::flush` through `BaseDocument::clear_focus`, firing no DOM `blur` or `focusout`, the fixup reading neither `disabled` nor `hidden`. Focus keeps `:focus-within` on its ancestors and asks for a frame (upstream #1226, a partial take now ratified): `BaseDocument::set_focus_to` returns `false` for a node not in the document, moves the `FOCUS_WITHIN` element state from the old focus's element ancestors to the new focus's (the shared prefix keeping it) and requests a redraw; `clear_focus` removes it from the cleared node's element ancestors and requests a redraw; a removed focus clears its chain, and `DocumentMutator::add_children_to_parent` carries the state with a moved subtree that holds the focus, or only clears the old chain when the focus left with it; the Tab key asks for no redraw of its own. Beside these, eight more ratified direct engine changes for every document — `visible_region` through transforms, a non-invertible transform's no hit, the focus fixup under `inert`, the tree's focus falling back to the window, a native control's `toggled` on a checkable role, the `multiple` select, `optgroup`, and `change` on a checkbox and a radio (`handle_click`'s arms dispatching `DomEventData::Change` after `input` with the same value, a checkbox always, a radio only where it was not checked before the click) — each flagged upstreamable and nothing sent, their merge surface a line owned by Upstream sync ahead of determinism and exploration, upstream `0980cce5f`'s `hit_inner` hunk a textual conflict with the non-invertible answer for the next sync, `0980cce5f` being left out at `e42ee1f25`. A dropped anonymous block clears its children's `layout_parent` beside those eight, a direct engine change for every document (ratified, flagged upstreamable and nothing sent, its merge surface a line owned by Upstream sync ahead of determinism and exploration): `BaseDocument::deallocate_anonymous_block` takes the block's `layout_children` and sets `layout_parent` to `None` on each child still in the slab naming the block, so a key press with focus on a control whose anonymous block was dropped does not panic, for `hidden`, `style="display:none"` and CSS alone, and every reader of a stale `layout_parent` is cured with it; focus stays and the key still acts, `DocumentMutator::flush` reading `is_inert()` alone. The select model, a direct engine change for every document, remote pages included (flagged upstreamable, no upstream pull request open): a `select`'s choice, or a `multiple` select's chosen set, is held as its options' `CHECKED` element state, so `:checked` matches the chosen option, and an option created with a `selected` attribute is seeded `CHECKED`; its rules sit in the crate-private `node::select` (no public type), cited to the WHATWG `select` element — a select's options are its `option` children and its `optgroup` children's, in tree order, an option's disabled reading the one rule `option_disabled`, its own attribute or its group's, an option's label its non-empty `label` attribute else its stripped and collapsed text, its value its `value` attribute when present else the text, and a single-choice select is settled by HTML's selectedness setting algorithm (the last chosen option, else the first option not disabled); the mutator records every select whose children an entry point touches, every select entering the document and the select of a `multiple` write or removal (`record_select_of_multiple_write`), so a removal settles its set to one option, a `selected` write sets that option chosen and, on a single-choice select, its select's other options not, a `multiple` select's others left alone, a cleared one sets it not chosen, and `flush` settles every recorded select, firing no event; a focused single-choice select, its list closed, that is no disabled form control takes a pressed `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` to the next / previous enabled option and `Home` / `End` to the first / last (with none chosen `ArrowDown` reads as `Home` and `ArrowUp` as `End`), and a character pressed with no Ctrl, Alt or Meta as typeahead — the first enabled option whose label starts with the buffered text, in lower case, the buffer (`select_typeahead`) starting afresh for another select or once the document's clock has moved 1 s (`TYPEAHEAD_TIMEOUT`) — Enter, and a Space with no typed text standing, opening its list, every other key doing nothing and a released Space doing nothing more; a focused `multiple` select takes its keys through `press_multiple_select_key`: `ArrowDown`, `ArrowUp`, `Home` and `End` alone choose that row alone, with Shift span from the anchor, and with Ctrl or Meta move the current row and change nothing, a Space flips the current row with no typed text standing and joins the text otherwise, a character with no Ctrl, Alt or Meta chooses its match alone, and disabled rows are never chosen; - `dispatch_recorded` installs a `RecordingHandler` on the underlying `BaseDocument` — it bypasses Dioxus VirtualDom forwarding.
- `dom_string()` is a stable one-node-per-line tree with geometry.
- The `query` helper panics with "invalid selector" on a selector that fails to parse.
- Synthesized pointer events set page = screen = client coordinates.

The headless Dioxus renderer on blitz: `DioxusDocument` integrates `BaseDocument` with a `VirtualDom`, writes vdom mutations into the DOM and routes DOM events back to vdom handlers. The windowed `dioxus-native` crate builds on it; the seven_guis stand runs through it.
- blitz-dom (shared as `Rc<RefCell<BaseDocument>>`), dioxus-core / dioxus-html 0.7.3.
- `DioxusDocument` (`vdom`, `inner`, `initial_build`, `poll`, `handle_ui_event`, `vdom_state.try_element_to_node_id(ElementId)`), `NodeHandle` backing `MountedData`.

- Stable element ids: `element_id(NodeId) -> Option<String>` and `element_ids() -> Vec<(NodeId, String)>` (document pre-order, pairwise distinct), computed on demand and written to neither the DOM nor the vdom; under the `accessibility` feature (which enables an optional `accesskit` and is forwarded from dioxus-native's) `DioxusDocument`'s `Document::accessibility_tree` override carries each one as its element node's AccessKit `author_id`, never on a `TextRun`, the document root or the `Window` node — four tiers: author key (the HTML `id`: non-empty, `/`-free, first in document order) → anchored path (`{key}//{segment}`, e.g. `box//p:0/b:0`, for an element under an element of its own component instance that reads an author key; the nearest one anchors) → component path (`TaskShell/Counter/div:0`; `{tag}[{key}]` for a Dioxus-keyed root; a component's template root always restarts here, so an anchor acts inside one component only) → document path (`/html:0/body:0`). An unusable `id` (empty, `/`-bearing, a later duplicate) neither keys nor anchors, and an anchored path is the only id holding `//`. Proven persistent on the stand: the same id across a re-render, a remount (fresh `NodeId`s for every element bar the `html`/`head`/`body`/`#main` skeleton, which lives outside the VirtualDom) and a second process (`stand_id_persistence`), and across edits of the code around an element — a keyed element under every edit, an anchored one under an edit outside its keyed element, any element under a behaviour edit; an earlier same-tag sibling or a wrapper inside the subtree a path starts at still renames an unkeyed element (`stand_id_edits`).

- Actionable-key check (under `accessibility` only): `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable() -> Vec<UnkeyedActionable>` returns every actionable element whose id is a positional path, in document pre-order — actionable meaning focusable (`Node::is_focussable()`), or an interactive role on its accessibility node, or a listener (`data-dioxus-id`), so a disabled control is held by its role and a hidden one by the other two. `UnkeyedActionable` carries `node` (a process-local `NodeId`), `id`, `tag`, `role: Option<Role>`, `focusable`, `interactive_role`, `listener` and `remedy()`; never text, a name or an attribute value. Read-only, logs nothing; no wire form and no driver command yet. The stand reads it empty on the four lean tasks and Home and, since 2026-10-14-stand-requirement-sweep, on Temperature Converter, Circle Drawer (its dialog open included) and Cells too (2 · 3 · 676 until then), and on the load page `stand::boot_load` mounts, its two elements keyed `load-fetch` · `load-done` — empty on all six served tasks (`stand_load_page`), keyed by author ids added as `id:` lines alone (`stand_actionable_keys`, `stand_non_lean_tasks`).

- Snapshot model (under `accessibility` only): `DioxusDocument::snapshot() -> Snapshot`, a read-only tree built from the `accessibility_tree` override. `Snapshot { roots }` with `nodes()` (pre-order) and `get(id)`; a `SnapshotNode` carries `id` (the `author_id`), `role` (`accesskit::Role`), `name` (the node's `label`, else its `labelled_by` targets' names, trimmed — since the 2026-10-17 upstream sync the `label` is also the computed text of an element's `aria-labelledby` targets, which outranks a `<label>`, while the snapshot reads no description and `aria-disabled` moves no snapshot reading, `enabled` still reading the `disabled` attribute), `state` (`NodeState { enabled, checked, value, selected, pressed, invalid, focused }` — seven fields, none for a list, the snapshot carrying no `expanded` node key and `NODE_FIELDS` keeping its thirteen keys; a struct literal without a spread names all seven), `bounds` (`BaseDocument::select_list_bounds(node)` first, a row's or a group's place in an open list, its select's client rect again once the list closes; else `get_client_bounding_rect` — viewport-relative, for every element, an option of a closed select, under an `optgroup` too, reading its select's client rect (the public, re-exported `closed_select_of`, called by the snapshot's builder and escher-driver's `lint.rs`, answering `None` for a select whose list is open, over the public, re-exported `is_multiple_select`, read within the workspace by `closed_select_of` alone, and `BaseDocument::select_of`; a box that is itself scrolled reads where it stands since 2026-10-10-scrolling-box-bounds-and-hit, the same before and after its content is scrolled) and `children`. A node is every element the accessibility tree keeps, generic containers included; `TextRun`s, the document root and the `Window` are not nodes. State is read from the element, since the tree gives an element no value: `enabled` follows the PRESENCE of `disabled` on an element that can be disabled (a `disabled="false"` and a bare `disabled` read `Some(false)` and, since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness, are not focusable either — the engine's focusability reader keys on presence too), `checked` is a native checkbox's or radio's own state, else, for a node whose tree role is one of the five checkable roles, `toggled == Toggled::True` — `None` where the role states nothing, a mixed one `Some(false)` (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), `value` is a `select`'s chosen option's value, a `multiple` select's first chosen option in tree order (`BaseDocument::select_value`, the reader taking the document and the node, no mask applying), else the editor's text, else — for a range `input`, since 2026-10-13-range-input-interaction — its current value `range_input_value()` (the formatted value a key or a pointerdown moved, while its `value` attribute keeps what the markup wrote), else the `value` attribute — and a password or file `input` — the public `is_masked_input(&ElementData) -> bool`, re-exported beside `MASKED_VALUE`, true for an `input` whose `type` reads `password` or `file` (ASCII case-insensitive), the test this reader calls and the one escher-driver's recorder reads to keep a masked `type` as its stand-in — reads the public constant `MASKED_VALUE` (eight U+2022) where it holds a non-empty value and `""` where that value is empty, never the text, its length or a file's host path (the DOM attribute and form submission still hold the path); `focused` is the tree's focus. No field holds a `NodeId`, tree id, `ElementId`, `ScopeId` or pointer; its one serialized form is the text below, which the driver's `snapshot` command returns (`stand_snapshot`, `stand_snapshot_state` — the selected and invalid readings each asserted equal to the accessibility node's — the flight type's chosen option, the selected CRUD row, a date field holding no date — the stand stating no `aria-pressed`, so `accessibility_states` pins the pressed reading on a fixture).

The driver's core (unpublished, no `[features]` of its own, no binary): a **session** — one headless app instance held by one process while commands arrive — the **command and refusal schema**, the one definition of what can be asked of the driver and of how it says no, the **executor** that runs a call on the held instance, since 2026-10-10-driver-cli the **command line** that carries a call out of the process, and since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface the **MCP server** that serves the twelve verbs as MCP tools over a caller's reader and writer (the `escher-session mcp` role), and since 2026-10-12-self-description the **self-description** (`describe`) that `help` answers on both surfaces, and since 2026-10-19-session-recording the **recording**: a session whose launcher names a recording directory keeps its answered calls at rest as one owner-only replayable check (`std` only, unix only like the socket), and since 2026-10-19-visual-lint the **visual lint** (`Session::lint` in process and the `lint` verb, the eighth instance verb, on every carrier (the socket's `call`, the command line, an MCP tool, `help`'s listing) and recorded — built by «Visual lint» (its gated part)), which reads the held screen and returns its layout and contrast defects as typed findings, which cross on the ratified carriers and rest in a kept check as the `lint` verb's answer — stable ids, the closed defect words and numbers, no page text, colour, control value or `NodeId` (a ratified boundary widening). It is app-agnostic: the caller supplies the boot and the time step, and the crate names no app and no stand type. `Session::run` validates a call, looks its target up on the screen, refuses a target that cannot take the action, runs its verb, settles the instance and returns a typed `Outcome` — for a call made in process, and for one a host decoded from its socket. A call and its answer cross the socket (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10), and an MCP client's stdio (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10, «Ратифицировать как есть»); since 2026-10-19-session-recording a recorded session's calls — the ids they named among them — rest in a kept check with its answers' digests and, since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay, each answer kept whole — its line as the driver wrote it, masked as on every carrier, a shot's without its pixels — so the screens' ids, names, values, snapshot text and diffs rest there too, never logged (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-19, F1 A · F2 B · F3 B); a kept check replays through `Session::run` alone (`Check::replay`), and the repository's own two scripted stand checks are committed in git, the one exception to owner-only. A settle verb on the socket is a later route entry.

- `std` only for the socket (`std::os::unix::net`), the spawn (`std::env::current_exe()` for the `start` command), the file modes, the host's idle clock and, since 2026-10-20-load-wait, the session's load wait (`std::time::Instant` and a sleep). No env read and no default state location; the schema is Rust data and every answer's JSON is written by hand in `json.rs` — `serde_json` reads MCP requests, since 2026-10-19-session-recording kept checks and, since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay, the live answer line a replay compares, and writes nothing. - `Session::act(step) -> Result<Settled, SessionError>` — runs the closure on the held instance, then settles it (`Harness::settle`) and, since 2026-10-20-load-wait, through the load wait (crate-private `settle_waiting`): while the answer is `NotSettled { busy: Busy::Loads }` it settles again every `LOAD_POLL` (10 ms, private) until the load is answered, a failed load answering it, or `LOAD_WAIT` (5 s of wall time, re-exported at the crate root) has passed, its last sleep the time left, then one more settle, while a `render` or `layout` answer returns at once; on `Ok` everything the step made due is on the screen; an instance that does not go quiet is `NotSettled(Busy)`, one still loading at the bound `NotSettled(Loads)`. The step is not rolled back, and no time is advanced — the wait reads `std::time::Instant` and sleeps, with no `tick`, `advance_time` or time step, no changed-set drain, no print and no `tracing` call. In process only. `Busy` and `Settled` are re-exported from blitz-test-harness. `Session::lint(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<Finding>, Refusal>` (since 2026-10-19-visual-lint; in process and, as the `lint` verb, the eighth instance verb, on every carrier (the socket's `call`, the command line, an MCP tool, `help`'s listing) and recorded — built by «Visual lint» (its gated part)) reads the held instance's current screen and returns one `Finding { id, defect, bounds, reason }` per defect it reads, in document order, then `Defect::ALL` order: it refuses `fonts-unavailable` before anything is read when `can_paint_text` reads false, reads `harness.doc.snapshot()`, recording each node's id in the session's record of ids as `snapshot` does, and runs no step, settle, pump or time move, so it changes nothing. `Defect` is closed at six (`overlap` · `clipped` · `truncated` · `off-screen` · `zero-size` · `contrast`), `Reason` holds the measured reason (`Overlap { other, area }` · `Clipped { visible }` · `Truncated { text, visible: Option<Bounds> }` · `OffScreen` · `ZeroSize` · `Contrast { ratio, required }`), and every rectangle is the lint's own `Bounds { x, y, width, height: f64 }` in the snapshot bounds' space, the crate naming neither blitz-dom nor stylo; the four types derive `Debug`, `Clone` and `PartialEq` and hold no `NodeId`, page text, colour or value. Each node's clip region is `visible_region` cut by the padding box of every DOM ancestor below the root whose computed `contain` includes `paint`, `clip_region` taking an open row's region from `visible_region` alone, with no `contain: paint` cut; `overlap` leaves out a closed select's options and an open list's rows and groups — `Entry.in_select_box` reads a closed select's option through `closed_select_of`, by the element and never the role, so CRUD's `role="option"` rows are not read as a select's, and is true also for an open list's row or group, and `overlaps` skips such an entry on either side, a `multiple` select's rows linted as usual; `truncated` reads blitz-dom's `BaseDocument::text_extent` (its one non-test caller) on a node that is no text control, and `contrast` `Harness::text_contrast` below `required_ratio()`, exempt at `enabled == Some(false)`, `None` not measured, a node past an element on the walk with a `mix-blend-mode` other than `normal` among them. The `lint` verb carries it — `Command::Lint`, `Outcome::Linted`, the `{"findings":[…]}` written form, an MCP tool and a recorded step, its answer kept whole — its `command` span recording `verb` and, refused, `cause` alone, no field added, and `VERBS` holds twelve.

- `Session::run(&Call) -> Result<Outcome, Refusal>` — the one entry point that runs a call. `validate` first: a refused call has run nothing, and a session-level verb (`start`, `status`, `stop`) is refused `unknown-verb`. Then per verb: `snapshot` reads the screen once and dispatches nothing — with no `part` and a text of at most `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` bytes it returns `Snapshot::to_text`'s text as `Outcome::Screen`, otherwise (since 2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts) it cuts `text_parts(SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET)` and returns part `n` — `part`, or 1 when absent — as `Outcome::Part` with the count `parts`, a part past the last the empty text with the same `parts`; `click`, `type`, `scroll` and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, a `screenshot` given an `id` look their id up on the screen as it reads NOW (the snapshot lists it, and the first `element_ids()` pair with it resolves through `get_node`) — an id that names no element there is refused with nothing run, `stale` when the session's record of ids read holds it, `not-found` when not. A `click` or a `type` on an element that cannot take it is then refused, one answer in a fixed order: `disabled` (the snapshot reads `enabled: Some(false)`), `off-screen` (the centre of its `bounds` is outside `BaseDocument::visible_region` — the viewport and every scrolling box that holds it, a row or a group of an open select list reading the list's scrollport in place of its clipping boxes; under a rotation a box's visible part reads as the bounding box of its rotated padding box, so an element in a corner it does not show can read in view, a measured limit `off-screen`'s meaning states), `covered` (the hit at that page point never reaches it, where a select list stands open a hit answering the list first, so a button under the list reads `covered`; an option of a closed single select is not clicked — a `click` on one is refused `covered`, under a group too, while a `click` on a `multiple` select's row is accepted and chooses it, a `click` on a single select opens its list or closes one standing, as `click`'s help says of a select, and a `click` on an open list's row chooses it). Otherwise they click the centre of the element's snapshot `bounds` plus the viewport's scroll, but for a `type` on a select, single or `multiple` (`Target` carries `select`), which does not click, a click landing on a `multiple` select's row at the centre and opening a single select's list: the crate-private `focus_select` focuses it with no click, so `type` fires no DOM focus events on a single select, clears the typeahead (`BaseDocument::clear_select_typeahead`, its one non-test caller), without which a second `type` joins the first's text, and closes any list (`BaseDocument::close_select_list`), and a text opening on a space types nothing on any select, since no label can match and on a `multiple` select the Space would flip a row — two `click`s on one point with no `advance` of at least 500 ms between them read as a double click, as `click`'s help says (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); `type` then replaces what the control holds — where the snapshot reads a `value` for the target (an empty text input reads one) it presses the engine's select-all (`a` with Control, Super on macOS) and types, and with an empty text deletes the selection, so an empty text clears; on a select the text is the engine's typeahead, choosing the first option whose label starts with it and, on a `multiple` select, its match alone, as `type`'s help says; `press` presses its key on what holds focus (shift when asked; it carries no Ctrl, so a set of rows of a `multiple` select that are not adjacent cannot be built through the driver, as its help states) — since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness a pressed `enter`, or a `space`, on a focused button with no `disabled` attribute dispatches its click (the engine's keyboard activation, [Scrolling and input]), and on a focused single select with its list closed a pressed `enter`, or a `space` with no typed text standing, opens its list, whose keys then move the highlight, choose and close, `press`'s help stating the keys on a closed select; `advance` moves the harness's clock by exactly its milliseconds (`Harness::advance_time`) inside one settled step on every session — the engine's animations, the overlay scrollbar fade and the app's own time together — then hands them to the session's time step where one was handed (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); `scroll` applies none of the three checks, scrolls every scrolling box that holds the element and then the viewport, at once (`Harness::scroll_into_view`), a row of an open select list writing that list's `scroll_y` alone, and answers `in_view` — false when no scroll could bring it into view; it is never refused for that; `screenshot` (since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot) dispatches nothing and is no step — with no `id` it returns the whole screen, with an `id` it crops the frame to the part of the element's bounds that can be seen, rounded outward to whole pixels, a crop of no pixel refused `off-screen`; an app whose font context resolves no `sans-serif` family (`BaseDocument::can_paint_text` false) is refused `fonts-unavailable` with nothing painted; the frame is the harness's `screenshot`, written as a PNG by the private `image::png`, and a shot changes nothing (`has_changes` stays false, focus and the next snapshot unchanged); `lint` (since 2026-10-19-visual-lint) takes no argument and its arm calls `Session::lint`, so a lint dispatches nothing, runs no step and settles nothing, answering its findings. Each acting verb is one settled step: snapshot, step, the load wait over `Harness::settle`, snapshot, diff — so since 2026-10-20-load-wait the five acting verbs wait on a load in flight, for at most `LOAD_WAIT`, on every carrier (in process, the socket, the command line and MCP), while `snapshot`, `screenshot` and `lint`, which run no step, wait on nothing. A refused call leaves the snapshot and both focus readings as they were.

- `Outcome` — `Screen { text }` · `Part { text, part, parts }` (since 2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts) · `Acted { settled, busy, diff }` · `Advanced { settled, busy, diff, advanced_ms }` · `Scrolled { settled, busy, diff, in_view }` · `Shot { width, height, png }` (since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot) · `Linted { findings: Vec<Finding> }` (since 2026-10-19-visual-lint); `diff` is dioxus-native-dom's `SnapshotDiff`, unchanged. An instance that did not go quiet is a result (`settled: false` with its `Busy` class), never a refusal and never a `SessionError`; the step is not rolled back. `advanced_ms` is exactly the `ms` asked: the clock's move, not what a counter inside the app gained, and a step's diff can be non-empty on any animated page (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18).

- Written forms — `Outcome::to_json`, `Refusal::to_json`, `SessionError::to_json`: one line of JSON each, keyed by the schema's own words, output only. An outcome is an object keyed by its verb's result fields in the table's order (`busy` only when not settled); a node is keyed by `NODE_FIELDS` in order — thirteen keys: `id` · `parent` · `role` · `name` · `enabled` · `checked` · `value` · `selected` · `pressed` · `invalid` · `focused` · `bounds` · `differs` (since 2026-10-12-self-description; written on a changed node only, after `bounds`: the node-key words whose reading differs from before the step, a node that only moved reading `bounds` alone, an added node written without it) — with `parent`, `enabled`, `checked`, `value`, `selected` and `pressed` left out when absent, `invalid` always written, `bounds` four numbers; a refusal is `{"refused":{"cause","meaning","remedy"[,"fault"]}}`; a session error `{"error":{"kind","message","remedy"}}` (the remedy since 2026-10-12-self-description); a `screenshot`'s outcome `{"width":…,"height":…,"png":"<base64>"}` (since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot), the PNG's base64 written by hand in the private `image::base64` (RFC 4648 §4, padded) — no base64 crate taken; a `lint`'s outcome `{"findings":[…]}`, each finding keyed `id` · `defect` · `bounds` (`[x, y, width, height]`, as a node's bounds), then its reason's keys — `other` and `area` for an overlap, `visible` for a clip, `text` then `visible` (left out when no part can be seen) for a truncation, `ratio` (its shortest decimal, `null` when not finite) and `required` for contrast, none for off-screen and zero-size; a paged `snapshot`'s outcome `{"text":…,"part":n,"parts":m}`, a whole screen's still `{"text":…}` alone; `start` answers `label`, `pid`, `idle_expiry_s`, `status` adds `served`, `stop` answers `{"stopped":true}`.

- `serve(state_dir, session, idle_expiry)` — hosts one session until a `stop` request or until no request has been answered for `idle_expiry` (`IDLE_EXPIRY`, 1,800 s, is what a command line's host serves under), on the calling thread (the instance is not `Send`): creates the state directory `0700` (a present one open to group or others is `StateDirNotPrivate`), binds `session.sock` and sets it `0600`, replaces a socket nothing answers on, reads `AlreadyRunning` when one answers, runs a `call` request through `Session::run` and nothing else, and at the end drops the session and removes the socket file and the directory — non-recursively, nothing else.

- `start(state_dir, host, ready)` → `Started { child, hello }` · `attach(state_dir)` → `Hello { pid, label, served, idle_expiry_s }` · `stop(state_dir)` (waits up to 5 s for the directory to go) · `call(state_dir, &Call)` → `Answer { accepted, json }` — it validates first, so a call the schema refuses is answered there and reaches no session; the answer is read under 30 s per read (`Timeout` past it; pinned since 2026-10-14-quality-gates by the unix-only unit test `client::imp::tests::an_answer_read_past_its_bound_is_a_timeout`, which reads the bound equal to `wire::ANSWER_BOUND` and a read past a shortened bound on a listener that never answers as `Timeout`).

- `SessionError`, fifteen: `AlreadyRunning` · `NoSession` · `Dead` · `HostExited(code)` · `Timeout` · `Protocol` · `InvalidLabel` · `StateDirTooLong` · `StateDirNotPrivate` · `Unsupported` · `Io(kind)` · `NotSettled(Busy)` · `AnswerTooLarge` (a call's answer over the socket's bound — the call ran) · `RecordDirNotPrivate` (a recording directory open to its group or others) · `RecordingFailed` (a recording that ended, read from an `ok v3 recording-failed` reply; both since 2026-10-19-session-recording) — fixed messages (`Io` and `NotSettled` append a kind or class name), never a path, label, id or value; `kind()` is one fixed kebab-case word per variant and, since 2026-10-12-self-description, `remedy()` a fixed remedy: each variant's kind, meaning and remedy are one row of the crate-private `SESSION_ERRORS: [ErrorSpec; 15]` (`ErrorSpec { kind, meaning, remedy, repeats }`, `repeats` not served), which `kind()`, `remedy()` and `Display` read; `dead` repeats `no-session`'s remedy and `answer-too-large` `not-settled`'s; `StateDirTooLong`'s message states its bound as a figure — at most 94 bytes as given on Linux, 90 on every other target — and its remedy is a shorter path for the state directory, or a relative one.

- `VERBS` — the verb table, twelve verbs in three levels (`Level::Instance` · `Level::Session` · `Level::Tool`, the third since 2026-10-12-self-description): `snapshot` (one optional `part`; result `text`, then `part` and `parts`, two counts written only when the screen is read in parts), `click` (`id`), `type` (`id`, `text`), `press` (`key`, optional `shift`), `advance` (`ms`), `scroll` (`id`; the sixth, ratified by the founder, 2026-10-07), `screenshot` (one optional `id`; result `width` (count), `height` (count) and `png` (`FieldKind::Png`, base64 text), all always present; the seventh, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, its help stating one measured limit — an element shot is cropped to the part of its bounds that can be seen — the overlay scrollbar fade reading the session's clock, so two shots of one state with no `advance` between them read the same pixels (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18)), `lint` (the eighth, since 2026-10-19-visual-lint: no argument, one named refused `malformed` with `Fault::Unnamed`; result `findings`, `FieldKind::Entries`, always present; its help stating the six defect words, each reason's keys and its limits — geometry only, no hit, right-to-left and vertical text read as left-to-right lines), then `start` (`app`), `status` and `stop` (session-level; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10), then `help` (tool-level, no argument; result `verbs` · `node_keys` · `key_names` · `busy_classes` · `causes` · `exit_statuses` · `session_errors`, each field with its help; since 2026-10-12-self-description, ratified by the founder, 2026-10-12); each a `VerbSpec { name, level, help, args, fields }`; `verb(name)` finds one by its exact name only. Argument kinds and bounds (`ArgKind`): `id` 1 to `MAX_ID_BYTES` (1024) bytes of text · `text` 0 to `MAX_TEXT_BYTES` (4096) bytes · `key` one of the twelve `KEY_NAMES` · `flag` · `milliseconds` 1 to `MAX_MILLISECONDS` (60000) · `name` 1 to 32 bytes of `a-z`, `0-9`, `-` · `part` a whole number 1 to `MAX_PART` (1000), `snapshot`'s, the seventh kind. The acting verbs' result: `settled` (its help stating the load wait's bound, «a load in flight waited for up to 5 s», since 2026-10-20-load-wait), `busy` (one of `BUSY_CLASSES`, only when not settled), `added`, `removed`, `changed` (nodes carry the `NODE_FIELDS`); `advance` adds `advanced_ms`, `scroll` adds `in_view` (always present); `help`'s fields are of the kinds `Words` · `Entries`, and `screenshot`'s `png` of `Png` (base64 text, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot) — ten `FieldKind`s. Since 2026-10-12-self-description the command line's four exit statuses are the schema's `EXIT_STATUSES: [ExitStatus; 4]` (`ExitStatus { status, name, meaning }`: `0` `accepted` · `1` `refused` · `2` `usage` · `3` `session-error`), which the command line's status constants read and `help` serves, and `describe() -> String` writes the tool's self-description, `help`'s answer, as one line of JSON from the tables alone — 12 verbs, 13 node keys, 12 key names, 3 busy classes, 8 causes and 15 session errors with their remedies (13 until 2026-10-19-session-recording), 4 exit statuses — reading no environment and printing nothing; the command line's `help` and the MCP `help` tool serve the same bytes. The help of `changed` and of `snapshot`'s `text` say the state words and the two limits of the boolean model — a mixed toggle reads unpressed (`pressed` false), a grammar or spelling error reads invalid — so an agent learns them from the tool; since 2026-10-12-self-description `NODE_FIELDS` is `[NodeFieldSpec; 13]`, each row `NodeFieldSpec { name, help }` whose help states the key's reading — `checked` a native checkbox's or radio's own state, else the toggle of the five checkable roles (`aria-checked`), a mixed one reading false, `selected` · `pressed` · `invalid` read by `aria-selected` · `aria-pressed` (left out for those five roles) · `aria-invalid`, the two limits among them — and the crate docs' one sentence says each limit is stated in its node key's help and that a changed node names the keys whose reading differs (`differs`).

- `validate(call: &Call) -> Result<Command, Refusal>` — a `Call` is a verb name and named `ArgValue`s (`Text` · `Number` · `Flag`); it receives no `Session`, so a refused call changes nothing. One answer per call, the first failure in this order: the verb by exact name (`unknown-verb`; a session-level verb and, since 2026-10-12-self-description, the tool-level `help` too), then the call's arguments in the order passed (a name the verb lacks, a name passed twice), then the verb's arguments in the schema's order (missing, wrong kind, outside its bound) — the last five are `malformed` with a `Fault` naming the rule. `Command` is `Snapshot { part: Option<u32> }` (a `part` admitted in `1..=MAX_PART` through `u32::try_from`, any other number `OutOfBound`, a text or a flag `WrongKind`) · `Click` · `Type` · `Press` · `Advance` · `Scroll` · `Screenshot { id: Option<String> }` (since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot) · `Lint` (validated from `("lint", [])`, since 2026-10-19-visual-lint), and `Command::spec()` is its verb's row. `validate_session(&Call) -> Result<SessionCommand, Refusal>` is the same check over the three session-level rows and, since 2026-10-12-self-description, the tool-level `help` — an instance-level verb `unknown-verb` there, an argument to `help` `malformed` with `Fault::Unnamed` (`SessionCommand`: `Start { app }` · `Status` · `Stop` · `Help`, `Help`'s spec `HELP`).

- `Refusal` — a `Cause` and, only beside `malformed`, a `Fault`. `CAUSES` is closed at eight (`[Cause; 8]`, ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18): `unknown-verb` · `malformed` · `not-found` · `stale` · `disabled` · `covered` · `off-screen` · `fonts-unavailable` (the eighth, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot: meaning "the app this session holds has no font it can paint text with", remedy "boot the app with a font it can decode"), each with a fixed `name()`, `meaning()` and `remedy()`. None of `Cause`, `Fault`, `Refusal` has a `String` field: a refusal holds nothing a call supplied. All eight are returned today — `unknown-verb` and `malformed` by `validate`, the other six by the executor, `fonts-unavailable` from `screenshot` and `lint` among the verbs — a shot checked before anything is painted, a lint, and `Session::lint` in process, before anything is read. On the stand a click is accepted on 68 of the 77 snapshot nodes at boot and refused on 9: the three disabled controls, each task's `task-header-spacer` as `covered` (a box 0 high; the hit at its centre answers the header), and the flight booker's two options `flight-type-one-way` · `flight-type-return` as `covered`, each read at its select's client rect.

- `serve_mcp(input, output, apps, boot, idle_expiry) -> Result<(), SessionError>` (since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface) — newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 in the handshake revisions `2025-11-25` · `2025-06-18` · `2025-03-26` · `2024-11-05` (`PROTOCOL_VERSIONS`; the first since 2026-10-12-self-description) on the `BufRead` and `Write` it is handed, holding at most one session in its own process. `initialize` answers the asked revision when it is one of the four, else `LATEST_VERSION`, `2025-11-25` (until 2026-10-12-self-description one of three, else `2025-06-18`; the current revision `2026-07-28` is answered so and not taken up, the founder's ruling of 2026-10-12) (`capabilities {"tools":{}}`, `serverInfo {name: "escher", version}`); `ping` → `{}`; `tools/list` → the twelve verbs of `VERBS` in order (`screenshot` after `scroll`, then `lint`), `help` last, each with a `description` — its help, then, since 2026-10-12-self-description, `. Returns: ` and each result field as `{name} ({kind}): {help}` joined by `; ` (the listing 2,984 → 8,844 bytes) — and an `inputSchema` (`additionalProperties: false`, `start`'s `app` an `enum` of the apps, `snapshot`'s `part` an `integer` from 1 to 1000); `tools/call`; any other method, `server/discover` included, `-32601`; a request with no `id` is a notification — no reply, nothing runs. Bounds (ratified with the crossing): a request line ≤ 65,536 bytes (longer → read to its end, dropped, `-32700`), an `id` echoed only as an i64 or a string ≤ 128 bytes (else `-32600`, `id: null`), a result's text ≤ 1,048,576 bytes (past it `AnswerTooLarge`'s result) — since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot a result that holds an image bounded by its whole written form instead, a text-only result by its text as before (`ToolResult::bounded`). Protocol errors: a fixed code and message, no `data`. A tool call's arguments become a `Call` (string → text, i64 → number, bool → flag, any other refused `malformed`; members in key order, so a repeated key collapses to its last value); an instance verb runs through `Session::run` on the held session (none held: validated first, else `no-session`); `start` (an app outside `apps` refused `malformed`; `AlreadyRunning` when held), `status`, `stop` and, since 2026-10-12-self-description, `help` are answered by the server — `help` held session or not, its text `describe()`'s line, accepted, and counted in a held session's `served` as every tool call is. A result is `{content:[…], isError}` — an accepted `snapshot` one text block, the screen text itself for a whole screen and its JSON line `{"text","part","parts"}` for a paged one — the screen text's quotes escaped inside that line, so a reader decodes the line before it matches the screen's own text; since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot an accepted `screenshot` two blocks, an `image` block (`data` the PNG's base64, `mimeType` `image/png`) then a text block holding the shot's line without `png` (private `json::shot_without_image`), `isError` false; any other accepted call one text block, its JSON line; a refusal, a refused shot included, or a session error one text block, its JSON with `isError: true`; no `structuredContent`. Since 2026-10-19-session-recording a call after which the session's recording ended is answered `ToolResult::failed(SessionError::RecordingFailed)` (`isError`), its `tool_call` span keeping `tool` and `ending` and `serve_mcp` its signature. The idle expiry is checked when a request arrives — no timer, no thread. Since 2026-10-16-file-splits the `mcp` module has three private children, each widened to `pub(super)` and no further — `framing` (the request reader, the id, the protocol errors and the reply writers), `listing` (the handshake and the tool listing) and `result` (a tool call's result and its written form; since 2026-10-19-session-recording its arguments are read into a call by `command`'s crate-private `call_of`, the builder a kept check's reader shares) — and its tests in `mcp_tests.rs`.

- `command_line(args, apps, boot) -> ExitCode` — the whole command line of a binary that boots apps (`boot` an `FnMut` since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface); it installs no subscriber and reads no environment variable. The reader's rules, in order: no first word → usage; `serve <app> --session <dir>` in exactly that shape or with one `--record <dir>` after it, else usage; `mcp` alone or with one `--record <dir>`, else usage (since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface; `--record` since 2026-10-19-session-recording); a `--record` anywhere else, twice or with no value is usage once the call passed `validate`; `help` with no argument and at most one `--session <dir>`, which is not read, answers `describe()`'s line on stdout, status `0`, reaching no session — `help` with an argument is refused `malformed`, `1`, and `--session` with no directory or given twice is usage, `2` (since 2026-10-12-self-description); a first word the verb table does not hold → the refusal `unknown-verb`; the call the remaining words spell (flags as the schema spells them — `--id`, `--text`, `--key`, `--ms` and `--part` each with one value, `--ms`'s and `--part`'s read as a number, `--shift` bare; `start`'s app as one plain word) is checked by `validate` or `validate_session` before the session address is asked for; then `--session <dir>` exactly once, else usage; `start` on an app the binary does not boot → usage. Four endings: accepted — the answer on stdout, status `0`; refused — the refusal on stdout, `1`; usage — one fixed line on stderr built from `VERBS` and the app names, `2`; session error — the error object on stdout and its message on stderr, `3`; the host role ends quiet, status `0`; the `mcp` role hands stdin and stdout to `serve_mcp` with `IDLE_EXPIRY` and writes nothing on stdout at its end — `0` on `Ok`, `3` with the error's fixed message on stderr on `Err` — and the usage line names it (`; mcp role: mcp [--record <dir>]`), with `snapshot [--part <part>]`, `start <app> [--record <dir>]` and `host role: serve <app> --session <dir> [--record <dir>]`; `start --record` and `mcp --record` check the recording directory first, a refusal ending status `3` with nothing spawned or served. No command's ending writes back anything the caller typed. `start` spawns the running binary again as `serve <app> --session <dir>`, with `--record <dir>` after it when it was given one, its streams closed, waits up to 30 s for it to answer, and neither kills nor reaps it.

- Consumed by seven_guis (the `escher-session` binary, native target only — its `main` hands argv, the six served slugs `counter` · `flight-booker` · `timer` · `crud` · `cells` · `load` (one private `TASKS` table, from which the usage line's apps and the MCP `start` tool's `enum` are written) and the stand's boot to `command_line`, the Timer's session carrying the stand's time step) and by blitz-tests (dev-dependency), whose sixteen `stand_act_*` checks drive the schema through `Session::run`; since 2026-10-15-cold-agent-test the binary's `mcp` role is also the cold-agent pipe's MCP server (`bash scripts/cold-agent.sh run stand`: one isolated `claude -p` session allowed `mcp__escher` alone, the live server child run as `mcp --record` into the owner-only `target/cold-agent/record/` over the six served apps, the agent's JSON check replayed on fresh `escher-session mcp` children without `--record`), a `run` precondition the operator builds, never the pipe.

- The wire (`wire.rs`, crate-private, versioned `v3`, `v2` until 2026-10-19-session-recording) is one request line and one reply line per connection: `hello v3` → `ok v3 pid= label= served= idle_expiry_s=`, `stop v3` → `ok v3 stopping`, `call v3 <verb> [<name>=<kind>:<value>]…` → `ok v3 accepted <json>` · `ok v3 refused <json>` · `ok v3 oversize` · `ok v3 recording-failed` (sent in place of the answer when the host's recording ended after the call, the client reading it as `RecordingFailed`), another version of a known word → `refused version`, anything else → `refused malformed`. Kinds are `t` text · `n` whole number · `f` flag; the verb, the names and a text value are percent-escaped byte for byte and decoded strictly. A request is bounded at 16,384 bytes, a lifecycle reply at 128, an answer at 1,048,576 on its JSON line; each read and write at 2 s, a client's read of an answer at 30 s. **What the screen reads crosses it in an answer** — ids, accessible names, control values (a password's or a file input's as the mask), the snapshot's text and the diff — and an element id and typed text cross in (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10); no `NodeId` crosses. Inside the text and the diff an element that states one also reads selected, pressed or invalid — closed words in the text, booleans in a diff node, never an attribute's value as typed: an inventory fact of the ratified crossing, not a further widening (the founder, 2026-10-10), who set the rule with it — a new field of a closed value set inside an already ratified carrier is not a widening; authored text, an open value set, a new carrier or a new exit still is. The MCP surface was that next crossing question: since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface the same content crosses to an MCP client in tool results over the `mcp` role's stdio, the request-id echo and the bounds above ratified by the founder with it (2026-10-10, «Ратифицировать как есть»); the next surface that carries any of it is a new crossing question — since 2026-10-15-cold-agent-test the operator-driven live cold-agent run carries the stand's screen (element ids, accessible names and control values in snapshot texts and diffs, from this MCP server) on to the model provider, one run, on the founder's «Один запуск, до $3 (Рекомендую)» and «JSON-проверка с повтором (Рекомендую)» (2026-10-15). Since 2026-10-12-self-description the command line's stdout and the `mcp` role's stdio also carry the program's own fixed text, held as `'static` data of the one table — the `help` self-description, a session error's remedy and each tool's description with its result fields — riding those ratified carriers, and a changed node's `differs` crosses as a closed set by the rule of 2026-10-10 (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-12); text from a page, a call or a screen, a new carrier or a new exit still widens. Since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot a shot's pixels cross in band on those carriers — its PNG as base64 inside the answer on the session socket and the command line's stdout, and as an MCP `image` block on the `mcp` role's stdio — screen content and no closed value set, with no new carrier, exit or path argument and the 1,048,576-byte bounds unchanged, a bigger image ending `oversize` / `AnswerTooLarge`: a boundary widening ratified by the founder (2026-10-12). Since 2026-10-19-visual-lint a lint's findings cross on those carriers and rest in a kept check as the `lint` verb's answer — stable ids, the closed defect words and numbers, no page text, colour, control value or `NodeId` — with no new carrier, exit, path argument, cause, session error, span field or dependency: a ratified boundary widening; since 2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts a screen over the snapshot budget crosses them in parts — `snapshot`'s optional `part` (a whole number, 1 to `MAX_PART` = 1000) in, one part's text with the closed counts `part` and `parts` out, a part past the last the empty text, a screen within the budget answering whole as before, over MCP a paged answer its JSON line — with no new verb, carrier, exit, cause, session error, span field or dependency: a ratified boundary widening. Since 2026-10-31-select-popup the select list crosses the ratified carriers only as a row's own `bounds` in the snapshot and the diff — `differs` naming `bounds`, a closed set inside the ratified crossing — and as pixels in a `screenshot`, with no new carrier, exit, cause, session error, node key, log field or span; an option's and a group's label leaving as pixels in every shot of an open list is a boundary widening, ratified.

- `served` counts every request answered, refusals included, and each one starts the idle count again — an `attach` or a `status` keeps a host alive; a refusal or a broken connection changes nothing; a `stop` takes effect once its reply is written; an `oversize` reply is no refusal — the call ran.

- Unix only: on other targets `serve`, `start`, `attach`, `stop` and `call` return `Unsupported`, and so does `Session::recording_into`; a `Session` held in process without a recording works everywhere — `run` included. The schema's three modules (`command`, `refusal`, `schema`) carry no `cfg` gate; `execute` carries two macOS ones, the backward-delete arm of `press` and the select-all's modifier. Since 2026-10-16-file-splits `schema` holds its six shape types `ArgKind`, `ArgSpec`, `FieldKind`, `FieldSpec`, `Level` and `VerbSpec` in its private child `spec`, re-exported, and its tests in `schema_tests.rs`.

- The schema is the one table every surface reads — the actions, the span's cause field, the command line and its usage line, the MCP tools, the self-description: a later entry ADDS its verbs to `VERBS` at its own promotion, never states a second table — and the CI-script pin `test_capability_statement.py` (the `ci-scripts` leg) reads the verb names from `VERBS`, the cause names from `Cause::name`'s match arms (`refusal.rs`) and the lengths of `SESSION_ERRORS` (`error.rs`), `NODE_FIELDS` and `EXIT_STATUSES`, holding `docs/capabilities.md` (every verb and cause a code span, the five counts stated in words) and README.md («the {word} driver commands as tools») to those tables. A cause's texts are fixed and reworded only with a recorded reason; three of the tool's own texts say measured limits — `covered`'s meaning, which also says an option of a closed select lies under it and to click the select first, then the option, two readings — a box clipped on one axis stopping a hit at its whole padding box, so an element lying outside it along the axis it does not clip can read `covered` though it shows, and a box with no width or no height hit at its centre on the element that holds it, so it can read `covered` though nothing covers it; `off-screen`'s meaning, one — under a rotation a box's visible part reads as the bounding box of its rotated padding box, so an element in a corner it does not show can read in view; and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, `screenshot`'s help, one: an element shot is cropped to the part of its bounds that can be seen — the overlay scrollbar fade reading the session's clock, so two shots of one state with no `advance` between them read the same pixels (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); the help of `changed` and of `snapshot`'s `text` state none since 2026-10-10-scrolling-box-bounds-and-hit, which fixed the two limits they named.

- No panic path on anything a call or a command line supplies: no `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!`, `unreachable!` or index in `validate`, in the executor or in the argv reader; the executor never calls `Harness::layout_rect_of`, which panics on a node that does not resolve; a write to a closed pipe is dropped, not a panic — pinned since 2026-10-14-quality-gates by `cli_commands`' `a_closed_stdout_drops_the_answer_and_keeps_the_ending` (with its stdout's read end closed, `help` exits 0 and `snapshot` with no session 3, neither printing a panic). Fixed in the engine since 2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph: a key press with focus on a control whose anonymous block was dropped does not panic, for `hidden`, `style="display:none"` and CSS alone; focus stays and the key still acts (`BaseDocument::deallocate_anonymous_block` setting `layout_parent` to `None` on each child still naming the block).

- No `NodeId` outlives a call, and no field of `Session`, `Outcome` or `Refusal` holds one. The one thing of its screens the session keeps between calls is a record of the ids they have read, to tell `stale` from `not-found` (beside it, since 2026-10-19-session-recording, only the optional crate-private recording `recording_into` sets, which keeps calls, their answers' digests and, since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay, each answer whole, a shot's pixels excepted): id text only, in a crate-private `SeenIds` bounded at `MAX_SEEN_IDS` (4096 ids — a count, not the 4096 bytes of `MAX_TEXT_BYTES`), least recently read forgotten first, an id longer than `MAX_ID_BYTES` not recorded, fed from the session's own snapshots — every snapshot a call takes once `validate` has admitted it and, since 2026-10-19-visual-lint, the one `Session::lint` reads — in process or through the `lint` verb — which takes no argument, with no public reader; never print, log or field it. No step reads or drains the changed set — the diff is two snapshots and `Snapshot::diff`.

- Settling moves no time: time on a held instance moves only by `advance`, which moves the session's clock on every session and, through the caller's step where one was handed, the app's own time (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); since 2026-10-20-load-wait an acting driver command waits on a load in flight for at most `LOAD_WAIT`, the bound the `settled` field's help states, and `snapshot`, `screenshot` and `lint` wait on none — so a kept check whose app meets a load can read `settled` differently on a replay whose load lands at another time (recorded, not established); the two committed Counter checks meet no load.

- What a command prints is its answer, never a log line: an `Outcome` is written by `to_json` alone — as a command's answer, and as an MCP tool result's text; an accepted `screenshot` over MCP as an `image` block and its line without `png` (`json::shot_without_image`), since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot — and nothing of it goes into a span or a log field.

- A Unix socket address leaves about a hundred bytes for the whole path (108 on Linux, 104 on macOS): keep a state directory's name short — a long scratch path cannot hold a session; an over-long one is `StateDirTooLong` (status `3`), whose message states the bound — at most 94 bytes as given on Linux, 90 on every other target — and whose remedy is a shorter path, or a relative one, which counts only its own bytes.
- A host ends by itself after its idle expiry, exactly as on `stop`. A watcher that polls `attach` or `status` restarts the count and keeps the host alive: watch the state directory instead.
- `start` does not check that the answering pid is the child it spawned.
- The `Io` message is spelled "input or output" — "I/O" holds a `/`, and the messages are asserted to hold none.

- A test's working directory is its package: build a check's state directory from `env!("CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR")`, never from a relative path. Since 2026-10-19-session-recording escher-driver's unit tests reach the workspace `target/tmp` through the compile-time `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")`; the other exception, since 2026-10-14-quality-gates, is the unix-only client unit test `client::imp::tests::an_answer_read_past_its_bound_is_a_timeout`: it binds a test-only `UnixListener` in `eab-{pid}` under the system temporary directory (`std::env::temp_dir()`, reading `TMPDIR` on unix — test code only), a short name so the socket's path fits, accepts one connection, never answers and removes the directory; no binary serves it and no caller reaches it, so it is no crossing (the operator, 2026-10-15).
- Two `Command`s meet at the crate root: the schema's `Command`, and the `std::process::Command` that `start` takes. A grep for `Command` over the crate reads both.

- `Command`, `Call` and `ArgValue` derive `Debug`, which prints the id and the typed text they hold, and `Outcome` derives it too, printing the ids, accessible names, control values and state readings of its diff: never field one with `?` in a span or a log, and never field an argument by its schema name (of the names only `text` is in the sink's scrub set).

- The command span: every call handed to `Session::run` leaves one `tracing` span — target `escher_driver`, name `command`, INFO, built by hand with `tracing::info_span!` (no `#[instrument]`), entered before `validate` and held until `run` returns. Its eight fields are each created unrecorded and recorded only where they apply: `verb` (the verb table's own word, never the caller's text — a session-level verb's and, since 2026-10-12-self-description, the tool-level `help`'s too, beside `unknown-verb`), `cause` (`Cause::name()` of the returned refusal), `settled`, `busy` (the schema's busy-class word), `passes` (on a step the load wait settled again, the passes of the settle that went quiet), and `added` · `removed` · `changed` (the lengths of the returned diff). `snapshot` and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, an accepted `screenshot` record `verb` alone, as do an accepted `lint` and a part read; a refused call `verb` and `cause` only. Never fielded: `in_view`, `advanced_ms`, the screen text or its length, a part's number, the part count, a shot's image, its size or its dimensions, a lint's findings or their count, the label, the record of ids, the recording, its directory or its kept check (since 2026-10-19-session-recording), any argument, any `Command`, `Call`, `ArgValue`, `Outcome`, `Refusal` or `Fault`. The crate installs no subscriber: with none the span is disabled; under escher's sink it is one line per call at `info` or below, none at the default `warn` — an `escher-session` host writes it for every hosted call. A call the schema refuses on the command line or in `client::call` reaches no session and opens no span; an idle expiry writes no record.

- The `tool_call` span (since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface; the founder, 2026-10-10, «Span с tool и ending»): one per MCP `tools/call` request, target `escher_driver`, INFO, opened and entered before its params are read and held until its reply is written; two fields only — `tool` (the table's word, unrecorded for an unknown tool) and `ending` (`accepted` · `refused` · `error`); the `command` span of an instance verb is its child by nesting, while `start` · `status` · `stop` and, since 2026-10-12-self-description, `help` leave a `tool_call` with no child. `serve_mcp` itself and the rest of its protocol write no record. A check that installs a scoped subscriber with `with_default` reads no span when another test thread reached the same callsites with no subscriber first (`tracing`'s callsite interest is process-global): give each test its own recorder.

- In `command.rs` an assertion over a call carries a row index only (`assert!(a == b, "row {row}")`), never `assert_eq!` on a call or a command — a failing leg's log is uploaded as a CI artifact. The `stand_act_*` checks keep the same rule: a message names a layout mode, a task and an index.

- Fixed in the engine at 2026-10-10-scrolling-box-bounds-and-hit: a box that is itself scrolled reads its `bounds` where it stands — a step that scrolls it does not name it among the changed nodes, and a `click` or a `type` naming the box lands at its centre (`stand_act_scroll`).

- Fixed in the engine (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18): a hit stops at the padding box of a box paint clips — by `overflow` or by a computed `contain` that includes `paint` — so content clipped by `contain: paint` no longer reads `covered`.
