escher's telemetry bootstrap (unpublished, no `[features]`): one process-global stderr `tracing` subscriber that stamps the service identity on every line, applies a target allowlist in its formatter — it scrubs the records of engine and escher targets and drops every other target's — bridges `log` records and chains a panic hook. Not its job: OTel export (escher 0.1.0 ships none — ruled by the founder, 2026-10-06; the transport and credential path are a residual in `.andromeda/residuals.md`), a log file or JSON schema, and the agent-run / cold-agent harness logs (harness metadata, not this sink) — though since 2026-10-15-cold-agent-test the cold-agent pipe spawns its live `escher-session mcp --record <abs target/cold-agent/record>` child with `RUST_LOG=info` set on that child only (its kept checks owner-only under `target/cold-agent/record/`, never printed or copied), so this sink's closed `tool_call` / `command` span lines land in `target/cold-agent/server.log`, which the pipe reads only to count ` span="tool_call" ` lines, their ` ending="refused" ` / ` ending="error" ` and the accepted lines of each counted verb (`lint` · `screenshot` · `advance`), never printing or copying it; its two replay children, spawned without `--record`, send stderr to `/dev/null`.
- `tracing` (ungated), `tracing-subscriber` (features env-filter · fmt · registry · std · tracing-log), `tracing-log`.

- `RUST_LOG`, read through `EnvFilter` — the default is `warn` when it is unset or unparsable. A directive naming a target outside the allowlist does not re-admit it: the formatter is the last thing a record meets.
- `init(ServiceIdentity) -> Result<InitOutcome, InitError>` (the stderr sink) and `init_with_writer(ServiceIdentity, W: MakeWriter)` (a caller-given sink).

- `ServiceIdentity { name, version }`, built by `service_identity!()` from the CALLER's `CARGO_PKG_NAME` / `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`; `InitOutcome::{Installed, AlreadyInstalled}`; `InitError::ForeignSubscriber` (`Display` + `Error`, never a panic).
- Five public scrub constants: `ENGINE_TARGET_PREFIXES`, `ESCHER_TARGET_PREFIXES`, `SAFE_FIELDS`, `CONTENT_FIELDS`, `REDACTED`.

- Line shape, one per printed event, no ANSI: `{RFC 3339 UTC time} {LEVEL} {target} service.name={name} service.version={version} {field}={value}…` — newlines escaped, string values Debug-quoted, a bridged `log` record printed under its `log.target`, that field itself omitted. An event from a target outside the allowlist prints nothing at all, not an empty line.

- A second record class — a boundary widening, ratified by the founder (2026-10-09) as built: one line per closed span whose target the allowlist admits, and nothing when a span is created, recorded to, entered or exited. The line is the same prefix, then `span={the span's name}` (`span` a reserved field name), the span's own fields in the order recorded, then the layer's `message`, `time.busy` and `time.idle`; every pair is judged as an event's field of that name is under the span's target, an outside target's span writes no byte, and the value of a content-named span field is never stored. An event's line is unchanged, inside a span included. The layer is stated once, in the private `sink_layer` (`with_span_events(FmtSpan::CLOSE)`, the crate-private field formatter `SpanFields`); no public item moved.

- Events of its own: `info` `telemetry installed` at target `escher_telemetry`, once per successful init; ERROR `panic` at target `escher_telemetry::panic` with `panic.file` · `panic.line` · `panic.column` · `panic.payload` (redacted), then the previous hook.

- Consumed by seven_guis' two binaries — `seven_guis_native` (`main`, before `dioxus_native::launch`) and the session host `escher-session` (first thing in `main`); in both an `Err` is reported with `eprintln!` and the binary continues, and both stamp `service.name=seven_guis` — and, as a dev-dependency, by blitz-tests.
- Its startup and panic events are ungated — the engine crates gate every `tracing` call site behind their `tracing` feature; this crate has no feature to gate on.
- stderr only, never stdout.

- The target allowlist and the scrub live in `format.rs`, three outcomes by target (a bridged record judged by its `log.target`): a target starting with a prefix in `ENGINE_TARGET_PREFIXES` (`blitz` · `dioxus_native` · `stylo_taffy` · `accesskit_xplat` · `debug_timer` · `js_console`) prints only `SAFE_FIELDS` (`node_id` · `status` · `waiting_nodes` · `property` · `log.module_path` · `log.file` · `log.line`), every other field — the message included — as `{name}=[redacted]`; a target starting with a prefix in `ESCHER_TARGET_PREFIXES` (`escher_`, the underscore part of the prefix) prints every field not in `CONTENT_FIELDS` (`url` · `href` · `src` · `html` · `text` · `value` · `attrs` · `path` · `request` · `error` · `panic.payload`), those redacted; a target starting with a prefix of neither set is dropped whole — zero bytes, at every level, WARN and ERROR included, whatever `RUST_LOG` names. No engine call site is edited, and no filter layer is added: the drop sits in the formatter.

- Process-global: a second `init` changes nothing (`AlreadyInstalled`), and another global subscriber or `log` logger makes it `ForeignSubscriber`. The first install is recorded in a static `OnceLock<ServiceIdentity>` behind a static `Mutex<()>`; it spawns no thread.

the boot starts a session through `stand` only (Cells through `stand::boot_cells`, the load page through `stand::boot_load`) and hands the timer's session its time step (`stand::timer_step` over the tick handle, through `Session::with_time`; the other five carry none and still take `advance`, which moves their session's clock alone (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18)). `start <task> [--record <dir>]` checks its recording directory itself before it spawns, then spawns the same binary in its host role, `serve <task> --session <dir> [--record <dir>]` (passing `--record` to the host); since 2026-10-19-session-recording `--record <dir>`, taken at most once on `start`, the host role and the `mcp` role, keeps the session as one owner-only replayable check — `check-{n}.json` (`0600`, never replacing a file) in a `0700` directory whose parent must exist, never removed by escher, holding per call its verb, arguments, acceptance, the answer's digest and, since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay, the answer itself as an `answer` key — the line the driver wrote, masked as on every carrier, a shot's kept as `{"width":…,"height":…}` without its `png` — read back and replayed by `Check::replay` (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-19: F1 A · F2 B, F3 B) — a directory open to its group or others refused as the session error `record-dir-not-private` (exit 3, `start` spawning nothing), a recording that ends answering `recording-failed` (exit 3; over MCP `isError`); the host serves until `stop` or its 30-minute idle expiry and writes nothing to stdout; every other command is one client run that answers one line of JSON on stdout (exit `0` accepted · `1` refused · `2` usage · `3` session error — the four read from `EXIT_STATUSES` and served by `help`), save `help` (since 2026-10-12-self-description), which needs no `--session` — it admits at most one and reads it not — and answers the tool's self-description with status `0`, reaching no session; title: 2026-10-31 — A classifier that dies twice on the output-token limit is answered yes, by hand

data.head: ## 2026-10-31 — A classifier that dies twice on the output-token limit is answered yes, by hand

body:
A Haiku · max classifier can spend its whole output-token limit on one listing and die with no file, and its retry can do
the same, each death costing over half an hour. The letter's second failure halts. A `yes` only sends an entity to the
strong reader, so all-`yes` loses nothing: the operator ruled that the answer file is written by hand, class `stale`, each
clause saying no classifier answered, the second death and the word, and read through `detail.py answered` and `fanout.py
check`. The batch's false-yes figure then reads high for that reason.
Where it applies: a classifier that fails twice with no file, on the operator's word at that halt.

title: 2026-10-31 — A count pattern misses the form "`N` tests"

data.head: ## 2026-10-31 — A count pattern misses the form "`N` tests"

body:
A site sweep's count pattern shaped `{target}.{0,4}\(?N\b` reads `` `inert_subtree` (4) `` and misses "`N` tests in both
layout modes" further along a long line, so a master's count can stand outside the pattern that names it. A bare `\b676\b`
also matches citation digits (18 of 19 hits on one pattern were digits), and `synthesi[sz]` read a harness's input synthesis
at 7 of 9 hits. Write the wording of the sentence beside the name token, read a long line's offsets through `cascade.py
window`, and keep the detectors' own sweeps as the control.
Where it applies: P1's site sweep over test counts and any pattern naming a bare number or a common verb.

title: 2026-10-27 — `fanout-results.md`'s lines are a grammar fanout.py parses, not prose

data.head: ## 2026-10-27 — `fanout-results.md`'s lines are a grammar fanout.py parses, not prose

body: The wrap's Validate dispositions in `fanout-results.md` are the apply batch's input, read by `fanout.py`'s own patterns: each proposal file's heading is its bare file name alone on a line (`fanout-architecture.md`, never `### fanout-architecture.md` — a decorated heading leaves every disposition under it unread, and the render refuses with `no disposition line`), and an item main raises is aimed at the first `.andromeda/…md` path its line names, else at the master's body. A raised item that names a category file by its bare name (`conventions.md:27`) passes the render and lands on the body.

Where it applies: every raised item at a wrap's Validate. Name each target by its full `.andromeda/{doc}-detail/{slug}.md` path, one target file per item, and split an item that spans files. A render is refused again once it exists, except as `--respawn` or `--fresh`, so check the lines before the first render.

title: 2026-10-27 — A phase P5 control that plants a home-dir path trips hygiene at the operator pass

data.head: ## 2026-10-27 — A phase P5 control that plants a home-dir path trips hygiene at the operator pass

body:
A phase P5 control script that plants a host-path literal to prove a `/home/` probe reads red (a literal like
`/home/someone/x`) lands in the committed run dir, and `gate.py hygiene` P1 refuses it at the operator pass, costing a
respell and a re-fire there. Plant the control's literal in a form hygiene does not read as a host path — a
placeholder such as `/home/<user>/x` keeps the probe red and the run dir clean — from the first write.
Where it applies: every control a phase P5 writes into `.andromeda/runs/*-phase/` whose subject is a host-path probe.

title: 2026-10-25 — A sweep pattern's negated class must not exclude the dot the masters' paths carry

data.head: ## 2026-10-25 — A sweep pattern's negated class must not exclude the dot the masters' paths carry

body:
A cascade sweep pattern that bounds its window with a negated class such as `[^;.]{0,300}` (to stop at a clause end)
cannot cross a backticked path — `` `.andromeda/residuals.md` `` holds a dot — so a clause like «owned by a
`.andromeda/residuals.md` line (target: next)» never matches, its known-positive control reads unfired, and
`cascade.py sweep` refuses the call. Bound the window by `;` alone (`[^;]{0,300}`) or by a plain count, and keep the
control on a line whose clause holds a path.

Where it applies: every `cascade-patterns.toml` and `report-patterns.toml` a wrap writes for a claim worded inside
master clauses that cite files.

title: 2026-10-25 — The session hooks write the handoff in the middle of a wrap

data.head: ## 2026-10-25 — The session hooks write the handoff in the middle of a wrap

body:
The harness's own hooks append to `.claude/session-handoff.md` while a wrap runs — the Stop hook rewrites its
`## Session End Status` line, and an auto-compaction appends an `## AUTO-COMPACT` block — so a P2 snapshot pair that
spans either shows `M .claude/session-handoff.md` beside the agents' files, and the path check stops on it. Before
asking the operator to rule, diff the handoff between the pair's two trees: a hunk that is only those hook blocks is the
harness's write, not an agent's; name it in the batch note and leave the file for P6's rewrite.
Where it applies: every snapshot pair of wrap P2 (and phase P2), above all one that spans a context compaction.

title: 2026-10-25 — An agent's hand-back is its return

data.head: ## 2026-10-25 — An agent's hand-back is its return

body:
Under Agent spawns the hand-back message is both the agent's return and the session's wake; the task-notification
that follows it starts nothing (the overseer's ruling, F342). Count running = spawned − returned by hand-backs, and
take a batch's after snapshot once every hand-back has arrived, without waiting for the notifications behind them.
Where it applies: the pacing and the path check of every fan-out batch (wrap P2, phase P2, consolidation).

title: 2026-10-20 — Read a capability's acceptance against the plan's steps before writing its test

data.head: ## 2026-10-20 — Read a capability's acceptance against the plan's steps before writing its test

body:
When the verification matrix's acceptance for a capability names more than the plan step that satisfies it — an
acceptance reading «the same walk through `serve_mcp`» while the step names two calls — the acceptance is the contract.
Compare the two before writing the satisfying test, not after its first green run: a gap found after green costs a
full re-run of the gate block.
Where it applies: implement, at the step that writes a claimed capability's satisfying test.

title: 2026-10-20 — A case-blind sweep pattern turns a code token into its plain-word homonym

data.head: ## 2026-10-20 — A case-blind sweep pattern turns a code token into its plain-word homonym

body:
A site-sweep pattern written `ignore_case = true` that holds a code token alongside its prose wording (`\bVERBS\b`
beside «eleven verbs») matches every plain word the token spells, so a table-name alternative becomes a sweep of
every mention of the word, and its standing figure counts rows that never name the table. Put a code token in a
case-sensitive pattern of its own, and keep `ignore_case` for the prose wording alone.

Where it applies: P1's site sweep and P2's cascade sweep, whenever a moved fact is named both by an identifier and by
an ordinary word.

title: 2026-10-20 — A write-set probe must allow the files a new enum variant's exhaustive matches live in

data.head: ## 2026-10-20 — A write-set probe must allow the files a new enum variant's exhaustive matches live in

body:
A plan gate that asserts "no tracked file changed outside the write set" (a `git diff --name-only` filtered by an
alternation of allowed paths) reads red when a step adds an enum variant: every exhaustive `match` on that enum gains
an arm, and those files are often outside the step's own list. A must-fail control that plants some other file never
exercises this companion. When a step adds a variant to a public enum, list the files holding its exhaustive matches
(search for `match` on the enum's name) in the probe's alternation, or record them as companions in the scope record
before the gate runs.

Where it applies: phase P4/P5 when a plan's Test Commands carry a write-set probe, and implement when such a probe
reads red on a file that holds only a new match arm.

title: 2026-10-20 — escher-driver names no engine type, so a driver type cannot hold one

data.head: ## 2026-10-20 — escher-driver names no engine type, so a driver type cannot hold one

body: escher-driver depends on blitz-test-harness, dioxus-native-dom, `tracing`, `serde_json` and `png` and on neither blitz-dom nor stylo, so a type it exports cannot carry blitz-dom's `BoundingRect` or read stylo's `Contain` or `Overflow` without a manifest and lockfile change. A plan that types a driver field with an engine type, or reads a computed style as an engine enum inside the driver, should first read the crate's `[dependencies]`. If the manifest is out of scope, the driver holds its own rectangle and reads computed styles through `BaseDocument::resolved_style_value` as closed keyword sets.
Where it applies: phase planning and implement steps that add a public escher-driver type built from engine data.

title: 2026-10-20 — A count stated in more than one form needs every form in its sweep pattern

data.head: ## 2026-10-20 — A count stated in more than one form needs every form in its sweep pattern

body: The masters state one reader count several ways on the same line: `25 readers`, `by 25 checks`, `by 25`, and in words, `twenty-five checks`. A sweep pattern for the digits beside one noun misses the other forms. A site that matched only on the path beside the count then reads as a path citation, and the count stays stale. Write the pattern for a moved count with every form: the digits before each noun the masters use, `by N`, and the number in words. Extended 2026-10-20: spell the count as the masters do, never as a gate prints it — `99 passed` is a test runner's line, while the masters say `99 unit tests`.
Where it applies: P1's site sweep and P2's cascade sweep, whenever a chunk moves a shared module's reader count or any count the masters also spell out.

title: 2026-10-19 — A new name that is a prefix of the name it replaced counts the old sites

data.head: ## 2026-10-19 — A new name that is a prefix of the name it replaced counts the old sites

body: When a chunk renames a symbol to a shorter name that the old one begins with (`HeldNet` replacing `HeldNetProvider`), a bare grep or sweep pattern for the new name also matches every surviving site of the old one, and a count reads the retired name's sites as the new one's. Bound the new name at its end (`HeldNet\b`) and sweep the old name as its own alternative, so each site is counted once and as what it is.

title: 2026-10-19 — An evidence time is read, never estimated

data.head: ## 2026-10-19 — An evidence time is read, never estimated

body: A time written into chunk evidence (a run's start or end, a stamp beside a reading) is copied from a recorded event's own stamp or from `date -u` at the moment of writing. An estimated time ahead of the clock is refused by the stamp-ahead hook, and one behind it still misdates the reading.

title: 2026-10-19 — Provenance is counted by class and span, not by the words beside it

data.head: ## 2026-10-19 — Provenance is counted by class and span, not by the words beside it

body:
[corrected 2026-10-20: under classify v1.3 an in-line edit beside a standing provenance parenthesis read provenance 0
on every master this wrap edited]
`classify.py check --mode standing` (v1.3) counts a provenance span — a chunk marker as a stamp, a date, a chunk named
by reference, who ruled, what a value was — by its class and span over the whole file: it is new only when the file
adds it more often than it removes it, whatever words stand beside it. An in-line edit next to a standing parenthesis
(a value changed in place, a clause added before it) leaves the parenthesis standing and reads nothing new. Two things
still fail the arm: a new marker, date or who-ruled written anywhere in the body, and a row "cleared" by deleting
standing text, which never clears it. Write the new truth without provenance and put the ratification, the date and
the old value in the sidecar entry.

title: 2026-10-18 — An atomic read-modify-write that builds on the MSRV and on the host toolchain

data.head: ## 2026-10-18 — An atomic read-modify-write that builds on the MSRV and on the host toolchain

body: `AtomicU64::fetch_update` reads as deprecated on the dev host's toolchain ("renamed to `try_update`"), so under clippy's `-D warnings` it fails the lint leg, while `try_update` is newer than the workspace's MSRV (1.91) and fails the MSRV build. Write the update as a hand `compare_exchange_weak` loop — load, compute, `compare_exchange_weak(current, next, …)`, retry on `Err(actual)` — which builds clean on both; blitz-dom's `VirtualClock::advance` is written that way, its saturating add pinned by a unit test.

title: 2026-10-18 — A count the plan names may stand in no master

data.head: ## 2026-10-18 — A count the plan names may stand in no master

body: A plan's baseline count is often taken from the previous chunk's gate log or CI run, and that chunk's wrap may never have written it to a master — a wrap that carries counts without re-reading the tallies leaves the masters on an older figure. A site sweep for the plan's own numbers then finds nothing. Before amending a tally, sweep for the masters' latest recorded reading, move the record from that figure, and name the reading in between as skipped.

title: 2026-10-18 — A sweep pattern's clause in a master's stock wording widens it past its fact

data.head: ## 2026-10-18 — A sweep pattern's clause in a master's stock wording widens it past its fact

body: A site-sweep pattern built from a fact's wording can carry a clause the masters also use as stock phrasing for unrelated facts: a CARRY pattern's `observed absent` clause matched 71 unrelated «observed absent» lines across five masters, and a `0 high` alternative matched «600 high». The pattern's count then measures the phrase, not the fact, and every extra row costs a disposition. Anchor such a clause to the fact's own name token (`observed absent: a test naming the builder's merged`) or drop it — a bare stock phrase belongs in no pattern.

title: 2026-10-17 — A leaf comparer cannot see a count its group's sources do not state

data.head: ## 2026-10-17 — A leaf comparer cannot see a count its group's sources do not state

body:
`cascade.py leaves` groups a leaf by the masters its provenance names, and the comparer it spawns is told that a
statement no source states is not its own. `.claude/docs/services/escher-driver.md` names architecture alone, yet it
restates test-plan §1's per-file unit-test counts for escher-driver (`73 unit tests (… mcp_tests.rs 11 …)`). A wrap
that moves those counts amends test-plan, and the escher-driver leaf's comparer, reading architecture, raises
nothing. The stale count shows up only as the step-2 sweep's `leaf` row on that file.

Where it applies: a wrap that moves a per-crate test count. Dispose the sweep's `leaf` rows on
`services/escher-driver.md` by hand, and on any other services leaf that restates test-plan text, because no comparer
reaches them. A count pattern that carries the leaf's own spelling (the backticked file names) finds the rows.

title: 2026-10-16 — Moving Rust items between modules strands two kinds of import

data.head: ## 2026-10-16 — Moving Rust items between modules strands two kinds of import

body:
Splitting a module along its seams leaves two imports behind that the compiler only reports one at a time. An import
whose only use is an intra-doc link (`[`VERBS`]` in a doc comment) reads as `unused_imports` to rustc, so clippy
`-D warnings` fails on it, while dropping it breaks the link under rustdoc `-D warnings` — name the target by path
instead (`[`VERBS`](schema::VERBS)`, `[`NAME`](super::NAME)`), or keep the import only where code uses it. And a
`#[cfg(test)]` child module reaches its parent's private `use` imports through `use super::*`: when the code that
needed an import moves out, the parent stops importing it and the tests lose it too, moved item or not — the test
module then names it with its own `use` line.

Where it applies: any split of a Rust file into child or sibling modules, and any test module moved out of line
through `#[path]`; plan the test file's own `use` lines for every name the parent no longer imports, not only for the
moved items.

title: 2026-10-15 — A saved `cargo build` capture in a run dir holds the project root

data.head: ## 2026-10-15 — A saved `cargo build` capture in a run dir holds the project root

body: A phase or implement step that saves a `cargo build` run's output into its run dir commits the project root's absolute path: cargo's `Compiling {crate} v{version} ({root}/{path})` lines name it. `gate.py hygiene` refuses the file as an in-root host path. Because the path is under the root, `gate.py respell` fixes it, dropping the root prefix and nothing else, and the respell is recorded. Where it applies: any build or test capture kept as evidence. Keep the raw capture in the session scratchpad with its figures in a record, or respell it before the hygiene read.

title: 2026-10-15 — In a master sweep, `flake` reads Nix and `repeated` reads everything

data.head: ## 2026-10-15 — In a master sweep, `flake` reads Nix and `repeated` reads everything

body: A site-sweep pattern for the flakiness budget built on `flake` matches the Nix `flake` / `flake.nix` sites of the masters — 13 of 14 standing rows at the 2026-10-14-quality-gates wrap — and one built on `repeated` matched 11 master rows, none about the stand-repeat leg. Spell the budget by `flakiness` or `zero-failure`, and the leg by its name `stand-repeat`, and disposition every row that is left.
Where it applies: P1's site sweep and P2's cascade sweep over the masters, whenever a chunk touches the flakiness budget or a repeated run.

title: 2026-10-15 — `git fetch upstream main` moves FETCH_HEAD; read upstream's head live

data.head: ## 2026-10-15 — `git fetch upstream main` moves FETCH_HEAD; read upstream's head live

body: `git fetch upstream main` prints `main -> FETCH_HEAD`, which says nothing about whether `upstream/main` names upstream's current head. Before a record states that upstream stands at a commit, read it live with `git ls-remote upstream refs/heads/main` and compare it with `upstream/main` (at 2026-10-14-quality-gates both read `e72650a6`).
Where it applies: a merge-surface read, an upstream-sync take-up, or any claim about upstream's `main` that a later sync will rely on.

title: 2026-10-14 — An operator gate entry's output survives a context clear; a bare-fired one does not

data.head: ## 2026-10-14 — An operator gate entry's output survives a context clear; a bare-fired one does not

body: `gate.py run --operator {n}` writes each entry's whole output to `$TMPDIR/andromeda-gate/{marker}/run-{UTC}/{n}.log`, outside the session and the repository, and that log outlives a pause-clear of the window. So an operator entry whose printed result was lost with the window can be read back from there instead of re-run. An operator entry the operator fires bare — `gate.py hygiene`, say — leaves no such log, and its result then rests only on the word of whoever saw it.

Where it applies: resuming a chunk after a clear. Look in that directory before calling an operator entry's output lost. For an entry whose result must survive, fire it through `gate.py run --operator` rather than bare. Extended 2026-10-18: an earlier wrap's gate log in that directory is also a per-target baseline — pairing its `test result:` lines against a new run's attributes a moved tally to the one target that moved.

title: 2026-10-13 — An added-line census reads inline test modules too

data.head: ## 2026-10-13 — An added-line census reads inline test modules too

body: A plan's security census over the chunk's added engine lines (`git diff … | grep -c '\.expect\('` and its kin) counts every added line, including the `#[cfg(test)]` module inside a source file. A `.expect(…)` in a new inline test therefore reddens the census though no engine line carries one. In inline test modules write `let Some(x) = … else { panic!(…) };` (or an assertion) instead of `.expect`. Then the census reads 0 without a carve-out, and the plans' own note — inline test modules use assertions — holds.

title: 2026-10-13 — obs-plan words its silent-check census "installs no subscriber"

data.head: ## 2026-10-13 — obs-plan words its silent-check census "installs no subscriber"

body: The census of checks that install no subscriber, read no env var and print nothing (obs-plan §3, the stand bullet) is never called a "silent census" in the master. A site-sweep pattern built on the plan's shorthand "silent census" finds no master row and is refused as an unfired control (`cascade.py sweep` exit 3). Sweep the master's own wording, `installs no subscriber`.

title: 2026-10-13 — A phase control that reads a scratchpad file lands a host temp path in the run dir

data.head: ## 2026-10-13 — A phase control that reads a scratchpad file lands a host temp path in the run dir

body: A phase or implement control that records the command it ran, where that command reads a file in the session's scratchpad under the OS temp dir, writes the absolute host path into the committed run dir. `gate.py hygiene` refuses it (`· tmp`), and `gate.py respell` cannot fix it because the path is not under the project root, so the operator pass has to mask it by hand.
Where it applies: authoring a control. Point the recorded command at a file inside the run dir, or record it with the temp prefix already written as `$TMPDIR/…`, so the hygiene read stays clean.

title: 2026-10-13 — `gate.py run … --operator {n} --dry-run` writes the run dir's gate trail

data.head: ## 2026-10-13 — `gate.py run … --operator {n} --dry-run` writes the run dir's gate trail

body: A dry run of an operator entry is not read-only: it appends to the run dir's `gate-{marker}.json` trail. Once that trail is tracked (after the operator pass's pre-CI commit), a dry run fired before the push entry dirties the tree, and the push entry's own `git diff --quiet` guard then fails. Set the trail aside before the dry run and restore it before the push entry runs, or skip the dry run once the trail is tracked (as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-12-headless-screenshot/evidence/operator-pass.md, entry 20).
Where it applies: an operator pass whose plan carries a push entry guarded by `git diff --quiet`.

title: 2026-10-13 — The token `screenshot` in the masters mostly names something other than the driver's verb

data.head: ## 2026-10-13 — The token `screenshot` in the masters mostly names something other than the driver's verb

body: Before 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot the masters held `screenshot` 32 times, 31 of them the upstream `examples/screenshot.rs` example, the browser's `capture` (`blitz-screenshot-<unix-secs>`) or the `screenshot` Cargo feature. A grep or sweep pattern for the verb reads all of them as the verb. Key a pattern on the verb's own context (`` `screenshot` `` beside `verb`, `--id`, `Outcome::Shot`, `fonts-unavailable`) and disposition every row that names the example, the capture or the feature as a true claim sharing the token (as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-12-headless-screenshot/report.md, Counts).
Where it applies: a site sweep or a cascade sweep for the `screenshot` verb, its counts or its result fields.

title: 2026-10-12 — `cascade.py sweep --pattern` takes its ids after one flag

data.head: ## 2026-10-12 — `cascade.py sweep --pattern` takes its ids after one flag

body: `--pattern` is a list option: `--pattern A B C` runs the three named patterns, while `--pattern A --pattern B --pattern C` keeps only the last one given and silently runs one. A re-fire that should run only the patterns whose control never fired therefore names them all after a single `--pattern`. Read the count line of each pattern the listing prints before trusting a re-fire: the number of patterns run is in its `total (N patterns)` line.
Where it applies: a wrap's P1 site sweep and P2 step-2 sweep, whenever only part of a patterns file is re-fired.

title: 2026-10-12 — A sweep pattern for a bare count also matches a citation's digits

data.head: ## 2026-10-12 — A sweep pattern for a bare count also matches a citation's digits

body: A pattern for a count such as `\b805\b` matches every master citation whose range holds the same digits (`render.rs:805-812`), so the sweep lists a true claim beside the count it was written for. Anchor a count pattern on the words that state it (`805 passed`, `805 · 0 · 11`, `over 170 result lines`) rather than on the bare number, and when a bare number cannot be avoided, read every row it prints before dispositioning any as the count.
Where it applies: writing `report-patterns.toml` and `cascade-patterns.toml` for a moved test count, re-export count or line count.

Extended 2026-10-19: a count pattern keyed on a target's name followed by a number (`recording\W{0,3}\d+`) also matches a chunk marker that ends in that word followed by a history count («…2026-10-19-session-recording, 73 until…»), so read every row before counting it.

Extended 2026-10-25: a count alternative with no leading word boundary (`6 (test )?files`) also matches inside a longer number or a slice name («the 17 listed s06 files», «86 files»), so open every count alternative with `\b`.

title: 2026-10-11 — `gh api` refuses a job's log that holds terminal escapes

data.head: ## 2026-10-11 — `gh api` refuses a job's log that holds terminal escapes

body: A CI job log read through `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/jobs/{id}/logs` is refused when its text carries terminal escape sequences — and a runner's log usually does (coloured cargo and rustup output) — unless the call passes `--allow-escape-sequences`. Read a failed job's log with that flag (still with `-R` on the fork, per the Tier 1 note), and read the step's failure from the text, never from the refusal: the refusal says nothing about the job.

title: 2026-10-10 — A grep for a struct literal cannot tell a spread from a full literal

data.head: ## 2026-10-10 — A grep for a struct literal cannot tell a spread from a full literal

body: `grep 'TypeName {'` lists every site that opens a literal of a struct and says nothing about how each one closes. A literal that ends with `..base()` or `..Default::default()` compiles unchanged when the struct gains a field; a full literal does not. A sweep that counts the hits and reads them as "closes with a spread, no change needed" is a forecast: before a plan says a set of literals compiles unchanged after a field is added, each hit is read to its closing brace, or the claim is left to the compiler and said so.
Where it applies: any research or plan step that sizes the fallout of a new struct field from a grep — the snapshot model's state struct is the measured case.

title: 2026-10-10 — A green test run prints no figure the test only formats into its failure message

data.head: ## 2026-10-10 — A green test run prints no figure the test only formats into its failure message

body: A size, a count or a list that a test computes and puts only inside an assertion's message never reaches the log of a passing run: the entry's log holds the test's `ok` line and nothing else. A plan that says a reading "is taken from the listed entries' logs" needs an entry that prints the figure on success — or names the instrument that does (a kept measurement script, a one-shot restored mutation that makes the assertion fail and show its message, a run of the binary by hand).
Where it applies: authoring a plan's readings and its Test Commands block — name the producer of every figure the report must state before the gates run.

title: 2026-10-10 — An Edit that cuts the tail off a line takes the line's terminator with it

data.head: ## 2026-10-10 — An Edit that cuts the tail off a line takes the line's terminator with it

body: On a one-entry-per-line file — the working route, a master record — an Edit whose replacement is empty and whose matched text runs to the end of its line also removes the newline after it, so the next line is joined onto the entry: on the route that is the `↓` separator, and the file still reads plausibly by eye. The route tool says it (`UNPARSED: … entry line carrying ↓ inside it`) and the file is one line short of the count the edit should leave. When cutting freight off the end of a line, carry the newline and the head of the next line in both strings of the Edit, and after any such cut re-run `route.py markerless` and compare the line count before going on.

title: 2026-10-10 — A hand re-point of a citation can match a longer citation that starts the same

data.head: ## 2026-10-10 — A hand re-point of a citation can match a longer citation that starts the same

body: At a wrap's citation sweep a master citation is re-pointed by an anchored replace of its own text, and a citation such as `tests/common/mod.rs:1-4` is also the head of `tests/common/mod.rs:1-40`: a replace keyed on the bare citation matches both, and under replace-all it would write the longer one's digits into a range nobody read. Anchor the replace on the citation plus the character that closes it — `)` or `;` — and after any replace-all search the file for the new text followed by a digit before moving on. The same holds for a single number: `host.rs:35` heads `host.rs:350`.

title: 2026-10-09 — In the jobs API a step's seconds and conclusion do not say whether a guarded command ran

data.head: ## 2026-10-09 — In the jobs API a step's seconds and conclusion do not say whether a guarded command ran

body: A workflow step written `a || b` reads `success` whether `b` ran or not, and where `a` succeeds it reads 0 s. So a count of "the steps that call the script" is not a count of the jobs that ran it: the ci-scripts job's PyYAML guard calls the install script only where `import yaml` fails, and on a runner image that already carries PyYAML the script is never reached. What says whether a command ran is the job log — the command's own output is there or it is not.

Finding the step in the jobs listing has its own trap: a `run:` step has no name of its own, so the API names it `Run {the command}` — select it by a word of its command, and an action step by its `name`. Where a plan or a record states how many jobs ran something, take the number from the logs, and name a guarded call separately.

title: 2026-10-07 — `tracing-subscriber`'s fmt layer: what a span's close record carries, and the builder's order

data.head: ## 2026-10-07 — `tracing-subscriber`'s fmt layer: what a span's close record carries, and the builder's order

body: Read from the locked `tracing` 0.1 and `tracing-subscriber` 0.3 while building a sink that prints closed spans; each of these cost a rework before it was known.

The builder's order is fixed by its types: `with_span_events` exists only while the layer still holds the stock event formatter, so it is called before `event_format`; and when the event formatter is implemented for one field formatter only, `fmt_fields` comes before `event_format` too. The layer's record of a span closing is an event that carries the span's own metadata (`is_span()` reads true) with the span as its explicit parent, and its own fields are `message`, `time.busy` and `time.idle`. A span's fields reach the field formatter without the span's target, so a formatter that judges a field by target has to store the fields and judge them when the close record arrives; the default `add_fields` also puts a space between two recordings, which a stored form has to override.

Two spellings follow from how a value is recorded: a `&str` recorded on a span or an event prints Debug-quoted and a `format_args!` message prints bare, hence `message="close"` on a span's line beside a bare message on an event's. And the span macros take field names as literal tokens, so a `const` table cannot name them: a macro that takes the list once and emits both the span and the table is how the names are stated in one place.

title: 2026-10-07 — A fork CI run with one job still open is not green, and how to read and re-run a hung job

data.head: ## 2026-10-07 — A fork CI run with one job still open is not green, and how to read and re-run a hung job

body: A run is the witness of a gate only when its conclusion reads `verdict: green`. A run whose other jobs all read `success` while one is still open reads `in progress`, however long it has stood: fifteen of sixteen is not the acceptance, and it is never recorded as one.

`ci.py conclusion --wait` names the oldest running job and its age, not the step that job is in, so a hang looks the same as a slow build until the bound fires. When a wait returns `in progress` with no failed job, read the open job's steps (`gh run view {run} -R {fork} --json jobs`) before waiting again: a step that normally takes seconds and has stood for minutes is the hang. `gh run cancel {run}` on a run whose only open job is the hung one keeps every concluded job's result, and `gh run rerun {run} --job {databaseId}` then re-runs that job alone as a new attempt of the same run, which the conclusion read counts as one run on the same commit. Bound the re-runs before starting: stop after a second hang in the same step.

A job log fetched with `gh run view --log` carries its colour codes as literal text — `^[[1m` between `Running` and the test target's path — not as escape bytes, so a parser that strips ANSI escapes leaves them in and a pattern anchored on `Running tests/` finds nothing. Extended 2026-10-10: the Windows job prints the path with a backslash, `tests\{name}.rs`, so a `/`-only pattern misses that job even with the colour codes handled — count cargo lines in a CI log only with a pattern that has first matched a known positive from that same log, such as the bare target name.

title: 2026-10-07 — `$TMPDIR` is unset in the Bash tool's shell on this host

data.head: ## 2026-10-07 — `$TMPDIR` is unset in the Bash tool's shell on this host

body: A redirect to `$TMPDIR/x.log` expands to `/x.log` and fails with "Permission denied", and the command before it in the pipeline still runs — its exit then reads as a failure of the thing being measured. Write scratch output to the session's scratchpad directory by its full path. The gate tool's printed `$TMPDIR/andromeda-gate/…` names the OS temp dir (`tempfile.gettempdir()`), not the shell variable.

title: 2026-10-07 — A per-crate `cargo clippy` is not the CI lint leg

data.head: ## 2026-10-07 — A per-crate `cargo clippy` is not the CI lint leg

body: `cargo clippy -p {crate} -- -D warnings`, with or without `--all-targets`, builds blitz-dom under that one crate's feature set, and a crate that does not turn on blitz-dom's `file-input` feature gets a `needless_return` in blitz-dom's library code: the `return` stands just before a block gated on that feature, so with the feature off it is the function's last statement. The CI form, `cargo clippy --workspace --locked -- -D warnings`, unifies features across the workspace, turns `file-input` on and is green — an upstream lint that is nobody's red. To lint a chunk's new code the way CI will, run the leg itself (`bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh clippy`, or `fast`); for a quick compile check of one crate use `cargo test -p {crate} --locked`. A per-crate clippy run is a different check, and its failure says nothing about the gate. [corrected 2026-10-07: the cause is the feature set, not `--all-targets` or test code — the same red reads without `--all-targets`, and blitz-dom alone lints clean with `file-input` on]

title: 2026-10-07 — A sed or grep address that ends at an item's name also selects every item whose name opens with it

data.head: ## 2026-10-07 — A sed or grep address that ends at an item's name also selects every item whose name opens with it

body: A gate that lifts one function or constant out of a file by its opening line — `sed -n '/^fn controls/,/^}/p'` — lifts every item whose name starts the same way: the table `controls` and the test `controls_lie_inside_the_viewport` both match, and the comparison built on it reads red on a correct tree. Close the name with the character that follows it in the source (`fn controls(`, `const INPUT_NAMES:`), and sweep the file for other items opening with the same word before trusting the address. A control built with the same open address proves nothing here: it carries the extra item on both sides and compares equal, so plant the control's difference in the item the gate is for and check that the gate's line count is the item's own.

title: 2026-10-07 — `str::escape_debug` and `{:?}` on a `str` do not escape alike

data.head: ## 2026-10-07 — `str::escape_debug` and `{:?}` on a `str` do not escape alike

body: Both escape a `"`, a backslash, a line break and a tab, so they read as interchangeable — but `escape_debug` also backslash-escapes an apostrophe (`it's` becomes `it\'s`) and leaves a combining mark in mid-string bare, while the `Debug` form (`{:?}`) writes the apostrophe as it is and escapes the mark. Text that an agent or a person reads — the snapshot's text form, a diff, a CLI's output — wants the `Debug` form.

When a plan names one of the two and its research names the other, nothing has been decided yet: run both on a string holding an apostrophe before writing the code, and say in the plan which one the design means.
See: `.claude/docs/services/dioxus-native-dom.md` (the snapshot text bullet)

title: 2026-10-06 — A case-insensitive grep for an upper-case acronym matches inside ordinary words

data.head: ## 2026-10-06 — A case-insensitive grep for an upper-case acronym matches inside ordinary words

body: A licence or protocol acronym searched with `grep -i` matches inside common words: `-i 'MPL'` hits every "example", so a per-master site count reads dozens where the acronym itself occurs once or not at all. Sweep for an acronym case-sensitively with word boundaries (`grep -E '\bMPL\b'`), and when an `-i` count looks large, read a few hits before trusting it.

title: 2026-10-06 — Committed run-dir and evidence text must not spell a host temp path, even as prose

data.head: ## 2026-10-06 — Committed run-dir and evidence text must not spell a host temp path, even as prose

body: The hygiene read (`gate.py hygiene`) refuses any committed run-dir or evidence file whose text holds an absolute host path, and a temp-dir path counts even inside an explanatory sentence: a phase extract that named the Claude Code session's temp-folder prefix literally, to say the README must not contain it, was refused at the pre-CI commit. When such a file has to talk about a host path, describe it in words ("the session temp-dir prefix") or write it repo-relative, and run the hygiene read before the commit.

title: 2026-10-06 — A presentation guard that diffs grepped source lines must strip leading whitespace

data.head: ## 2026-10-06 — A presentation guard that diffs grepped source lines must strip leading whitespace

body: A gate that proves "no class / style / author-id change" by grepping those lines from the base and the working tree and diffing them reads RED on a re-nest alone: un-nesting an element by one level shifts its `class:` line's indentation while the expression stays byte-identical. The guard's intent is the attribute text, not the indentation — so pipe both grepped sides through `sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//'` before the diff (a CSS-block comparison, whose indentation is content, stays exact). When authoring the guard, add a re-nest control beside the changed-value controls.

title: 2026-10-06 — Inside a Bash tool call `grep` is ugrep, and a long bounded repetition can print nothing

data.head: ## 2026-10-06 — Inside a Bash tool call `grep` is ugrep, and a long bounded repetition can print nothing

body: Inside a Bash tool call `grep` is a shell function that runs Claude Code's embedded ugrep; the host's own `/usr/bin/grep` is GNU grep, and `command grep` reaches it [corrected 2026-10-07: this entry said the host's grep is ugrep — measured, `type grep` reads "grep is a function", bare `grep --version` reads ugrep 7.8.4, `command grep --version` and `/usr/bin/grep --version` read GNU grep 3.12]. A pattern carrying a long bounded repetition — a context window like `.{0,200}` around the match — exceeds ugrep's complexity limit: the error goes to stderr, and in a call that pipes or alternates several patterns stdout stays empty, which reads exactly like zero hits. Two site sweeps over the masters returned nothing that way while the same patterns in Python found four sites. For a site sweep or an absence claim, use Python's `re` (print a window around `match.start()`), or keep ugrep patterns free of long `{m,n}` counts, and read stderr before trusting an empty result.

title: 2026-10-06 — A grep hit seen through a clipped view is not read

data.head: ## 2026-10-06 — A grep hit seen through a clipped view is not read

body: The `.andromeda/` masters carry lines of 1–5 KB, so a grep row viewed through `cut -c1-N`, `head -c` or a truncating tool shows a few hundred characters of a line whose fact may sit thousands of characters further in. A report that calls such a hit "unrelated" or claims "no master states X" from the clipped view is guessing; the hit is read at its match offset (a script printing a window around `match.start()`, or `cascade.py window --at`) before it is dispositioned. Absence and caught-all claims carry the full hit list, each row with its offset and its disposition.

title: 2026-10-06 — Grepping `agent-run` also finds the cold-agent marker and "agent-runnable"

data.head: ## 2026-10-06 — Grepping `agent-run` also finds the cold-agent marker and "agent-runnable"

body: A fixed-string grep or sweep pattern `agent-run` matches inside the chunk marker `cold-agent-run-pipe` (every evidence path and sidecar citation under it) and the prose word "agent-runnable". So a hit count of the agent-run contract's sites overcounts. Anchor the pattern on the contract's own forms (`scripts/agent-run`, `target/agent-run`, `agent-run contract`) or read every row before counting it as a site.

Extended 2026-10-27: a file-citation pattern on a bare file name (`lint\.rs:\d+`) also matches every citation of a file whose name ends in it (`stand_lint.rs:`), so anchor it on the path's directory (`src/lint\.rs:`).

title: 2026-10-06 — A probe's write-up claims only what the probe read

data.head: ## 2026-10-06 — A probe's write-up claims only what the probe read

body: A probe that reads an attribute and a selector match says nothing about a third consumer of the same attribute. blitz-dom reads `disabled` two ways — presence for the element state, `:disabled` and click targeting, a parsed bool for focusability — so a probe that saw `disabled="false"` match `:disabled` did not show the control leaving the focus order, yet the evidence file, the implement report, the operator question and the regression test's doc comment all said it did; two drift detectors reading the cited source caught it at the wrap. When a write-up names a mechanism, either the probe measures it or the sentence cites the code line that decides it — and a claim about one consumer of an attribute is not a claim about the others.

title: 2026-10-06 — The rustfmt write hook leaves a crate root unformatted when its module files do not exist yet

data.head: ## 2026-10-06 — The rustfmt write hook leaves a crate root unformatted when its module files do not exist yet

body: The PostToolUse hook formats each file as it is written, but rustfmt resolves `mod` declarations: a new crate's `lib.rs` written before its `format.rs` / `panic.rs` exist fails to resolve its modules and is left as written, while the module files written after it are formatted. The miss surfaces only at the `fast` leg's `cargo fmt --check`. When creating a crate, write the module files first, or run `cargo fmt -p {crate}` once the burst of writes is done. Extended 2026-10-06: an edit made through a Bash script (`python`, `sed`) never fires the hook at all — write Rust through the Write/Edit tools, or run `cargo fmt --all` after a scripted edit.

title: 2026-10-06 — The Bash guard's heredoc arm reads a payload's prose too

data.head: ## 2026-10-06 — The Bash guard's heredoc arm reads a payload's prose too

body: The guard's `cat`/`tee`-heredoc match is a token match over the whole command text, so a heredoc PIPED into a tool — an evolve append, an inline python script — is refused when its payload's prose quotes the guarded shell form: the record's text trips it, not the command. When a payload must mention the guarded form, describe it in words instead of quoting it. The two guard rules themselves — a heredoc with a file target, a `cd` that moves the working directory — are in `.claude/rules/host-linux.md`. [corrected 2026-10-10: trimmed to the one fact the host rule file lacks — that file has carried both rules on every turn since 2026-10-07, and the match over payload prose read true in the guard's source on 2026-10-09]

title: 2026-10-05 — A chunk that moves cited source lines stales the masters' file:line citations

data.head: ## 2026-10-05 — A chunk that moves cited source lines stales the masters' file:line citations

body: The spec masters cite code as `file:line` throughout. A chunk that inserts or removes lines in a cited file — a profile stanza in `Cargo.toml`, a guard in a workflow, a rewritten `ci.yml` — leaves every citation past the edit pointing at the wrong line, and no drift detector sees it: the detectors read the chunk report alone, and the report carries no map of moved lines. The first such chunk on escher left 114 stale citations across five masters.

The wrap's citation sweep owns the repair: it opens the wrap's reconcile phase, re-points the digits of every citation whose cited line moved, and lists each row it leaves to a read — which is read at the cited lines and dispositioned before the drift fan-out. Re-point no citation by hand outside a row the sweep lists. [corrected 2026-10-10: this entry told a wrap to grep the masters and re-point by hand — the sweep, first written on escher at the 2026-10-09-audit-corrections-agent-surfaces wrap, does it at every chunk wrap]

title: 2026-10-05 — Count from the listing you just read, never from the plan's forecast

data.head: ## 2026-10-05 — Count from the listing you just read, never from the plan's forecast

body: A plan's implementation notes often predict a count ("one cache per compiling job, 6 + 4 = 10"). When an evidence record states the measured figure, take it from the tool output read at that moment and count it there; a number carried over from the plan's forecast survives into the record looking measured. On escher the operator-pass evidence first recorded the plan's 10 caches where `gh cache list` listed 11 + 1, caught only when the report re-counted the listing. If the measurement disagrees with the forecast, record both and name the forecast as disproved.

title: 2026-10-05 — A secret probe over a record that quotes the probe matches itself

data.head: ## 2026-10-05 — A secret probe over a record that quotes the probe matches itself

body: A credential or secret grep run over an evidence record (`grep -ciE 'token=|password=|…'` expecting `0`) counts its own pattern when that record lists the probe's command verbatim — a self-match, never a leaked secret. A plan that asks the record to copy "every gate run verbatim" and also runs a secret probe over the same record is jointly unsatisfiable for the probe's own line.

When a record must name such a probe, cite where its command lives (the plan's Test Commands entry) instead of copying the pattern; when authoring a plan, keep the probe's pattern out of the files it scans. Read the hit before treating a non-zero count as a leak.
Each entry follows this structure:
This file is **Tier 3 — on-demand**. Claude reads it when explicitly needed (debugging, planning, reviewing patterns), not at session start.
Other tiers:
- **Tier 1** (always loaded) — universal safety rules in `CLAUDE.md` `USER:session-learnings` section (critical, short)

_Extracted from architecture.md and project conventions by `/andromeda-setup-project`. How work actually flows on escher._
- **Branching:** one long-lived build branch per version — `build/escher-0.1.0` for 0.1.0; chunks commit on it (no per-chunk feature branches).
- **Commit format:** conventional commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `refactor:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `perf:`, `build:`, `ci:`).

- **Main branch:** `main` (upstream Blitz CI runs on `main` and `v0.*`; escher's `ci.yml` also runs on every `build/**` push); the fork's GitHub default branch is the version's build branch, `build/escher-0.3.0`, whose root `README.md` is the front page GitHub renders.

- **Before a push:** `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast` — the local pre-push gate, the same leg commands CI runs for fmt, clippy, test and CI scripts, then `embolden`, which has no CI job; `blitz-paint/font-embolden` is built locally by the `embolden` step of `fast`, `--features blitz-paint/font-embolden` on `cargo test -p blitz-tests` the local witness for a paint change under that feature.
- **Never force push** to main/master. Use `gh` for GitHub operations.
- **Upstream:** escher is a fork of Blitz; keep upstream conventions (spec citations, one-behaviour test files) so merges stay cheap.

This project was adopted into the Andromeda pipeline (`/andromeda-adopt` at `0f60502e`); its masters describe the code as built. Upstream DioxusLabs/blitz `main` was last merged at `23b9b26a9` (merge commit `3eda07bc`, 2026-10-17), the next sync's merge base; upstream `main` was last read at `e42ee1f25`, thirty-six of the fifty-seven commits past the merge base taken by no-commit cherry-picks with the merge base unmoved and twenty-one left out; git Stylo 0.23-pre, the six Taffy-main commits and Dioxus 0.8.0-alpha.3 wait for escher's next version, so Stylo stays "0.22.0", Taffy the registry "0.15" and Dioxus "0.7.3".
**Initial planning (done):** adopt → architecture + 6 specialist plans → `/andromeda-route` (escher-0.1.0 working route) → `/andromeda-setup-project` (this ecosystem).
**Per chunk (main development loop):**
1. `/andromeda-new-session` — load context, run the health check, propose the next action
2. `/andromeda-phase` — promote and plan the next working-route chunk
3. `/andromeda-implement` — execute the plan (writes code and tests, runs the gates green; it never commits)
4. `/andromeda-wrap-session` — reconcile, capture learnings, commit, push
5. Repeat; when the version's verification matrix is complete, `/andromeda-route` starts the next version
- **Start:** `/andromeda-new-session` — reads the handoff, dashboard, health check, next action.

- **During:** follow the current chunk's plan; run the gates (`bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fmt` / `clippy` — or `fast` for all four fast legs, then the `embolden` step — and targeted `cargo test -p …`).
- **End:** `/andromeda-wrap-session` — commits, updates `.claude/session-handoff.md`, curates learnings into the right tier.
**Don't skip session boundaries** — new-session and wrap-session keep CLAUDE.md and the masters current.

Shell mechanics of the Bash tool on this host: the recurring ways a recipe breaks. Every rule is measured on live
work, not hypothetical.

- The working directory MAY persist across calls (measured both ways on one host: persisted in one session,
  reset after every call in another) — rely on neither: anchor every cross-call path absolutely, or `cd` only
  inside a subshell `( cd X && … )` (setup's Bash guard denies a `cd` that would move the cwd); a
  `cd` inside a compound command can also trip a permission prompt.

- A zero-is-healthy count probe (`grep -c` / `grep -q`) exits non-zero on no matches and aborts a
  `&&` chain — suffix `|| true`, or chain with `;`.

- Never build JSON — or any multi-KB document — through shell quoting: `printf` collapses escapes
  content-dependently.

- Documents: the Write tool, whole-content (setup's Bash guard refuses a `cat`/`tee` heredoc with a file
  target). Ledger appends: a VALIDATED python append (`json.dumps(json.loads(...))` — a mangled payload fails
  loudly instead of landing).

- Inline `python -c` is fine for a SHORT, quote-free, single-expression probe; anything longer,
  quote-bearing, or document-carrying goes through a scratchpad file run by path (the measured failure
  modes are size and unquoted expansion, not inlining or quoted heredocs).

- `rm -rf` + `mkdir` + launch compounds get denied by permission layers and abort mid-chain —
  granular steps, fresh unique dirs, no `rm` in a launch path.
- `;` over `&&` for optional probes: an optional probe's failure must not abort the chain.

- Never `pgrep -f` / `pkill -f` on a pattern the invoking shell's own command line contains — it matches, and
  kills, that shell. Select by `ps -eo pid,comm,args` and act on the pid.

- Read `$?` from the BARE command — `| tail` / `| head` report the pipe's LAST command's exit
  (measured green-masking red gates). Redirect output to a file and inspect the file.
- When a tool prints its own verdict, the printed text outranks an unisolated `$?`.

- Heredoc terminators must be column-0 and whitespace-exact — a padded terminator silently
  swallows the rest of the script.

- The repo pins LF through `.gitattributes` (setup appends the lines): `git ls-files --eol` on a pipeline file
  reads `i/lf w/lf`. Never write CRLF into a pipeline file, and never fix a terminator reading with a
  terminator-agnostic script.
- 2026-10-10: `pgrep -x` matches nothing for a process name over 15 characters and says so on stderr only — take a census by `ps -eo comm=` and the name's first 15 characters (`seven_guis_nati`).

- 2026-10-13: Run every pipeline tool (`{tools_dir}/*.py`, a CI leg script) bare or redirected to a file that is then read whole — never piped into `head`, `tail`, `grep`, `cut`, `sed` or `awk`, even when its verdict is its last line (the founder's standing direction).

- 2026-10-13: `escher-session` refuses a state directory whose socket path passes 94 bytes (`state-dir-too-long`, exit 3), and the session scratchpad's absolute path is already over it — give a manual driver run a relative `target/tmp/{name}` directory, as the session checks do.
- 2026-10-20: A whole-tree `grep -rn` from the repository root walks `target/` and runs past the Bash tool's 120 s limit — search tracked files with `git grep`, which answers at once.

- 2026-10-27: `rerere.enabled` is on for this checkout, so a cherry-pick's conflict resolutions land in the shared `.git/rr-cache` and replay on later picks — run every trial or take cherry-pick of an upstream sync as `git -c rerere.enabled=false cherry-pick …`.

Path-scoped rules for telemetry, logging and timing code. Source: `.andromeda/obs-plan.md` (obs tier 0).

- **escher binaries:** install `escher_telemetry::init(escher_telemetry::service_identity!())` at start (today the two binaries of seven_guis — `seven_guis_native`, before `launch`, and the session host `escher-session` (its command line, host role and, since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface, `mcp` role), first thing in `main` — both stamping `service.name=seven_guis`; an `Err` is `eprintln!`ed and the binary continues; the in-process headless stand `seven_guis::stand`, the driver library `escher-driver` — its session and its command schema — and their checks install none, save `stand_act_spans`'s two re-run children, which install the sink over an in-memory capture, and `stand_mcp_tools`, which installs a hand-written in-process recorder that prints nothing) — stderr only, never stdout; filter from `RUST_LOG`, default `warn`; one line per printed event, `{RFC 3339 UTC} {LEVEL} {target} service.name=… service.version=… {field}={value}…`, and — a boundary widening ratified by the founder, 2026-10-09 (obs-plan §6) — one per closed span of an admitted target, the same prefix then `span={name}`, the span's fields and the layer's `message` · `time.busy` · `time.idle`, nothing before the span closes; `log` records bridged into the same formatter. A second `init` is `AlreadyInstalled`; a foreign subscriber is `InitError::ForeignSubscriber`, never a panic.

- **Engine and upstream crates:** `tracing` 0.1 events compiled only with each crate's `tracing` cargo feature; every call site is `#[cfg(feature = "tracing")]` with a `#[cfg(not(feature = "tracing"))] let _ = …;` fallback — keep the gate (the engine features stay off in a package-alone build; a workspace-wide build turns blitz-dom's on).

- The `tracing` feature forwards down the crate chain (dioxus-native → dioxus-native-dom, blitz-shell, blitz-dom, blitz-html, blitz-net); `blitz` turns it on by default, `blitz-vibey-script` does not.
- Upstream subscribers: `tracing_subscriber::fmt::init()` (stdout) in the apps under `tracing`; `tracing_wasm` on wasm; the WPT runner uses the `log` facade with `env_logger`.
- JS console output goes to the `log` crate at debug level, target `js_console`, keeping stdout/stderr clean; embedders drain JS errors with `take_js_errors` (≤256 retained between drains).
- Panics: escher-telemetry's hook logs one ERROR at target `escher_telemetry::panic` (`panic.payload` redacted) and chains the previous hook.

- Two spans exist, both escher-driver's, built by hand with `tracing::info_span!` at INFO under the target `escher_driver`: the command span — every call handed to `escher_driver::Session::run` leaves one, name `command`, its eight fields (`verb` · `cause` · `settled` · `busy` · `passes` · `added` · `removed` · `changed`) each recorded only where it applies and holding a fixed word of the schema, a bool or a count — and, since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10), the `tool_call` span — one per MCP `tools/call` request, its two fields `tool` (the table's word) and `ending` (`accepted` · `refused` · `error`), the parent of the call's `command` span — the session verbs `start` · `status` · `stop` and, since 2026-10-12-self-description, `help`, answered by the server, leave a `tool_call` with no `command` child. Add no field to either that holds what a call supplied or a screen reads: never field a `Command`, `Call`, `ArgValue`, `Outcome`, `Refusal` or `Fault`, nor an argument by its schema name — they print an id, typed text, an accessible name or a control's value, and of the argument names only `text` is scrubbed. The crate installs no subscriber. No `#[instrument]`, metrics or OTel exist (observed absent), and the settle loop `Harness::settle`, the driver's load wait over it (`settle_waiting`, bounded by `LOAD_WAIT`, run inside the call's `command` span, its eight fields as they are), `Session::act` and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, `Harness::screenshot` / `screenshot_rect` and the driver's private `image` encoder and, since 2026-10-13-stand-contrast-harness, the harness's contrast reader `Harness::text_contrast` (which reads and changes nothing in the document) carry no span of their own, nor does the recording (`Session::recording_into`, `Session::recording_failed`, the recorder, `Check::from_bytes`, the replay `Check::replay` — each replayed step writing its own `command` span through `Session::run`, the replay adding none —, the wire's `recording-failed` reply), nor `Session::lint` itself, which the `lint` verb reaches inside its call's `command` span, opening none of its own, with blitz-dom's read-only `BaseDocument::text_extent`, and dioxus-native-dom's `Snapshot::text_parts`, the part read's cut, which open no span, emit no event and record no field, escher-driver keeping its 2 `info_span!` sites, nor the select list, which adds no span, field, event or log line (blitz-dom's `node::select_list`, blitz-paint's `render::select_list`, the `BaseDocument` readers `open_select` · `select_list_bounds` · `select_list_view` · `select_row_layout` and writer `close_select_list`, dioxus-native-dom's `is_select` and the driver's `focus_select` open no span) — and nothing logs, fields or prints a lint `Finding` or `Reason`, which derive `Debug` and hold stable ids; the command span keeps its eight fields a recording held or not, and an MCP call after which the recording ended is answered `isError` as `RecordingFailed`, its `tool_call` ending `error` with `tool` and `ending` alone; a `screenshot` or `lint` call's or a part read's (`Outcome::Part`) command span records `verb` (and `cause` when refused) alone — never a shot's image, its byte size or its `width` / `height`, nor a lint's findings or their count, nor a part's number or the part count. `docs/capabilities.md` restates both spans and the scrub's limits, and its pin `.github/scripts/test_capability_statement.py` reads none of these claims — a change to the span set or to the scrub's limits is made in that document by hand.

- The agent-run test contract (`scripts/agent-run.sh`) writes JSON-line harness events to stdout and `target/agent-run/events.jsonl` — harness metadata, not a telemetry sink and not escher's line format; its rules live in `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`.

- The cold-agent pipe (`scripts/cold-agent.sh`) writes JSON-line run events (`run.start`, `run.end`, `status`, `cleanup`) to stdout, `run.start` and `run.end` also appended to `target/cold-agent/events.jsonl` — counts, booleans and closed words only, never transcript text, a tool argument, a tool answer, a reply or the agent's check; its raw session transcript stays in `target/cold-agent/transcript.jsonl`, the agent's check in `check.json` and the live session's kept checks in the owner-only `target/cold-agent/record/` (`mkdir -m 700`), none printed or copied; since 2026-10-15-cold-agent-test its one MCP server is `escher-session mcp --record <abs target/cold-agent/record>` spawned with `RUST_LOG=info` on that child only, so escher's sink writes its closed `tool_call` / `command` span lines to `target/cold-agent/server.log`, which the pipe reads only to count ` span="tool_call" ` lines, their ` ending="refused" ` / ` ending="error" ` and the accepted lines of each counted verb (`lint` · `screenshot` · `advance`, `span_counts`), never printing or copying it; a judged check is replayed on two further `escher-session mcp` children without `--record`, stderr to `/dev/null` (test-plan §3).
- Phase timing is opt-in: `log-phase-times` (→ `debug_timer/enable`) and `log-frame-times`; `debug_timer` swaps in a zero-cost dummy when `enable` is off and prints to stdout when on.

- escher's sink applies an allowlist of targets in the formatter (obs-plan §8): engine targets (`blitz*`, `dioxus_native*`, `stylo_taffy`, `accesskit_xplat`, `debug_timer`, `js_console`) print only `node_id` · `status` · `waiting_nodes` · `property` · `log.module_path` · `log.file` · `log.line`; escher's own targets (`escher_*`) print every field except `url` · `href` · `src` · `html` · `text` · `value` · `attrs` · `path` · `request` · `error` · `panic.payload`, which are redacted; a record from any other target (Stylo's `style::*`, `selectors::matching`, `dioxus_core::*`; on the windowed stand also `naga::*`, `wgpu_*`, `winit_wayland::*`) is dropped whole, at every level and whatever `RUST_LOG` names — a third-party WARN or ERROR included. A closed span's every pair — its name under `span`, its fields, the layer's close fields — is judged by the same rule as an event's field, and an outside target's span writes nothing. A sink-installing binary's stderr holds no id and no name at any level (measured on `escher-session` and on the windowed stand, before and after the drop; typed text measured on the `escher-session` host while it runs calls — 0 occurrences of a typed sentinel at `trace`, under both builds, with one command-span line per hosted call — and, since 2026-10-14-quality-gates, on the windowed stand, where no command runs, built with the workspace and on the host's display — 0 needles at every level; a shot's image, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, measured on the `escher-session` host and its `mcp` role — 0 occurrences of its first 64 base64 characters at `trace`, under both builds; a lint's `command` line holds no finding, id, bound or count — `host_log` and `mcp_log` each drive one `lint` at `trace` with 0 needles; a part read's `command` line, `verb="snapshot"`, holds no part number, count, size or text — `host_log` and `mcp_log` each drive one part read at `trace` with 0 needles; an option's label, on a select list opened and chosen — `host_log` and `mcp_log` each read one at `trace` with 0 option needles); what `escher-session` prints on stdout is a command's answer — ids, names, values and state readings by the ratified crossing, and since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot a shot's PNG as a command's answer, a shot of an open list carrying a page's option labels and group `label`s as pixels (a boundary widening ratified, the shot's own fields unmoved) — never a log line, and none of it goes into a log field; a recording's kept check (`check-{n}.json`, `0600`) holds each answered call's arguments — unmasked typed text included —, its `accepted`, its answer's FNV-1a 64 digest and the answer itself as `answer` (a shot's without `png`) at rest, written through the crate's `json` writer, never a log line, field or print (`host_log` and `mcp_log` read 0 of the recording needles at `trace`, the span counts unchanged) — and a "nothing in the logs" check must still run against a host that installs the sink (seven_guis' `host_log` does), since a zero from one that does not proves nothing. `SelectListRow.label` holds page text in a public read type and is never logged; a label leaves only as a painted pixel and the snapshot's existing `name`. A failed load's error text travels `NetHandler::error` (a default that does nothing unless the handler overrides it) into `ResourceLoadResponse` and the `Resource load failed` line; `url` and `error` are in escher-telemetry's scrub set, so the sink prints `waiting_nodes` and every other field, the message included, `[redacted]`, and no other carrier takes the text. A new field carrying user content takes a name in the content set — or is not logged.
- The upstream apps' `fmt::init()` and the WPT runner's `env_logger` still log URLs, attribute values, text-node contents and outer HTML as-is.

Universal security rules for escher. No `paths:` frontmatter — this file loads on every turn, so it stays lean.
Source: `.andromeda/security-plan.md` (security tier 0; application threat model NOT YET MEASURED).

- Secrets live only in GitHub Actions secrets/vars (macOS signing key, Android keystore + passwords, Apple certificate, `WPT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`); signing material written to disk in CI is removed in an `always()` step — keep that pairing. The jobs that reach them (publish, WPT, post-results) run only in `DioxusLabs/blitz` — keep the `github.repository` guard; a ref-only `if:` re-arms them on the fork.

- On the dev host only, the cold-agent live run (`scripts/cold-agent.sh run`) authenticates with the operator's own Claude Code login, held by the `claude` CLI outside the repo (`apiKeySource` none; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-06) — no API key, no CI secret, and no copy in code, fixtures, events or committed evidence. The MCP surface's one live trial (2026-10-10-mcp-surface, `evidence/live-trial.py`) used the same login on the founder's word for that trial — no new secret source.

- Source reads no secret: env reads are `WPT_DIR`, `PAINT_TREE_BENCH_HTML`, `HOME`, `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`, `RUST_LOG` (escher-telemetry's filter) and `MULTI_DOC_N` · `MULTI_DOC_SEQ` · `MULTI_DOC_FLAT` (the root example `multi_doc` alone) only — and, at build time in the session checks, `CARGO_BIN_EXE_escher-session` and `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` — plus `TMPDIR` through `std::env::temp_dir()` at two test-only sites, escher-driver's unix-only client unit test and blitz-vibey-script's `tests/dom.rs` helper `temp_dir_with_files` (test code only, not secret). Never commit `.env*`.

- Remote HTML/CSS/images/fonts/sub-documents are untrusted: keep the recursion caps (`MAX_SUBDOCUMENT_DEPTH = 10`, `MAX_IMPORT_DEPTH = 16`) and the stale-iframe-response discard by request id. A key press with focus on a control whose anonymous block was dropped does not panic, for `hidden`, `style="display:none"` and CSS alone: `BaseDocument::deallocate_anonymous_block` sets `layout_parent` to `None` on each child still in the slab naming the block, so the id does not go stale; focus stays and the key still acts.

- `blitz-net` reads `file:` URLs from disk with no path restriction and has no response-size cap or request timeout — do not route agent- or user-supplied URLs through it without a decision recorded in the security plan. A failed load reaches `NetHandler::error`, on the public trait a default that does nothing, so a wrapping implementer that does not forward it compiles and drops the failure silently — forward it.
