- **Integration:** `tests/blitz-tests/tests/*.rs`, one file per behaviour, depending only on dev-dependencies; the stand checks read the tables and helpers they share from `tests/common/mod.rs` (`mod common;`) and the checks that hold a session — the session checks, `stand_settle`, the sixteen driver-action checks `stand_act_*`, `stand_mcp_tools`, `stand_screenshot_repeat`, `stand_requirement_sweep`, `stand_virtual_clock`, since 2026-10-19-session-recording `stand_session_recording` and, since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay, `stand_replay` and, since 2026-10-19-visual-lint, `stand_lint` and, since 2026-10-20-load-wait, `stand_load_wait` and, since 2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts, `stand_snapshot_parts` and the two served-page checks `stand_cells_served` and `stand_load_page` (32 readers, `stand_cells_served` and `stand_load_page` the thirtieth and thirty-first, `stand_act_popup` the thirty-second; `stand_mcp_masked`, `password_painted_masked`, `stand_non_lean_tasks` and `password_caret_click` declare none) — what they share from `tests/session_common/mod.rs` (`mod session_common;`: the held session, the driver's call builders `click` · `type_into` · `press` · `advance` · `scroll` · `snapshot` · `screenshot` · `screenshot_of` · `lint` · `snapshot_part`, the outcome reader `act`, the part reader `part` (a paged snapshot's text, part and count), the shot reader `shot`, the lint reader `linted` (a lint's findings), the refusal readers `refused` and `refused_unchanged`, since 2026-10-19-session-recording the recording readers `kept` and the unix-only `mode`, and since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay `shot_prefix` (the first 64 base64 characters of a whole-screen shot) — its `replay` removed then for the replay `Check::replay`); and, since 2026-10-19-shared-fixtures, what 31 checks — 23 `stand_*` files (`stand_snapshot_parts` since 2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts, `stand_act_select`, `stand_load_wait` since 2026-10-20-load-wait, `stand_lint` since 2026-10-19-visual-lint, `stand_act_popup`), `font_face_sniffed_source`, `select_interaction`, `select_popup`, `select_popup_painted`, `inert_subtree`, `accessibility_states`, `checkable_change_event` and `text_range_no_change_event` — share from `tests/fixtures/mod.rs` (`mod fixtures;`, `#![allow(dead_code)]`: the fixture boot `boot(app, incremental)` with the stand's options `stand::options(incremental)`, `hold(label, app, incremental)` over it, the pages more than one check reads — `password_labelled`, `password_named`, `covered` and `many_items` with its `ITEMS` (read by `stand_snapshot_parts` and `stand_act_spans`) — and the held network stand-in `HeldNet`); none is a test target. Every other file is its own target: `tests/all.rs` is upstream's single-binary target, kept in the manifest at `test = false` and never built — add no `autotests = false` and no second `[[test]]` table (`BlitzTestsTargetsTest`, in the `ci-scripts` leg, pins it). A check that needs a session process starts and stops its own host (its test binary re-run on one `#[ignore]` child, or the package's binary through `CARGO_BIN_EXE_*`), bounds every wait, guards the host with kill-and-reap and, holding a session over the socket, is `cfg(unix)`-gated — a check that drives the `escher-session mcp` stdio child (`mcp_server`, `mcp_log`) does it through the shared `Speaker` (piped stdin, stdout read line by line on a thread under a 30 s bound, kill-and-reap in its `Drop`) and is not unix-gated but `mcp_server`'s two command-line comparisons; since 2026-10-19-session-recording a check that records is `cfg(unix)`-gated item by item, in-process and `mcp` stdio ones included (`mcp_log`'s recorded test), beside an off-unix check that a recording is refused `Unsupported`, which the windows job alone runs; a host ends by itself after its idle expiry, so a check that waits for one watches the state directory — an `attach` or a `status` is an answered request and starts the count again. The seven_guis checks also run the `escher-session` binary once per command as a client and read its stdout, stderr and exit status (`0` · `1` · `2` · `3`) through `tests/common/mod.rs`, which since 2026-10-19-test-splits also states the log checks' fragment once — `Needles` and `stand_needles` (the CRUD stand's id and name needles), `stamped_lines`, `found`, `occurrences`, the unix-only `recorded_needles` and `cells_needles(part)` (part `part`'s author keys of the in-process Cells screen and the middle column-A cell it holds) — called by `host_log` and `mcp_log` alone, and `option_needles()` (the needle list of a select's options read from a snapshot), called by the same two; the two flows under `tests/flows/` are POSIX `sh` scripts run by the Rust target `cli_flow` and, since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay, a third, `record_checks.sh`, by seven_guis `recording`'s unix-gated `the_committed_checks_are_what_the_binary_records` — assets of a `cargo test` target, not a runner of their own.
- **Headless E2E:** `blitz_test_harness::Harness` over `HtmlDocument` / `DioxusDocument`; WPT via `cargo run -rp wpt css svg` (needs `WPT_DIR`).
- **CI scripts:** `python3 -m unittest discover -s .github/scripts` (the `ci-scripts` leg; PyYAML for the workflow tests), one `TestCase` per function.

- No mocking library, property-test or snapshot crate is used (blitz-tests carries the assertion crate test-that 0.6.0 with test-that-macro 0.6.0 as dev-dependencies, 0.5.2 until 2026-10-17-upstream-sync-engine-debts, whose `verify_that!` and `TestResult<()>` upstream's merged `accessibility_label` and `accessibility_description` checks assert through under the same `#[test]` harness) — stand-ins are hand-written fakes (`RecordingNetProvider` and `ManualNetProvider`, upstream's; escher's one held network stand-in `fixtures::HeldNet`; since 2026-10-20-load-wait `stand_load_wait`'s in-file self-answering `LateNet`, whose `fetch` answers each request from its own thread after a 200 ms sleep; the stand's own `LoadNet`, private to `examples/seven_guis/src/stand.rs`, which `stand::boot_load` puts in its options' `net_provider` and which answers the fixed `http://stand.test/load.css` from a thread of its own after `LOAD_ANSWER_DELAY` (200 ms), `is_noop` not overridden; `RecordingShell`, `select_popup`'s own `CountingShell`, blitz-shell's test-local `CountedWakes`, `NoopEventHandler`, probe widgets). A check decodes a PNG through blitz-tests' `png` dev-dependency, or, in seven_guis, which has none, by a hand base64 reader and the PNG header.

- Each integration file opens with a `//!` doc naming the behaviour and any guarded bug; regression tests cite the upstream issue/PR URL and the real page that exposed it. `docs/capabilities.md` ends on `## Where each claim is proven`, naming the check behind each claim it makes — the stand checks among them — and only its names and counts are pinned, so a check renamed or moved changes that section by hand.
- Descriptive snake_case test names; `#[track_caller]` on assertion helpers.
- Assert first that the fixture produces the condition under test, then the behaviour.
- Build documents with `HtmlDocument::from_html` + a `DocumentConfig` carrying a fixed viewport (800×600 or 400×300, scale 1.0, `ColorScheme::Light`) and `HtmlProvider`, then `resolve(0.0)`.
- Run pipeline scenarios in both layout modes: `for incremental in [false, true]` (upstream's `pseudo_element_flow_classification` among them, `incremental_oracle` the layout-identity witness).
- Drive pure-restyle paths through `:hover`, not attribute mutation — a mutation inserts full damage and masks under-damaging bugs.
- Randomized stress uses a seeded LCG, never an unseeded RNG.

- The pre-existing font-dependent tests skip with `eprintln!` when no usable font exists (`system-fonts` is on when testing the workspace); this skip is a known gap, not a pattern to copy. Stand checks boot through `seven_guis::stand::boot(task, stand::options(incremental))` — the served pages through `stand::boot_cells` and `stand::boot_load` — pinned 800×600 · scale 1 · Light, the bundled DejaVu Sans with system fonts off, offline but for the load page, whose `net_provider` is the stand's `LoadNet`, every other field kept — and assert unconditionally: no font skip, no sleep (drive the timer through its `TimerTicks` handle; two recorded exceptions whose subject is wall time: `stand_virtual_clock`'s 800 ms sleep, taken so a shot after a scroll is read to repeat across wall time until `advance` moves the fade, and, since 2026-10-20-load-wait, `stand_load_wait`, which reads `Instant::now()` around its call to measure the load wait against `LOAD_WAIT` and whose in-file `LateNet` answers from its own thread after a 200 ms sleep; the 200 ms sleep of the stand's own `LoadNet` is the stand's, not a check's, `stand_load_page` waiting it out through the driver's load wait with no sleep or clock read of its own), no `dispatch_recorded`.

- A harness check that needs a font or a layout mode sets `HarnessOptions.font_ctx` / `.incremental`. A harness-built document reads the harness's `VirtualClock`: move its time with `tick(dt)` or `advance_time(Duration)` (`screenshot`, `screenshot_rect`, `text_contrast` and `settle` never move it), while `wrap(doc)` gives the harness a fresh clock and the wrapped document keeps the one its own config gave it (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18).

- Inline HTML string constants or `format!`-built pages; a fixture page more than one check reads is stated once as an `rsx!` component in `tests/fixtures/mod.rs` (`password_labelled`, `password_named`, `covered`, `many_items` — `ITEMS`, 400 buttons whose screen passes `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET`) and booted through `fixtures::boot`, while a page with one reader, or whose ids differ, stays in its check's file; image loads injected as `ImageData` with `Status::Ok`; blitz-vibey-script's two `file:`-load tests write their sibling files at test time under `std::env::temp_dir()` (`temp_dir_with_files`), test data on disk beside the in-code seeds; test URLs use the `.test` TLD or `example.com`, while blitz-net's `delivers_network_and_bad_url_errors` and `http_error_body_is_not_delivered_as_css` each bind a `std::net::TcpListener` on `127.0.0.1:0`, test-only TCP on loopback, served by no binary and reached by no caller, beside the module's test-local `Handler`.
- Blitz-dom unit tests build DOM by hand through `DocumentMutator` — blitz-html would be a circular dev-dependency.

- Two recorded Counter sessions are committed as test data under `tests/blitz-tests/checks/` (`counter-cli.json`, `counter-mcp.json`, no target): `stand_replay` replays them through `Check::replay`, and seven_guis `recording` compares them byte for byte with what `record_checks.sh` records through the binary — re-record them with that script, never edit them by hand, and keep the scripts free of a `screenshot` step (a shot's PNG bytes differ by OS).
- **One file:** `cargo test -p blitz-tests --test {name}`
- **One crate:** `cargo test -p {crate}`

- **Agent-driven (stand checks · blitz-tests):** `bash scripts/agent-run.sh boot`, then `run stand` · `run all` · `run {name}` — JSON-line results, exit `0`/`1`/`2`/`3` (test-plan §3; `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md`)

- **Cold-agent pipe (one live model session — operator host only, never in CI):** `bash scripts/cold-agent.sh run stand` (after `cargo build --locked -p seven_guis --bin escher-session` — the pipe builds nothing; `run counter` a usage error) → `target/cold-agent/verdict.json`; its contract tests run in the `ci-scripts` leg under a `claude` shim and a fake `target/debug/escher-session` (`.github/scripts/test_cold_agent.py`)
- **Whole workspace (CI leg):** `cargo test --workspace --locked` — or `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh test`, exactly as CI runs it

- **Before a push:** `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh fast` (fmt → clippy → test → CI scripts → embolden, stopping at the first red); a paint change under the OS-gated `blitz-paint/font-embolden` has its local witness in `embolden`, `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --no-fail-fast --features blitz-paint/font-embolden --test select_popup_painted`, a leg with no CI job of its own, macOS exercising the feature there
- **Benchmarks (ignored):** `cargo test -p blitz-tests --release --test paint_tree_bench -- --ignored --nocapture`

- A performance budget (§10) is not set. Path-scoped rules for the agent-driven verification harness. Source: `.andromeda/test-plan.md` §3.
Development Style is agent-driven — escher's own driver is meant to become the harness.

- Run from the repository root: `bash scripts/agent-run.sh boot`, then `run stand` · `run all` · `run {blitz-tests file}`, `status`, `logs`, `cleanup`. `scripts/agent-run.ps1` only forwards to it (Windows; untested here — no `pwsh`). The scripts are project-authored: setup preserves them, never re-renders them.

- Exit grammar, every verb: `0` success · `1` the verb ran and failed — a build failure, a failing run, or an EMPTY run (cargo 0 with no test line parsed is never a pass) · `2` usage, checked before · `3` a precondition is unmet (not booted; `logs` with nothing to read).

- `{name}` must match `^[a-z0-9_]+$` and name an existing `tests/blitz-tests/tests/{name}.rs`; `run stand` with no `stand_*.rs` files is an empty run (exit 1, no cargo call); under `all`, `run.start.files` is `[]`.

- Stdout is JSON lines only — `boot`, `run.start`, one `test {file, test, outcome}` per libtest line, `run.end {passed, failed, ignored, cargo_exit, outcome}`, `status`, `cleanup` — encoded by python3's `json`, never by bash string building. No event carries captured test output or a panic message, and no field takes a scrub-set name (`url href src html text value attrs path request error`); raw cargo output stays in `target/agent-run/run.log`.

- State lives in `target/agent-run/{status.json, events.jsonl, run.log}` only — the script itself starts no daemon and has no PID file, socket, port or env var (adding one is an arch §Occupied Resources registration); the stand checks boot in process, bar `stand_session_lifecycle` and `stand_session_quiet`, which start and stop their own session host and its Unix-domain socket under `target/tmp/`. One driver at a time: a killed run leaves `running`, the next `run` overwrites it.

- libtest's `--format json` is nightly-only, so the parser reads the pretty lines (`Running …`, `Doc-tests …`, `test … ... ok|FAILED|ignored`); the contract tests are `.github/scripts/test_agent_run.py` (a `cargo` shim, run by the `ci-scripts` leg).

- Test-data bootstrap: nothing is seeded — the fixtures are code (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/fixtures/mod.rs` and the one-reader pages in their checks' own files), compiled into each target by `boot` (`cargo test --no-run`), so `boot` is the bootstrap; `run stand` runs the 23 `stand_*` readers of the shared module, `run font_face_sniffed_source`, `run select_interaction`, `run select_popup`, `run select_popup_painted`, `run inert_subtree`, `run accessibility_states`, `run checkable_change_event` and `run text_range_no_change_event` its eight non-stand readers, and there is no `run fixtures` selection.

- Run from the repository root: `bash scripts/cold-agent.sh run stand` (`run counter` a usage error), then `status` · `logs` · `cleanup`; `scripts/cold-agent.ps1` only forwards. Same exit grammar as agent-run (`0` · `1` a `failed` verdict · `2` usage, checked first · `3` precondition — `claude`/`python3` absent, `target/debug/escher-session` absent or not executable (the pipe builds nothing: `cargo build --locked -p seven_guis --bin escher-session` first), no verdict, no events).

- `run` starts ONE live model session (`claude -p`, the operator's own login; ratified by the founder, 2026-10-06) from a per-run `mktemp -d` dir whose path names nothing, holding only an `mcp.json` naming one stdio server `escher`, the driver's own `escher-session mcp --record` into the owner-only `target/cold-agent/record/` (`mkdir -m 700`) (the twelve verbs; its stderr at `RUST_LOG=info` in `server.log`, counted by `tool_call` span lines, their `refused` / `error` endings and the accepted lines of each counted verb, `lint` · `screenshot` · `advance`, never printed or copied), with a fixed prompt asking for six apps one at a time — counter, flight booker (its return booking chosen on its flight type control, plus one screenshot), timer, CRUD, cells (plus one visual lint) and the load page — and a JSON check as the reply's last fenced json block (`--model claude-opus-5-5 --max-budget-usd 3`) — never fire it in CI or in a loop; the contract tests (`.github/scripts/test_cold_agent.py`) use a `claude` shim and a fake `target/debug/escher-session`.

- The verdict (`target/cold-agent/verdict.json`) reads `passed` only on positive evidence — client exit 0, a successful `result`, `isolated` (exactly the twelve `mcp__escher__*` tools, one server `escher`), `counts_agree` (the server's `tool_call` span lines against the transcript's escher tool uses, its refused + error lines against the results marked `is_error`), ≥ 1 tool call, all six apps in `tasks_met` (read from an accepted `snapshot` answer while the app is the latest accepted `start`'s, a paged screen read as the latest answer of each of its parts joined, never the agent's reply), each of `lint_calls` · `screenshot_calls` · `advance_calls` · `part_reads` above 0, `recording_kept` (each accepted `start` left one kept check), `wrong_calls × 100 ≤ 5 × tool_calls`, and the agent's check — at most 400 steps, never replayed when malformed — replayed green on a fresh `escher-session mcp` child (`check_passed`) and failing with its acting steps left out (`check_can_fail`); `wrong_calls` decides the outcome against `wrong_call_bar_pct` (5 %), a run over it failing `wrong-calls-over-bar`, beside the reasons `capability-unused` and `recording-not-kept`. Events carry counts and identities only — no transcript text, tool argument, tool result, reply or check text.

- State lives in `target/cold-agent/{verdict.json, events.jsonl, transcript.jsonl, client.log, server.log, check.json, record/}` only (`record/`, `mkdir -m 700`, the live server child's kept checks, never printed, copied or committed) (`cleanup` touches nothing else; `server.log` counted by span name and `check.json` written as parsed, neither ever printed or copied); `transcript.jsonl` is raw (host paths included) — a copy committed as evidence is host-path-masked first (`gate.py hygiene` refuses an unmasked one).
- Constructors `from_html`, `from_html_with(html, HarnessOptions)`, `from_component`, `from_vdom` pump once; `wrap` does not.

- `pump` polls with no waker and resolves at harness time — a `VirtualClock` its documents read, advanced by `tick(dt)` (a negative or non-finite `dt` moving nothing) and by exactly the duration by `advance_time(Duration)`, each then pumping, and never moved by `screenshot`, `screenshot_rect`, `text_contrast` or `settle` (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); `dispatch` / `dispatch_recorded` do NOT pump. Input helpers (`click`, `type_text`, `press`, `tap`, `wheel_at`, `drag`, `apple_keybinding`, `scroll_into_view`, `ime`, …) pump after dispatch; the crate re-exports keyboard-types 0.8's `Key`, `Modifiers` and, since 2026-10-17-upstream-sync-engine-debts, `NamedKey` — the two types `press_with` takes and the named-key enum a 0.8 `Key::Named` holds.
